T3-0001.ex: 직장이 집에서 멀어서 매일 일찍 나가요.
T3-0001.x: My workplace is far from home, so I leave early every day.
T3-0001.t: 직장 means your workplace or job in general; 회사 is specifically a company.

T3-0002.ex: 직장인들은 보통 아침 아홉 시까지 출근해요.
T3-0002.x: Office workers usually get to work by 9 a.m.

T3-0003.ex: 우리 회사는 올해 신입 사원을 열 명 뽑았어요.
T3-0003.x: Our company hired ten new employees this year.
T3-0003.e: Literally 'company member'. A homonym 사원 (different hanja) means 'temple'.

T3-0004.x: I gave the meeting materials to the department head earlier.
T3-0004.t: Add 님 when talking to or about your boss: 부장님, 과장님, 팀장님.

T3-0005.x: Sorry, but the manager is in a meeting right now.
T3-0005.e: Literally 'section head'. A homonym 과장 (different hanja) means 'exaggeration'.

T3-0006.ex: 김 대리님이 이번 프로젝트를 맡고 있어요.
T3-0006.x: Assistant Manager Kim is in charge of this project.
T3-0006.e: Literally 'manage on behalf of' — originally a deputy role.
T3-0006.t: 대리운전 is a popular service where a driver takes you and your car home after drinking.

T3-0007.ex: 팀장님이 오늘 저녁에 회식을 하자고 하셨어요.
T3-0007.x: The team leader suggested we have a team dinner tonight.

T3-0008.x: I asked my boss for time off next week.
T3-0008.t: A homonym 상사 (different hanja) means 'trading company', as in 종합 상사.

T3-0009.x: The head of that company is a young woman.
T3-0009.e: Literally 'stand in and show' — someone who stands for a group.
T3-0009.t: In companies, 대표님 usually means the CEO or owner.

T3-0010.x: I have a lot of work today, so I'm leaving late.
T3-0010.t: Pronounced [엄무] — nasalization; 업무 sounds formal, while everyday speech just uses 일.

T3-0011.ex: 우리 회사 근무 시간은 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지예요.
T3-0011.x: Our company's working hours are from nine to six.

T3-0012.x: I'm going on a business trip to Busan next week.
T3-0012.e: 출 means 'go out' — work done away from the office.
T3-0012.t: Say 출장을 가다 'go on a business trip'; 출장 중 means 'away on business'.

T3-0013.x: We have a team dinner this evening.
T3-0013.t: 회식 is a big part of Korean office culture and often involves drinking.

T3-0014.x: The new company pays a higher annual salary.
T3-0014.t: 월급 is monthly pay; 연봉 is the yearly figure used in job offers and negotiations.

T3-0015.x: My store's income has gone down lately, so I'm worried.
T3-0015.e: Literally 'taking in'. A homonym 수입 (different hanja) means 'import'.

T3-0016.x: I spent way too much this month.
T3-0016.t: 수입 and 지출 are a common pair: income vs. spending.

T3-0017.x: My older brother got a job right after graduating from college.
T3-0017.t: 취업 준비 means job hunting; 취업 and 취직 are near-synonyms.

T3-0018.x: I wrote my résumé to apply to that company.
T3-0018.e: Literally 'will and wish'. A different 지원하다 (different hanja) means 'to support'.
T3-0018.t: Use place + 에 지원하다: 회사에 지원하다 'apply to a company'.

T3-0019.x: I wrote my education and work experience on my résumé in detail.
T3-0019.t: Korean résumés often include a photo, birth date and other personal details.

T3-0020.x: Writing a personal statement is really hard.
T3-0020.t: Often shortened to 자소서 in casual speech.

T3-0021.ex: 이 일은 경력이 삼 년 이상 필요해요.
T3-0021.x: This job requires at least three years of experience.
T3-0021.t: Pronounced [경녁] — ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-0022.x: The new employees came to work for the first time today.
T3-0022.t: Common combos: 신입 사원 'new employee', 신입생 'freshman'.

T3-0023.ex: 이 회사는 올해 직원 채용을 늘렸어요.
T3-0023.x: This company increased its hiring this year.

T3-0024.x: I saw a help-wanted ad for part-timers at a convenience store.
T3-0024.t: Common on signs: 직원 모집 means 'Now hiring'.

T3-0025.x: My older brother was promoted to manager this year.
T3-0025.t: Use (position)으로 승진하다: 과장으로 승진하다 'be promoted to manager'.

T3-0026.x: My father retired from his company last year.
T3-0026.e: Literally 'withdraw and hide' — stepping back from working life.
T3-0026.t: 은퇴 is used for careers and athletes; 퇴직 focuses on leaving a company job.

T3-0027.x: As the economy worsens, the number of unemployed people is rising.

T3-0028.x: I signed the contract for a new house yesterday.
T3-0028.t: Common patterns: 계약을 하다 'make a contract', 계약이 끝나다 'a contract ends'.

T3-0029.x: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.

T3-0030.x: I reported the results of today's meeting to the department head.
T3-0030.t: When reporting to a superior, 보고드리다 sounds extra polite.

T3-0031.x: At work, I'm the one in charge of this work.

T3-0032.x: Please ask the person in charge directly for details.
T3-0032.e: -자 = person who does it: 담당자, 과학자, 기술자.
T3-0032.t: Handy phrase on the phone: 담당자 좀 바꿔 주세요 'May I speak to the person in charge?'

T3-0033.m: to take charge of, to be responsible for; to keep (for someone)
T3-0033.x: I took charge of this new project.
T3-0033.e: Homonym warning: another 맡다 means 'to smell', as in 냄새를 맡다.
T3-0033.t: 자리 좀 맡아 주세요 means 'Please save me a seat.'

T3-0034.m: to handle, to deal with, to process
T3-0034.x: Please take care of this issue by today.

T3-0035.ex: 우리 같이 이 문제를 해결해 봐요.
T3-0035.x: Let's try to solve this problem together.
T3-0035.t: Usually paired with 문제: 문제를 해결하다 'solve a problem'.

T3-0036.ex: 이 문제는 생각보다 해결이 쉽지 않아요.
T3-0036.x: This problem isn't as easy to solve as I thought.

T3-0037.x: I work in my company's marketing department.
T3-0037.t: To ask someone's department, say 어느 부서에서 일하세요?

T3-0038.x: I'm in charge of sales at my company.
T3-0038.t: On shop signs, 영업 중 means 'Open'; 영업 시간 means business hours.

T3-0039.x: We're promoting the new product online.
T3-0039.e: Literally 'broad report' — spreading the word widely.
T3-0039.t: 홍보 is broader than 광고, which means a specific ad.

T3-0041.ex: 보고서 마감이 내일이라서 오늘 밤에 써야 해요.
T3-0041.x: The report is due tomorrow, so I have to write it tonight.
T3-0041.t: It also means closing time: 오늘 영업 마감 means 'closed for today'.

T3-0042.x: The deadline for submitting the assignment has already passed.
T3-0042.t: 유통기한 on food packages means 'expiration date'.

T3-0043.x: I worked hard and got good results.

T3-0044.x: That person is excellent at their work.
T3-0044.t: Pronounced [능녁] — ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-0045.ex: 이 일을 하려면 어떤 자격이 필요해요?
T3-0045.x: What qualifications do you need to do this job?

T3-0046.x: I'm studying to get a computer certificate.
T3-0046.e: -증 = certificate or ID card: 자격증, 학생증, 면허증.
T3-0046.t: Use 따다 with certificates: 자격증을 따다 'earn a certificate'.

T3-0047.ex: 건강 문제는 전문가와 상담하는 게 좋아요.
T3-0047.x: For health problems, it's best to consult an expert.
T3-0047.e: -가 = professional or expert: 전문가, 작가, 화가.

T3-0048.x: This restaurant specializes in Korean food.
T3-0048.t: X 전문 means 'specializing in X' and is common on shop signs.

T3-0050.x: A technician came and fixed the air conditioner.

T3-0051.x: I exchanged business cards with someone I met for the first time.
T3-0051.t: Give and receive business cards with both hands as a sign of respect.

T3-0052.ex: 복사기가 고장 나서 복사를 못 했어요.
T3-0052.x: The copier broke, so I couldn't make copies.

T3-0053.x: There's no paper at all in the office printer.
T3-0053.t: To print something, Koreans say 프린트하다 or the more formal 출력하다.

T3-0054.ex: 사장님 비서에게 전화로 회의 시간을 물어봤어요.
T3-0054.x: I called the president's secretary to ask about the meeting time.
T3-0054.e: Literally 'secret documents' — someone trusted with private papers.

T3-0055.ex: 우리 언니는 서울에서 변호사로 일하고 있어요.
T3-0055.x: My older sister works as a lawyer in Seoul.

T3-0056.ex: 그 작가의 새 소설이 아주 인기가 많아요.
T3-0056.x: That writer's new novel is very popular.

T3-0057.ex: 그 화가의 그림은 색깔이 정말 예뻐요.
T3-0057.x: That painter's pictures have really beautiful colors.
T3-0057.t: Don't confuse it with 화가 나다 'to get angry', where 화 means anger.

T3-0058.x: My older brother works as a researcher at a company lab.
T3-0058.e: Literally 'research member'. A homonym (different hanja) means 'research institute'.

T3-0059.ex: 어릴 때 제 꿈은 과학자가 되는 거였어요.
T3-0059.x: When I was little, my dream was to become a scientist.
T3-0059.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 기술자, 담당자.

T3-0060.x: My friend is a designer who makes clothes.

T3-0061.x: The firefighters came and quickly put out the fire.
T3-0061.e: Literally 'official who puts out and prevents (fires)'.

T3-0062.x: I asked the driver for directions as I got on the bus.
T3-0062.t: Taxi and bus drivers are politely addressed as 기사님.

T3-0063.x: My grandfather worked as a farmer in the countryside.

T3-0064.x: My mother is a homemaker who runs the household.

T3-0065.ex: 그 아나운서는 뉴스를 아주 정확하게 읽어요.
T3-0065.x: That announcer reads the news very accurately.
T3-0065.e: From English 'announcer'; in Korean it usually means a broadcaster or news anchor.

T3-0066.x: The interpreter translated Korean into English at the meeting.
T3-0066.t: 통역 is spoken interpreting; 번역 is written translation.

T3-0067.ex: 그 모델은 키가 정말 크고 멋있어요.
T3-0067.x: That model is really tall and stylish.

T3-0068.ex: 그 영화 감독은 상을 많이 받았어요.
T3-0068.x: That film director has won many awards.
T3-0068.t: In sports, 감독 is the head coach or manager; 코치 is an assistant coach.

T3-0069.x: The coach teaches us soccer every day.

T3-0070.x: What field do you want to work in someday?

T3-0071.ex: 요즘 많은 기업들이 새 직원을 뽑고 있어요.
T3-0071.x: Many companies are hiring new staff these days.
T3-0071.t: 기업 sounds more formal than 회사 and is common in news and economics.

T3-0072.ex: 많은 대학생들이 대기업에 취업하고 싶어 해요.
T3-0072.x: Many college students want to get jobs at big companies.

T3-0073.x: They make cars at this factory every day.

T3-0074.x: Rice production rose sharply this year.
T3-0074.e: Literally 'bring to life and give birth'.

T3-0075.ex: 이 공장은 하루에 자동차를 천 대 생산해요.
T3-0075.x: This factory produces a thousand cars a day.
T3-0075.e: Literally 'bring to life and give birth'.

T3-0076.x: This product was made in a Korean factory.
T3-0076.t: 제품 stresses something manufactured; 상품 stresses goods for sale.

T3-0077.x: This store sells a wide variety of goods.
T3-0077.e: Literally 'trade goods'. A homonym 상품 (different hanja) means 'prize'.

T3-0078.x: Korea exports a lot of cars every year.
T3-0078.t: The opposite is 수입 'import' — a different 수입 from 'income'.

T3-0079.x: Our company imports wine from France.
T3-0079.t: Don't mix it up with the homonym 수입 meaning 'income' — context tells you which one is meant.

T3-0080.ex: 고객의 의견을 잘 듣는 것이 중요해요.
T3-0080.x: It's important to listen carefully to customers' opinions.
T3-0080.t: Staff address customers as 고객님 — very polite, common in phone calls and announcements.

T3-0081.ex: 우리는 그 회사와 10년 동안 거래를 했어요.
T3-0081.x: We did business with that company for ten years.
T3-0081.e: Literally 'going and coming' — goods and money moving back and forth.
T3-0081.t: 거래처 means a business client or partner company.

T3-0082.ex: 이번 일로 회사가 큰 손해를 봤어요.
T3-0082.x: The company took a big loss because of this.
T3-0082.t: The key collocation is 손해를 보다, 'to take a loss' — not 손해를 하다.

T3-0083.x: This year we made a lot more profit than last year.

T3-0084.ex: 이 분야는 회사들 사이의 경쟁이 아주 심해요.
T3-0084.x: Competition between companies in this field is really fierce.
T3-0084.t: Common pattern: 경쟁이 심하다, 'competition is fierce.'

T3-0085.x: My father runs a small restaurant business.
T3-0085.t: 사업을 하다 means 'to run your own business,' not just to work at a company.

T3-0086.ex: 그는 젊은 나이에 성공한 사업가가 되었어요.
T3-0086.x: He became a successful businessman at a young age.
T3-0086.e: -가 = person skilled in a field: 사업가, 작가, 전문가.

T3-0087.ex: 요즘 주식 투자를 하는 젊은 사람이 많아요.
T3-0087.x: These days a lot of young people invest in stocks.

T3-0088.x: I opened a new account at the bank.
T3-0088.e: Literally 'counting place' — where your money is tallied.
T3-0088.t: 계좌 is the account itself; 통장 is the bankbook, but people often use them interchangeably.

T3-0089.x: I checked how much money was left in my account.
T3-0089.e: A little ledger book that records money passing in and out.

T3-0090.ex: 저는 매달 10만 원씩 적금을 넣고 있어요.
T3-0090.x: I'm putting 100,000 won into a savings plan every month.
T3-0090.e: Literally 'piled-up money' — you add to it every month.
T3-0090.t: Koreans say 적금을 붓다 or 적금을 넣다 for making the monthly deposits.

T3-0091.ex: 미래를 위해 매달 조금씩 저축을 해요.
T3-0091.x: I save a little every month for the future.

T3-0092.ex: 여행을 가려고 돈을 열심히 저축하고 있어요.
T3-0092.x: I'm working hard to save money for a trip.
T3-0092.t: Pronounced [저추카다] — ㄱ + ㅎ become an aspirated ㅋ.

T3-0093.m: deposit (of money), payment into an account
T3-0093.ex: 입금이 확인되면 바로 물건을 보내 드릴게요.
T3-0093.x: As soon as the payment is confirmed, we'll send the item.
T3-0093.e: Literally 'money entering'; the opposite is 출금, 'money leaving.'
T3-0093.t: Pronounced [입끔] — the ㄱ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T3-0094.x: Sending money overseas comes with pretty high fees.

T3-0095.ex: 여행 가기 전에 오늘 환율을 확인했어요.
T3-0095.x: I checked today's exchange rate before my trip.
T3-0095.t: After a vowel or ㄴ, 률 is written 율: 환율, 비율, but 확률.

T3-0096.x: Bank interest rates are really low these days.
T3-0096.e: Literally 'benefit's offspring' — money born from money.

T3-0097.x: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
T3-0097.t: It also means checking out library books: 도서 대출.

T3-0098.x: Please stamp your seal on this document.
T3-0098.e: A carved name seal, traditionally used in Korea instead of a signature.
T3-0098.t: Homonym: 도장 also means a martial-arts gym, as in 태권도 도장.

T3-0099.ex: 이 서류 맨 아래에 서명을 해 주세요.
T3-0099.x: Please sign at the very bottom of this document.
T3-0099.t: In everyday speech people usually say 사인 instead: 여기 사인해 주세요.

T3-0100.ex: 다른 은행 기계에서 돈을 찾으면 수수료를 내야 해요.
T3-0100.x: If you withdraw money from another bank's machine, you have to pay a fee.
T3-0100.e: Literally 'handling fee' — a charge for the work done.

T3-0101.ex: 이 근처에 현금 인출기가 어디 있어요?
T3-0101.t: In daily conversation most Koreans simply say ATM (에이티엠).

T3-0102.x: When your number comes up, please go to window 3.
T3-0102.e: Literally 'window opening' — the counter where a clerk serves you.

T3-0103.x: When you enter the bank, take a number ticket first.
T3-0103.t: The verb is 뽑다, 'to pull out': 번호표를 뽑다.

T3-0104.x: You have to sign up for classes by Friday.

T3-0105.x: Fill out this application form and hand it in at the window.

T3-0106.m: to fill out, to write up, to draw up
T3-0106.x: Please write your name and address accurately.
T3-0106.e: Literally 'make complete' — finishing a written document.
T3-0106.t: More formal than 쓰다; used for forms, reports and official documents.

T3-0107.x: Getting a passport issued usually takes about a week.

T3-0108.m: to get (a document or card) issued, to receive
T3-0108.x: I got a new card issued at the bank.
T3-0108.t: The office 발급하다 (issues it); you 발급받다 (receive it).

T3-0109.x: I didn't have cash, so I paid by credit card.
T3-0109.t: Cashiers may ask 일시불로 해 드릴까요? — pay in full, as opposed to 할부, installments.

T3-0110.ex: 지갑에 천 원짜리 지폐가 두 장 있어요.
T3-0110.x: I have two 1,000-won bills in my wallet.
T3-0110.t: Bills are counted with 장: 만 원짜리 지폐 한 장.

T3-0111.x: Please check the amount and sign here.

T3-0112.ex: 월급에서 세금을 내고 나면 얼마 안 남아요.
T3-0112.x: After paying taxes out of my salary, there isn't much left.

T3-0113.ex: 어제 주문한 물건이 오늘 택배로 왔어요.
T3-0113.x: The thing I ordered yesterday came by delivery today.
T3-0113.t: 택배 is for packages; food delivery is 배달, as in 배달 음식.

T3-0114.ex: 제 우편물이 오면 경비실에 맡겨 주세요.
T3-0114.x: If any mail comes for me, please leave it at the security office.

T3-0115.ex: 감기 증상이 있으면 집에서 푹 쉬세요.
T3-0115.x: If you have cold symptoms, get plenty of rest at home.
T3-0115.t: Doctors often ask 어떤 증상이 있으세요? — 'What symptoms do you have?'

T3-0116.x: I was examined by the doctor.
T3-0116.t: The doctor 진찰하다; the patient 진찰을 받다.

T3-0117.x: The doctor examined the patient carefully.

T3-0118.ex: 의사가 준 처방전을 가지고 약국에 갔어요.
T3-0118.x: I went to the pharmacy with the prescription the doctor gave me.
T3-0118.t: In Korea you get a 처방전 at the clinic, then take it to a separate 약국.

T3-0119.x: I got a lot better after receiving treatment.

T3-0120.ex: 의사 선생님이 상처를 잘 치료해 주셨어요.
T3-0120.x: The doctor treated my wound well.
T3-0120.t: 고치다 can mean 'cure' casually, but 치료하다 is the standard medical word.

T3-0121.x: Grandma's discharge date has been set.
T3-0121.e: Literally 'leaving the institution'; the opposite is 입원, 'entering.'

T3-0122.m: to be discharged from (the) hospital, to leave the hospital
T3-0122.x: I left the hospital a week after my surgery.

T3-0123.x: The hospital room my friend is staying in is on the fifth floor.

T3-0124.ex: 밤에 배가 너무 아파서 응급실에 갔어요.
T3-0124.x: My stomach hurt so much at night that I went to the ER.
T3-0124.e: Literally 'room for responding to urgent cases.'
T3-0124.t: Pronounced [응급씰] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T3-0125.x: There was an accident on the street, so we called an ambulance.
T3-0125.t: In Korea, dial 119 for an ambulance or the fire department.

T3-0126.ex: 배가 계속 아프면 내과에 가 보세요.
T3-0126.x: If your stomach keeps hurting, try going to an internal medicine clinic.
T3-0126.e: -과 = medical department: 내과, 외과, 안과, 소아과.
T3-0126.t: Pronounced [내꽈] — 과 in department names is usually tensed.

T3-0127.x: I hurt my leg, so I got treated in the surgery department.
T3-0127.t: For sprains and bone or joint pain, Koreans usually go to 정형외과 (orthopedics).

T3-0128.x: My child had a fever, so I took them to the pediatrician.

T3-0129.x: My eyes were red and sore, so I went to the eye doctor.

T3-0130.x: My skin was so itchy that I went to the dermatologist.

T3-0131.x: When you arrive at the hospital, check in at the front desk first.
T3-0131.t: At Korean clinics, 접수 is the check-in step before you see the doctor.

T3-0132.ex: 우리 회사는 매년 건강 검진을 받아요.
T3-0132.x: Everyone at our company gets a health checkup every year.

T3-0133.ex: 할아버지는 혈압이 높아서 매일 약을 드세요.
T3-0133.x: My grandfather has high blood pressure, so he takes medicine every day.
T3-0133.t: Pronounced [혀랍] — the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

T3-0134.ex: 열이 나는 것 같아서 체온을 쟀어요.
T3-0134.x: I felt like I had a fever, so I took my temperature.

T3-0135.m: body aches (with fatigue or chills), general achiness
T3-0135.ex: 어제 너무 무리해서 오늘 몸살이 났어요.
T3-0135.x: I overdid it yesterday, so today I'm achy all over.
T3-0135.e: Built on 몸 'body': aching all over, usually from exhaustion or a coming cold.
T3-0135.t: Say 몸살이 나다 or 몸살에 걸리다; English has no single word for it.

T3-0136.ex: 상한 음식을 먹고 하루 종일 설사를 했어요.
T3-0136.x: I ate some spoiled food and had diarrhea all day.

T3-0137.ex: 밥을 너무 빨리 먹으면 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
T3-0137.x: If you eat too fast, you won't digest well.
T3-0137.e: Literally 'dissolve and transform' — food breaking down.
T3-0137.t: 소화가 안 돼요 is the everyday way to say 'I have indigestion.'

T3-0138.ex: 어제 술을 너무 많이 마셔서 토했어요.
T3-0138.x: I drank way too much yesterday and threw up.

T3-0139.x: I stood up suddenly, and now I feel dizzy.
T3-0139.e: Also means 'messy, cluttered': 방이 어지러워요, 'the room is a mess.'

T3-0140.x: The mosquito bite is really itchy.
T3-0140.t: 가렵다 is itchy; 간지럽다 is ticklish, though people also use it casually for itchy.

T3-0141.forms: 부어요 · 부었어요 · 부을 거예요 · 부은 (+noun) (ㅅ irregular)
T3-0141.ex: 어젯밤에 라면을 먹고 자서 얼굴이 부었어요.
T3-0141.x: I ate ramyeon before bed last night, so my face is puffy.
T3-0141.e: Homonym: 붓다 also means 'to pour,' as in 물을 붓다, conjugated the same way.
T3-0141.t: Swelling is a result, so use the past form for a current state: 발이 부었어요, 'my feet are swollen.'

T3-0142.x: I fell and got a bruise on my leg.
T3-0142.t: The verb is 들다: 멍이 들다, 'to get a bruise.'

T3-0143.ex: 저는 땅콩 알레르기가 있어서 조심해야 해요.
T3-0143.x: I'm allergic to peanuts, so I have to be careful.
T3-0143.e: From German 'Allergie,' not English 'allergy' — hence the 'reu-gi' ending.
T3-0143.t: To say you're allergic, use 알레르기가 있다: 고양이 알레르기가 있어요.

T3-0144.ex: 담배를 피우면 암에 걸릴 위험이 높아져요.
T3-0144.x: Smoking raises your risk of getting cancer.
T3-0144.t: Diseases take 걸리다: 암에 걸리다, 감기에 걸리다.

T3-0145.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 많은 질병을 예방할 수 있어요.
T3-0145.x: Washing your hands often can prevent many diseases.
T3-0145.t: 질병 is formal and written; in conversation people usually just say 병.

T3-0146.x: A cold is an illness caused by a virus.
T3-0146.e: From English 'virus'; also used for computer viruses.

T3-0147.ex: 감기 예방을 위해 손을 자주 씻으세요.
T3-0147.x: Wash your hands often to prevent colds.

T3-0148.ex: 물을 자주 마시면 감기를 예방하는 데 도움이 돼요.
T3-0148.x: Drinking water often helps prevent colds.

T3-0149.x: I cut my finger with a knife, so I put on a Band-Aid.
T3-0149.t: In everyday speech many Koreans just say 밴드.

T3-0150.ex: 이 약은 부작용이 거의 없어서 안전해요.
T3-0150.x: This medicine is safe because it has almost no side effects.
T3-0150.t: It's also used figuratively for any unwanted result of a policy or plan.

T3-0151.ex: 이 약을 먹었는데 효과가 별로 없어요.
T3-0151.x: I took this medicine, but it isn't really working.
T3-0151.t: Both [효과] and [효꽈] are accepted standard pronunciations.

T3-0152.ex: 수술 후 회복이 빨라서 정말 다행이에요.
T3-0152.x: It's a real relief that the recovery after surgery has been fast.

T3-0153.x: After getting plenty of rest, I recovered my health.
T3-0153.t: It works beyond health too: 신뢰를 회복하다, 'to regain trust.'

T3-0154.ex: 아플 때는 영양이 많은 음식을 먹어야 해요.
T3-0154.x: When you're sick, you should eat nutritious food.

T3-0155.forms: 살을 빼요 · 살을 뺐어요; 살이 빠지다 = to lose weight (it just happens)
T3-0155.ex: 여름이 오기 전에 살을 빼려고 매일 운동해요.
T3-0155.x: I'm working out every day to lose weight before summer.
T3-0155.e: 살 'flesh' plus 빼다 'to take out' — literally 'take the flesh off.'
T3-0155.t: Use 살을 빼다 for deliberate effort and 살이 빠지다 when weight drops on its own.

T3-0156.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 스트레스를 많이 받아요.
T3-0156.x: I've had a lot of work lately, so I'm really stressed.
T3-0156.e: From English 'stress' — one English syllable becomes four Korean ones.
T3-0156.t: You 받다 (receive) stress and 풀다 (untie) it: 노래방에서 스트레스를 풀어요.

T3-0157.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 피로가 많이 쌓였어요.
T3-0157.x: I've had a lot of work lately, so fatigue has really built up.

T3-0158.x: Smoking is not allowed inside this building.
T3-0158.t: 금연하다 means 'to quit smoking,' while 금연 on a sign means 'No Smoking.'

T3-0159.ex: 그는 다리에 장애가 있지만 매일 운동을 해요.
T3-0159.x: He has a disability in his legs, but he exercises every day.

T3-0160.m: person with a disability, disabled person
T3-0160.ex: 이 버스는 장애인도 편하게 탈 수 있어요.
T3-0160.x: People with disabilities can ride this bus comfortably too.
T3-0160.t: 장애인 is the standard respectful term; avoid older words like 장애자 or 불구자.

T3-0161.ex: 보험이 있어서 병원비가 많이 나오지 않았어요.
T3-0161.x: I had insurance, so the hospital bill wasn't very high.
T3-0161.t: To get insurance, say 보험에 들다 or 보험에 가입하다.

T3-0162.ex: 규칙적인 운동은 신체 건강에 도움이 돼요.
T3-0162.x: Regular exercise is good for your physical health.
T3-0162.e: Literally 'body-body'; a formal word for the human body.
T3-0162.t: 신체 is formal and written; in everyday conversation just say 몸.

T3-0163.x: I fell on the stairs and broke a bone in my arm.
T3-0163.e: Also found in 갈비뼈 'rib' and 뼈다귀 'a bone' (casual).

T3-0164.x: I worked out every day, so I built a lot of muscle.
T3-0164.t: Pronounced [그뉵] — the ㄴ slides over into the next syllable.

T3-0165.x: I was so nervous that my heart was racing.

T3-0166.ex: 매운 음식을 많이 먹어서 위가 아파요.
T3-0166.x: I ate a lot of spicy food, so my stomach hurts.
T3-0166.e: Homonym warning: native 위 also means 'top, above.'
T3-0166.t: In everyday talk, Koreans usually say 배가 아파요 rather than 위가 아파요.

T3-0167.x: If you drink a lot of alcohol, your liver gets damaged.
T3-0167.e: Homonym warning: 간 also means 'seasoning, saltiness,' as in 간을 보다 'to taste for seasoning.'
T3-0167.t: 간이 크다, literally 'to have a big liver,' means to be bold or daring.

T3-0168.ex: 열이 있는지 아이의 이마를 만져 봤어요.
T3-0168.x: I touched my child's forehead to see if they had a fever.

T3-0169.x: That actor has dark, thick eyebrows.
T3-0169.e: Starts with 눈 'eye': the hair above the eye. Eyelashes are 속눈썹, 'inner eyebrows.'

T3-0170.x: It was cold, so the child's cheeks turned red.
T3-0170.e: Homonym warning: 볼 is also a form of 보다 'to see,' as in 볼 거예요.
T3-0170.t: 볼 and 뺨 both mean cheek, but slapping uses 뺨: 뺨을 때리다.

T3-0171.x: My dad has a lot of stubble on his chin.
T3-0171.e: Homonym warning: 턱 also means a raised ledge, as in 문턱 'doorsill.'
T3-0171.t: 한턱내다 means to treat people to a meal, usually to celebrate good news.

T3-0172.ex: 치아 건강을 위해 하루에 세 번 이를 닦으세요.
T3-0172.x: Brush your teeth three times a day for healthy teeth.
T3-0172.e: Literally 'tooth-tooth'; a formal word for teeth.
T3-0172.t: 치아 is formal or medical; in daily speech say 이, as in 이를 닦다.

T3-0173.x: I sat for so long that my bottom hurts.

T3-0174.x: Rotate your ankles before you exercise.

T3-0175.x: My wrist hurts from using the computer for a long time.

T3-0176.x: I cut my nails short every weekend.
T3-0176.e: Starts with 손 'hand'; toenails are 발톱, with 발 'foot.'

T3-0177.x: My grandfather grew a long white beard.
T3-0177.e: Sino-Korean; both syllables mean facial hair and rarely appear in other words.
T3-0177.t: Use 기르다 to grow a beard and 깎다 or 면도하다 to shave it.

T3-0178.ex: 처음 만났을 때 그 사람은 인상이 좋았어요.
T3-0178.x: When I first met him, he gave a good impression.
T3-0178.e: Literally 'stamped image,' the picture a person leaves in your mind.
T3-0178.t: 인상을 쓰다 means 'to frown'; a different 인상 means a price increase.

T3-0179.ex: 우리 형은 체격이 크고 힘이 세요.
T3-0179.x: My older brother has a big build and is strong.

T3-0180.x: That model has a really slim figure.
T3-0180.e: 몸 'body' + -매 'shape,' the same suffix as in 눈매 'shape of the eyes.'

T3-0181.ex: 우리 아기는 볼이 통통해서 정말 귀여워요.
T3-0181.x: Our baby has chubby cheeks and is really cute.
T3-0181.e: Built on the mimetic word 통통, which suggests something round and full.
T3-0181.t: 통통하다 sounds cute or neutral, while 뚱뚱하다 can sound negative or rude.

T3-0182.ex: 그 배우는 목소리에 특별한 매력이 있어요.
T3-0182.x: That actor's voice has a special charm.

T3-0183.x: My younger sibling has had curly hair since birth.

T3-0184.ex: 할머니는 웃을 때 눈가에 주름이 생겨요.
T3-0184.x: Wrinkles form around my grandmother's eyes when she smiles.
T3-0184.e: Used for skin and for fabric: 주름치마 is a pleated skirt.

T3-0185.ex: 그 사람은 입 옆에 작은 점이 있어요.
T3-0185.x: That person has a small mole next to their mouth.
T3-0185.e: Homonym warning: 점 also means 'dot, point, score,' and a different 점 means fortune-telling.
T3-0185.t: 점을 빼다 means to have a mole removed, a common cosmetic procedure in Korea.

T3-0186.x: That child has a round, cute face.
T3-0186.e: Related to 동그랗다 'round'; the darker vowels give a bigger, fuller feel.
T3-0186.t: The ㄹ drops before ㄴ, so 'round face' is 둥근 얼굴, not 둥글은 얼굴.

T3-0187.x: My older sister puts on perfume every time she goes out.
T3-0187.t: Use 뿌리다 for putting on perfume; a different 향수 means homesickness or nostalgia.

T3-0188.x: I got my hair dyed at the salon over the weekend.

T3-0189.ex: 그 사람은 옷 스타일이 정말 멋있어요.
T3-0189.x: That person's clothing style is really cool.
T3-0189.t: 제 스타일이에요 can mean 'He's (or she's) my type,' not just 'my style.'

T3-0190.x: Short hair is in style these days.

T3-0191.m: to be in fashion, to be popular; to go around (of an illness)
T3-0191.x: Big bags are in fashion this year.
T3-0191.t: Also used for illnesses: 독감이 유행하고 있어요 means 'The flu is going around.'

T3-0192.x: My friend is really interested in fashion.
T3-0192.e: From English 'fashion'; also in 패션쇼 'fashion show.'

T3-0193.x: A neat outfit is important for a job interview.
T3-0193.e: 옷 'clothes' + 차림 'getup,' from 차리다 'to get ready.'
T3-0193.t: Pronounced [옫차림] — the final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ.

T3-0194.x: He came to school in his workout clothes.
T3-0194.e: Noun form of 차리다 'to get ready, to dress up.'

T3-0195.x: I got pretty earrings as a birthday present.
T3-0195.e: 귀 'ear' + 걸이 'something hung,' from 걸다 'to hang.'

T3-0196.x: A button came off my shirt.
T3-0196.t: 단추를 채우다 means 'to button up'; 단추를 풀다 means 'to unbutton.'

T3-0197.ex: 오늘 줄무늬 티셔츠를 입고 학교에 갔어요.
T3-0197.x: I wore a striped T-shirt to school today.
T3-0197.t: Pronounced [줄무니] — ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

T3-0198.ex: 그 학생은 항상 옷을 단정하게 입어요.

T3-0199.x: My family moved from an apartment to a house.

T3-0200.ex: 저는 학교 근처 원룸에서 혼자 살아요.
T3-0200.x: I live alone in a studio near school.
T3-0200.e: From English 'one room'; Konglish for a studio apartment.
T3-0200.t: Pronounced [월룸] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T3-0201.ex: 대학교 때 학교 앞에서 하숙을 했어요.
T3-0201.x: In college, I boarded in a house near campus.
T3-0201.e: A rented room where the owner also serves meals; popular with college students.
T3-0201.t: 하숙 includes meals; 자취 means renting alone and cooking for yourself.

T3-0202.m: jeonse (a lease paid with one large deposit instead of monthly rent)
T3-0202.x: We found a small apartment on a jeonse lease.
T3-0202.e: A Korean system: you pay a big deposit, live rent-free, and get it back when you leave.
T3-0202.t: A different 전세 means 'charter,' as in 전세 버스 'chartered bus.'

T3-0203.ex: 이사 나갈 때 보증금을 다 돌려받았어요.
T3-0203.x: I got my whole deposit back when I moved out.

T3-0204.ex: 이번 달 집세를 아직 못 냈어요.
T3-0204.x: I still haven't paid this month's rent.
T3-0204.t: Pronounced [집쎄] — the ㅅ becomes tense after ㅂ.

T3-0205.ex: 겨울에는 난방 때문에 관리비가 많이 나와요.
T3-0205.x: In winter, the maintenance fee is high because of heating.
T3-0205.t: Pronounced [괄리비] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-0206.ex: 부동산에 가서 집을 몇 군데 봤어요.
T3-0206.x: I went to a real estate agency and looked at a few places.

T3-0207.ex: 이삿짐을 다 옮기는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
T3-0207.x: It took a whole day to move all our stuff.
T3-0207.e: 이사 'moving' + 짐 'load, luggage,' joined by an extra ㅅ.
T3-0207.t: Pronounced [이사찜] or [이삳찜] — the added ㅅ makes 짐 tense.

T3-0208.x: The air conditioner installation is tomorrow afternoon.
T3-0208.e: Literally 'set up and put in place.'

T3-0209.x: I had internet installed in my new place.
T3-0209.e: Literally 'set up and put in place.'
T3-0209.t: For apps, 앱을 설치하다 is standard; 앱을 깔다 is the casual version.

T3-0210.x: The washing machine broke, so I sent it in for repair.

T3-0211.ex: 이웃집 아이들이 자주 우리 집에 놀러 와요.
T3-0211.x: The neighbor's kids often come over to play.

T3-0212.ex: 밤마다 위층 소음 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
T3-0212.x: I can't sleep every night because of the noise upstairs.
T3-0212.t: 층간 소음, noise between apartment floors, is a very common neighbor complaint in Korea.

T3-0213.ex: 요리한 후에는 창문을 열고 환기를 하세요.
T3-0213.x: After cooking, open the windows and air out the room.

T3-0214.x: In winter we turn on the heat, so the house is warm.
T3-0214.t: Korean homes have floor heating, so people often say 보일러를 켜다 for 'turn on the heat.'

T3-0215.ex: 외출하기 전에 가스 불을 꼭 끄세요.
T3-0215.x: Be sure to turn off the gas stove before going out.
T3-0215.e: From English 'gas'; it means fuel gas, never gasoline, which is 휘발유.
T3-0215.t: A gas stove is 가스레인지, from Konglish 'gas range.'

T3-0216.x: It was so cold that the water pipes froze.
T3-0216.t: A different 수도 means 'capital city': 한국의 수도는 서울이에요.

T3-0217.ex: 이 동네 수돗물은 그냥 마셔도 괜찮아요.
T3-0217.x: The tap water in this neighborhood is fine to drink as is.
T3-0217.e: 수도 'water supply' + 물 'water,' joined by an extra ㅅ.

T3-0218.m: to leak; to escape (of light, gas, or a secret)
T3-0218.x: It's raining, and water is leaking from the ceiling.
T3-0218.e: Homonym warning: 새다 also means 'to dawn,' as in 밤이 새다.
T3-0218.t: Don't confuse 새다 'to leak' with 세다 'to be strong, to count'; they sound almost the same.

T3-0219.ex: 이 방은 천장이 높아서 넓어 보여요.
T3-0219.x: This room has a high ceiling, so it looks spacious.
T3-0219.e: Literally 'sky barrier,' the thing that blocks the sky indoors.
T3-0219.t: The correct spelling is 천장, not 천정, a very common mistake.

T3-0220.x: It snowed all night, and the roof turned white.
T3-0220.e: Probably from 집 'house' plus an old suffix.

T3-0221.ex: 안 쓰는 물건은 창고에 넣어 두었어요.
T3-0221.x: I put the things I don't use in the storage room.

T3-0222.x: I was tired, so I filled the tub with warm water.

T3-0223.x: The toilet was clogged, so I called a repairman.

T3-0224.ex: 거실 조명을 더 밝은 것으로 바꿨어요.
T3-0224.x: I changed the living room lights to brighter ones.

T3-0225.x: When we moved, we bought all new appliances.

T3-0226.x: Our apartment complex sorts recycling every Wednesday.
T3-0226.e: Literally 'separate, then collect and take away.'
T3-0226.t: Pronounced [불리수거] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-0227.x: Plastic and paper can be recycled.
T3-0227.e: 재- = again, re-: 재활용, 재사용, 재시험.

T3-0228.ex: 다 마신 병은 깨끗이 씻어서 재활용하세요.
T3-0228.x: Rinse empty bottles clean and recycle them.

T3-0229.ex: 음식물 쓰레기는 전용 봉투에 버려야 해요.
T3-0229.x: Food waste has to be thrown out in special bags.
T3-0229.t: In Korea, food waste is kept separate from other trash, often in special paid bags.

T3-0230.x: We apologize for the inconvenience caused by the construction.
T3-0230.t: 불편을 드려서 죄송합니다 is the standard formal apology for an inconvenience.

T3-0231.ex: 이 집은 위치와 가격 조건이 모두 좋아요.
T3-0231.x: This place is good on both location and price.
T3-0231.e: Literally 'clause and item,' like terms listed in a contract.

T3-0232.ex: 이 아파트는 운동 시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
T3-0232.x: This apartment complex has good fitness facilities.

T3-0233.ex: 이 집은 구조가 좋아서 방이 넓어 보여요.
T3-0233.x: This place has a good layout, so the rooms look spacious.
T3-0233.t: A different 구조 means 'rescue,' as in 구조대 'rescue team.'

T3-0234.m: to be old, worn out, shabby (of things)
T3-0234.ex: 이 아파트는 오래돼서 시설이 많이 낡았어요.
T3-0234.x: This apartment is old, so the facilities are really worn out.
T3-0234.e: Used only for things; for people getting old, use 늙다.
T3-0234.t: Usually used in the past form to describe a state: 옷이 낡았어요 'The clothes are worn out.'

T3-0235.ex: 우리 집은 아주 오래돼서 겨울에 좀 추워요.
T3-0235.x: Our house is very old, so it's a bit cold in winter.
T3-0235.e: 오래 'for a long time' + 되다 'to become': something that has existed a long time.

T3-0236.ex: 이 아파트 주민들은 서로 잘 알아요.
T3-0236.x: The residents of this apartment building know each other well.
T3-0236.e: Literally 'living people': the people who live in a place.

T3-0237.m: community service center, local neighborhood office
T3-0237.ex: 주민 센터에서 무료 한국어 수업을 들어요.
T3-0237.x: I take a free Korean class at the community service center.
T3-0237.t: It used to be called 동사무소, and older people may still use that name.

T3-0238.x: After moving, I went to the district office and reported it.
T3-0238.e: Literally 'district office'; big cities like Seoul are divided into 구, such as 강남구.

T3-0239.ex: 우리 집 근처에 소방서가 있어서 사이렌 소리가 자주 들려요.
T3-0239.x: There's a fire station near my house, so I often hear sirens.
T3-0239.e: Literally 'office that puts out and prevents' fires.

T3-0240.x: I lost my passport, so I have to go to the embassy.
T3-0240.e: Literally 'great-envoy building': where the ambassador (대사) works.

T3-0241.ex: 한국에 90일 넘게 살면 외국인 등록증이 필요해요.
T3-0241.x: If you live in Korea for more than 90 days, you need a residence card.

T3-0242.x: I extended my student visa for one more year.
T3-0242.t: Common collocations: 비자를 연장하다, 기간을 연장하다, 계약을 연장하다 (extend a contract).

T3-0243.x: Please don't talk loudly on the phone in public places.

T3-0244.x: Many citizens gathered in the square on the weekend.
T3-0244.t: 시민 is a city's residents or citizens in a civic sense; 국민 is the people of a whole nation.

T3-0245.m: the people (of a nation), citizens, nationals
T3-0245.x: The president must work for the people.
T3-0245.t: Pronounced [궁민] — nasalization: ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ.

T3-0246.m: bulletin board; message board, online forum
T3-0246.x: The notices are posted on the bulletin board.
T3-0246.t: It also means an online message board, where you 글을 올리다 (post something).

T3-0247.x: Be sure to check the notices on the website.

T3-0248.ex: 지하철에서 잃어버린 가방을 분실물 센터에서 찾았어요.
T3-0248.x: I found the bag I lost on the subway at the lost-and-found center.
T3-0248.t: 분실물 센터 is the lost-and-found office, found in subway stations and airports.

T3-0249.x: If you lose your card, report it to the bank right away.
T3-0249.e: Literally 'let it scatter and lose it'.
T3-0249.t: More formal than 잃어버리다; you'll see it on official notices, forms and in banks.

T3-0250.x: I saw a thief and reported it to the police.
T3-0250.e: Literally 'state and report' to an official body.

T3-0251.m: to report (to the authorities), to declare
T3-0251.x: If there's a fire, call 119 right away.
T3-0251.t: Mark the authority with 에: 경찰에 신고하다 (report to the police).

T3-0252.ex: 주말에는 이 박물관에 방문객이 정말 많아요.
T3-0252.x: This museum has a lot of visitors on weekends.
T3-0252.e: Literally 'visiting guest'; -객 = guest or customer: 관광객, 승객.

T3-0253.x: The library is open for use until 6 p.m.
T3-0253.t: 이용 is for services and facilities like the subway or library; 사용 is for tools and objects.

T3-0254.ex: 회원 가입을 하면 할인을 받을 수 있어요.
T3-0254.x: If you sign up as a member, you can get a discount.
T3-0254.t: The verb takes 에: 동아리에 가입하다 (join a club), 보험에 가입하다 (get insurance).

T3-0255.x: Class registration is open until next Monday.
T3-0255.t: Pronounced [등녹] — ㄹ turns into ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-0256.ex: 대학교 등록금이 너무 비싸서 아르바이트를 해요.
T3-0256.x: College tuition is so expensive that I work a part-time job.
T3-0256.e: Literally 'registration money'; -금 = money or fee: 요금, 장학금.

T3-0257.x: Admission to the concert hall begins at 7 p.m.
T3-0257.t: A different 입장 means 'position, standpoint' (제 입장에서는 = from my point of view).

T3-0258.ex: 이 주차장은 유료라서 돈을 내야 해요.
T3-0258.x: This parking lot isn't free, so you have to pay.

T3-0259.m: to discount, to give a discount
T3-0259.x: This store gives students a 10% discount.
T3-0259.e: Literally 'cut and pull down' the price.

T3-0260.x: Please line up in order, in a single line.

T3-0261.ex: 병원 대기 시간이 한 시간이나 됐어요.
T3-0261.x: The wait at the hospital was a whole hour.
T3-0261.t: A different 대기 means 'the atmosphere, air', as in 대기 오염 (air pollution).

T3-0262.ex: 설날에 떡국을 먹는 것은 한국의 전통이에요.
T3-0262.x: Eating rice cake soup on Lunar New Year's Day is a Korean tradition.

T3-0263.x: Table manners differ a little from country to country.
T3-0263.t: A key table rule: wait until the oldest person starts eating before you pick up your spoon.

T3-0264.forms: 예의 발라요 · 예의 발랐어요 · 예의 바른 (+noun) (르 irregular)
T3-0264.ex: 그 학생은 항상 예의 바르게 인사해요.
T3-0264.x: That student always greets people politely.
T3-0264.e: 예의 'courtesy' + 바르다 'straight, proper': manners kept straight.
T3-0264.t: The opposite is 예의 없다 or 버릇없다 (rude, spoiled), often said about children.

T3-0265.x: That teacher is respected by the students.

T3-0266.m: to respect, to look up to, to admire
T3-0266.ex: 제가 가장 존경하는 사람은 우리 어머니예요.
T3-0266.x: The person I respect most is my mother.
T3-0266.t: 존경하다 means looking up to someone; 존중하다 means respecting anyone's rights, opinions or choices.

T3-0267.ex: 가족 사이에도 서로에 대한 존중이 중요해요.
T3-0267.x: Mutual respect is important even within a family.

T3-0268.x: On Lunar New Year's morning, I gave my grandmother a New Year's bow.
T3-0268.e: Literally 'year bow'; afterward children receive 세뱃돈, New Year's money.
T3-0268.t: You 세배를 드리다 to elders while saying 새해 복 많이 받으세요.

T3-0269.m: ancestral rite, memorial service for ancestors
T3-0269.x: My family holds an ancestral rite every major holiday.
T3-0269.e: Literally 'offering and worship': food is set out for ancestors' spirits.
T3-0269.t: The verb used is 지내다: 제사를 지내다 (to hold an ancestral rite).

T3-0270.ex: 전주에 가면 오래된 한옥을 구경할 수 있어요.
T3-0270.x: If you go to Jeonju, you can see old traditional Korean houses.
T3-0270.e: Literally 'Korean house'; 한- = Korean: 한복, 한식.

T3-0271.ex: 한국 사람들은 설날 아침에 떡국을 먹어요.
T3-0271.x: Koreans eat rice cake soup on Lunar New Year's morning.
T3-0271.e: 떡 'rice cake' + 국 'soup'; eating it on New Year's means you turn a year older.
T3-0271.t: 떡국 몇 그릇 먹었어요? ('How many bowls of 떡국 have you eaten?') is a playful way to ask someone's age.

T3-0272.x: I'm going down to my hometown over this long holiday.

T3-0273.x: Hangeul Day on October 9 is a public holiday in Korea.

T3-0274.e: Literally 'a day to record and remember'.

T3-0275.x: To mark my graduation, I took photos with my family.
T3-0275.t: 기념하다 marks an event; 축하하다 congratulates a person on it.

T3-0276.x: On Children's Day, people give children presents.
T3-0276.e: 어린이 'child' + 날 'day'; it's a public holiday on May 5.

T3-0277.x: On Parents' Day, I gave my parents red carnations.
T3-0277.e: 어버이 is a literary word for 'parents'; May 8 is not a day off.
T3-0277.t: Koreans give carnations on this day; Korea has no separate Mother's Day or Father's Day.

T3-0278.ex: 스승의 날에 선생님께 감사 편지를 썼어요.
T3-0278.x: On Teachers' Day, I wrote my teacher a thank-you letter.
T3-0278.e: 스승 is a respectful native word for 'teacher, mentor'.
T3-0278.t: The particle 의 here is usually pronounced [에]: [스승에 날].

T3-0279.ex: 한글날은 세종대왕이 만든 한글을 기념하는 날이에요.
T3-0279.x: Hangeul Day is a day to honor the Korean alphabet created by King Sejong.
T3-0279.e: 한글 'the Korean alphabet' + 날 'day'; it marks the alphabet's proclamation in 1446.
T3-0279.t: Pronounced [한글랄] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ after ㄹ.

T3-0280.x: I went to my nephew's first birthday party and gave a present.
T3-0280.e: 돌 'first birthday' + 잔치 'feast'; the baby picks an object (돌잡이) said to predict its future.

T3-0281.ex: 올해 아버지 환갑이라서 가족 여행을 가요.
T3-0281.x: It's my father's 60th birthday this year, so we're going on a family trip.
T3-0281.e: Literally 'returning to 갑': the 60-year cycle of the traditional calendar starts over.

T3-0282.x: I got a wedding invitation from a college friend.
T3-0282.e: Literally 'letter of request', asking guests to come.
T3-0282.t: Used only for weddings; for other events, an invitation is 초대장.

T3-0283.x: The two of them went to Jeju Island for their honeymoon.
T3-0283.t: Pronounced [신혼녀행] — an extra ㄴ sound is added before 여.

T3-0284.x: People usually wear black to a funeral.
T3-0284.e: Literally 'burial rite ceremony'; -식 = ceremony: 결혼식, 졸업식.
T3-0284.t: Pronounced [장녜식] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-0285.x: My grandfather passed away last winter.
T3-0285.e: Honorific form of 돌아가다 'to go back', as if returning to where one came from.
T3-0285.t: Use it instead of 죽다 for elders and other people's family; 돌아가세요 can also just mean 'please go back'.

T3-0286.x: A big festival is held at the university in the fall.

T3-0287.ex: 할머니 생신에 온 가족이 모여서 잔치를 했어요.
T3-0287.x: The whole family got together and threw a party for Grandma's birthday.
T3-0287.e: A native word for a big celebration with food, as in 돌잔치 and 잔치국수 'banquet noodles'.
T3-0287.t: Noodles were served at weddings, so 국수 언제 먹여 줄 거예요? jokingly asks 'When are you getting married?'

T3-0288.ex: 결혼식에는 여러 가지 전통 의식이 있어요.
T3-0288.x: A wedding includes various traditional rituals.
T3-0288.t: A different 의식 means 'consciousness, awareness', as in 의식을 잃다 (to lose consciousness).

T3-0289.ex: 서울에는 경복궁 같은 아름다운 궁궐이 많아요.
T3-0289.x: Seoul has many beautiful palaces, like Gyeongbokgung.
T3-0289.t: Palace names end in -궁: 경복궁, 창덕궁, 덕수궁.

T3-0290.x: On Lunar New Year's morning, I bowed to my parents.
T3-0290.e: Homonym warning: 절 also means 'Buddhist temple', so check the context.

T3-0291.x: The children bowed respectfully to their grandfather on Lunar New Year's Day.
T3-0291.e: 절 'bow' + 하다; a full bow means kneeling and lowering the head toward the floor.
T3-0291.t: A quick nod or bow in greeting is 인사하다; 절하다 is a deep, formal bow.

T3-0292.ex: 이 건물은 중요한 문화재라서 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
T3-0292.x: This building is an important cultural asset, so you can't take pictures.
T3-0292.e: 문화 'culture' + 재 'asset': culture treated as a treasure.

T3-0293.x: Gyeongju has many historic sites from the Silla period.

T3-0294.x: King Sejong the Great was the Joseon king who created Hangeul.
T3-0294.e: Also a slangy prefix meaning 'huge, super': 왕만두 is a jumbo dumpling.

T3-0295.x: People in the Joseon era wore hanbok.

T3-0296.m: modern times, the present day; modern
T3-0296.x: In modern society, a smartphone is a must.

T3-0297.x: Each generation thinks in a slightly different way.
T3-0297.e: Literally 'generation era': the people of one period.

T3-0298.ex: 한국에는 여러 종교를 믿는 사람들이 있어요.
T3-0298.x: In Korea, there are people who follow many different religions.

T3-0299.x: I go to Catholic church with my family every Sunday.
T3-0299.t: 성당 is a Catholic church; a Protestant church is 교회, a key difference in Korea.

T3-0300.ex: 옛날 사람들은 산에 신이 산다고 믿었어요.
T3-0300.x: People long ago believed that gods lived in the mountains.
T3-0300.e: Homonym warning: a native 신 means 'shoes', now usually 신발.
T3-0300.t: For the Christian God, Protestants say 하나님 and Catholics say 하느님.

T3-0301.e: Both syllables mean 'pray', doubled for emphasis.

T3-0302.x: I prayed to pass the exam.
T3-0302.e: Both syllables mean 'pray', doubled for emphasis.
T3-0302.t: Prayers often use -게 해 주세요 'please let…': 건강하게 해 주세요.

T3-0303.x: The Taegeukgi is an important symbol that represents South Korea.

T3-0304.ex: 이 음식의 특징은 맵고 달다는 거예요.
T3-0304.x: What's special about this dish is that it's spicy and sweet.
T3-0304.t: Pronounced [특찡]; common pattern: N의 특징은 -다는 것이에요 'the feature of N is that…'.

T3-0305.x: This cafe's interior is really unique.
T3-0305.t: It can be a compliment (unique) or slightly negative (odd), depending on tone.

T3-0306.x: This market sells a variety of foods.

T3-0307.x: The cultural differences between the two countries are big.
T3-0307.e: Both syllables mean 'differ', doubled for emphasis.

T3-0308.ex: 한국어와 영어의 가장 큰 차이점이 뭐예요?
T3-0308.x: What's the biggest difference between Korean and English?
T3-0308.e: Literally 'point of difference'; -점 = point: 장점, 단점, 공통점.

T3-0309.ex: 우리 둘은 공통점이 많아서 금방 친해졌어요.
T3-0309.x: We have a lot in common, so we became friends quickly.
T3-0309.e: Literally 'a point that runs through both'.

T3-0310.x: Adjusting to life in Korea was easier than I expected.

T3-0311.ex: 새 학교에 적응하는 데 한 달쯤 걸렸어요.
T3-0311.x: It took me about a month to adjust to my new school.
T3-0311.t: Mark what you adapt to with 에: 새 환경에 적응하다 (adapt to a new environment).

T3-0312.ex: 처음 한국에 왔을 때 모든 것이 낯설었어요.
T3-0312.x: When I first came to Korea, everything felt unfamiliar.
T3-0312.e: 낯 'face' + 설다 'unaccustomed': a face you don't know yet.
T3-0312.t: Pronounced [낟썰다]; 낯선 사람 is the everyday word for 'stranger'.

T3-0313.ex: 처음 만난 사람과 이야기하는 것이 좀 어색해요.
T3-0313.x: Talking with someone I've just met feels a bit awkward.
T3-0313.e: Literally 'words blocked': when you can't find anything to say.
T3-0313.t: Also used for unnatural sentences: 이 문장은 좀 어색해요 means 'this sentence sounds a bit off.'

T3-0314.x: I want to study art in college.

T3-0315.ex: 이번 주말에 미술관에서 사진 전시가 있어요.
T3-0315.x: There's a photo exhibition at the art museum this weekend.
T3-0315.t: For the event itself, Koreans usually say 전시회: 전시회에 가요 'I'm going to an exhibition.'

T3-0316.ex: 이 작품은 유명한 화가가 그린 그림이에요.
T3-0316.x: This piece is a painting by a famous artist.

T3-0317.ex: 공연장 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 서 있어요.
T3-0317.x: People are standing in a long line in front of the concert hall.
T3-0317.e: -장 = place for an activity: 공연장, 운동장, 주차장.

T3-0318.ex: 어제 친구와 같이 뮤지컬을 봤는데 정말 재미있었어요.
T3-0318.x: I saw a musical with a friend yesterday, and it was really fun.

T3-0319.x: That pianist's performance was truly beautiful.
T3-0319.t: Use 연주하다 for instruments in formal contexts; in everyday speech 피아노를 치다 or 기타를 치다 is more common.

T3-0320.ex: 저는 요즘 한국 가요를 들으면서 한국어를 공부해요.
T3-0320.x: These days I study Korean while listening to Korean pop songs.
T3-0320.e: Literally 'songs and ballads.' Don't confuse it with 가요 'I go.'
T3-0320.t: K-pop is often called 가요 in Korea; 케이팝 is used more when talking about it internationally.

T3-0321.ex: 이 노래는 가사가 쉬워서 따라 부르기 좋아요.
T3-0321.x: This song has easy lyrics, so it's good for singing along.
T3-0321.e: Literally 'song words.' Homonym: 가사 can also mean housework.

T3-0322.ex: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
T3-0322.x: When the performance ended, the whole audience applauded.
T3-0322.t: 관객 is for a live show or movie audience; TV viewers are 시청자 and readers are 독자.

T3-0323.m: viewing, watching (a show, game or exhibit)
T3-0323.ex: 이 영화는 열다섯 살 이상 관람이 가능합니다.
T3-0323.x: This movie may be viewed by those 15 and older.
T3-0323.t: Pronounced [괄람]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T3-0324.ex: 표는 입구 옆에 있는 매표소에서 사세요.
T3-0324.x: Please buy your ticket at the ticket office next to the entrance.

T3-0325.ex: 인기 있는 공연은 예매가 빨리 끝나요.
T3-0325.x: Tickets for popular shows sell out quickly.
T3-0325.t: 예매 is buying tickets ahead; 예약 is reserving a table, room or appointment.

T3-0326.m: to book (tickets) in advance, to buy (tickets) ahead
T3-0326.x: I booked my weekend train ticket online in advance.

T3-0327.ex: 가수가 무대에 올라가자 사람들이 소리를 질렀어요.
T3-0327.x: As soon as the singer went up on stage, people screamed.
T3-0327.t: 무대에 서다 'to stand on stage' is the common way to say 'to perform.'

T3-0328.m: main character, protagonist; star (of an event)
T3-0328.x: The main character of this drama is an ordinary office worker.
T3-0328.t: Also used for the person of honor: 오늘의 주인공 means 'today's star,' like the birthday person.

T3-0329.m: appearance (on TV, in a film or show)
T3-0329.ex: 그 배우의 영화 출연 소식이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
T3-0329.x: News of that actor appearing in a movie came out.
T3-0329.t: Pronounced [추련]: the ㄹ batchim links to the next vowel.

T3-0330.m: to appear (on a show, in a film), to star in
T3-0330.ex: 제가 좋아하는 가수가 오늘 밤 예능 프로그램에 출연해요.
T3-0330.x: My favorite singer is appearing on a variety show tonight.
T3-0330.e: Literally 'come out to perform' plus 하다.
T3-0330.t: Use the particle 에: 영화에 출연하다 'to appear in a film.'

T3-0331.ex: 그 배우는 연기를 정말 잘해서 상을 받았어요.
T3-0331.x: That actor acts really well, so he won an award.
T3-0331.e: Literally 'performing skill.' Homonyms: 연기 also means smoke, and postponement.

T3-0332.ex: 그녀는 이 영화에서 의사 역할을 연기했어요.
T3-0332.x: She played the role of a doctor in this movie.
T3-0332.e: Literally 'performing skill' plus 하다. A homonym 연기하다 means 'to postpone.'
T3-0332.t: Watch the context: 회의를 연기했어요 means 'we postponed the meeting,' not acting.

T3-0333.ex: 영화의 마지막 장면이 너무 슬퍼서 울었어요.
T3-0333.x: The last scene of the movie was so sad that I cried.
T3-0333.e: Literally 'face of the place': what you see at one moment.

T3-0334.ex: 이 소설의 줄거리를 간단하게 말해 주세요.
T3-0334.x: Please briefly tell me the plot of this novel.
T3-0334.e: Built on 줄기 'stem, main line': the main thread of a story.

T3-0335.ex: 제 취미는 음악 감상과 영화 감상이에요.
T3-0335.x: My hobbies are listening to music and watching movies.
T3-0335.e: Literally 'examine and admire.' Homonym 감상 means one's impressions or thoughts.
T3-0335.t: 음악 감상 and 영화 감상 are the standard ways to list hobbies on forms or in self-introductions.

T3-0336.ex: 윤동주는 한국 사람들이 가장 사랑하는 시인 중 한 명이에요.
T3-0336.x: Yun Dong-ju is one of the poets Koreans love most.

T3-0337.ex: 어렸을 때 엄마가 매일 밤 동화를 읽어 주셨어요.
T3-0337.x: When I was little, my mom read me a fairy tale every night.

T3-0338.ex: 저는 한국 문학에 관심이 많아서 소설을 자주 읽어요.
T3-0338.x: I'm very interested in Korean literature, so I often read novels.
T3-0338.t: Pronounced [문학]: the ㅎ is kept in standard pronunciation.

T3-0339.x: After entering college, I joined a photography club.
T3-0339.e: Native word meaning 'a group of like-minded people'; the standard word for campus clubs.
T3-0339.t: 동아리 is used for school and college clubs; adult hobby groups are usually 동호회.

T3-0340.ex: 방학 동안 다양한 활동을 해 보고 싶어요.
T3-0340.x: I want to try various activities during vacation.

T3-0341.m: to be active, to work (as), to take part in activities
T3-0341.ex: 그 가수는 요즘 미국에서 활동하고 있어요.
T3-0341.x: That singer is working in the US these days.

T3-0342.m: participation, entry (in an event or contest)
T3-0342.x: Applications to enter this contest are due by Friday.

T3-0343.m: to participate in, to enter, to take part in
T3-0343.ex: 저는 다음 달에 한국어 말하기 대회에 참가할 거예요.
T3-0343.x: I'm going to enter a Korean speech contest next month.
T3-0343.e: Literally 'join and add yourself' plus 하다.
T3-0343.t: 참가하다 is for formally entering an event or contest; 참여하다 stresses actively getting involved.

T3-0344.ex: 이 행사는 시민들의 참여로 성공할 수 있었어요.
T3-0344.x: This event succeeded thanks to the participation of citizens.

T3-0345.m: to participate in, to take part in, to get involved
T3-0345.ex: 많은 학생들이 환경 보호 캠페인에 참여했어요.
T3-0345.x: Many students took part in the environmental protection campaign.
T3-0345.e: Literally 'join and take part' plus 하다.
T3-0345.t: Use the particle 에: 수업에 적극적으로 참여하세요 'Take an active part in class.'

T3-0346.ex: 주말마다 양로원에서 봉사 활동을 하고 있어요.
T3-0346.x: I do volunteer work at a nursing home every weekend.
T3-0346.t: Korean students often need 봉사 활동 hours for school records, so it's a very common phrase.

T3-0347.ex: 올림픽 때 많은 대학생들이 자원봉사를 했어요.
T3-0347.x: Many college students volunteered during the Olympics.

T3-0348.x: Namsan Tower is one of Seoul's best-known tourist attractions.

T3-0349.ex: 한옥 마을에서 전통 문화 체험을 했어요.
T3-0349.x: I tried some hands-on traditional culture activities at a hanok village.
T3-0349.e: Literally 'test with the body': learning by doing it yourself.
T3-0349.t: 체험 is a specific firsthand try-out, like 김치 만들기 체험; 경험 is experience in general.

T3-0350.m: to experience firsthand, to try out
T3-0350.ex: 이번 여행에서 한국의 시골 생활을 직접 체험했어요.
T3-0350.x: On this trip, I experienced Korean country life firsthand.
T3-0350.e: Literally 'test with the body' plus 하다.

T3-0351.ex: 제 꿈은 방송국에서 피디로 일하는 거예요.
T3-0351.x: My dream is to work as a producer at a broadcasting station.

T3-0352.ex: 오늘 아침 신문에서 재미있는 기사를 읽었어요.
T3-0352.x: I read an interesting article in this morning's newspaper.
T3-0352.e: Literally 'recorded matters.' Homonym 기사 means driver or technician.
T3-0352.t: Don't mix it up with 기사님, the polite way to address a taxi or bus driver.

T3-0353.ex: 뉴스 보도에 따르면 내일 큰 태풍이 온다고 합니다.
T3-0353.x: According to news reports, a big typhoon is coming tomorrow.
T3-0353.e: Literally 'report and tell.' Homonym 보도 also means sidewalk.
T3-0353.t: 보도에 따르면 'according to reports' is a very common news phrase.

T3-0354.ex: 재미있는 프로그램이 없어서 채널을 계속 돌렸어요.
T3-0354.x: There was nothing good on, so I kept changing channels.
T3-0354.t: 채널을 돌리다 'to turn the channel' is the everyday way to say 'change channels.'

T3-0355.m: to watch (TV, a broadcast), to view
T3-0355.ex: 오늘 밤 아홉 시 뉴스를 꼭 시청하세요.
T3-0355.x: Be sure to watch the 9 o'clock news tonight.
T3-0355.e: Literally 'see and listen.' Homonym 시청 means city hall.
T3-0355.t: 시청하다 sounds formal, like on TV announcements; in conversation people just say 텔레비전을 봐요.

T3-0356.ex: 이 드라마는 많은 시청자들에게 사랑을 받았어요.
T3-0356.x: This drama was loved by many viewers.
T3-0356.e: -자 = person who does it: 시청자, 참가자, 운전자.

T3-0357.ex: 저는 그 가수의 오랜 팬이라서 콘서트에 꼭 가요.
T3-0357.x: I'm a longtime fan of that singer, so I always go to the concerts.
T3-0357.e: From English 'fan.' Homonym: 팬 also means frying pan (프라이팬).
T3-0357.t: 팬 is short for 'fanatic'; K-pop fans call fan meetings 팬미팅 and fan signings 팬 사인회.

T3-0358.forms: 인기 있어요 · 인기 있었어요 · 인기 있는 (+noun)
T3-0358.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들에게 가장 인기 있는 음식이 뭐예요?
T3-0358.x: What food is the most popular with young people these days?
T3-0358.e: Literally 'has people's energy': people are drawn to it.
T3-0358.t: Pronounced [인끼 읻따]: the ㄱ in 인기 is tensed. Opposite: 인기 없다.

T3-0359.ex: 경찰이 그 사건을 아직 조사하고 있어요.
T3-0359.x: The police are still investigating that incident.
T3-0359.e: Literally 'matter item': a case to deal with.
T3-0359.t: Pronounced [사껀]. 사건 is an incident, often criminal; 사고 is an accident like a car crash.

T3-0360.ex: 이번 태풍으로 농촌에 큰 피해가 생겼습니다.
T3-0360.x: This typhoon caused major damage to rural areas.
T3-0360.t: 피해를 주다 'give harm' and 피해를 입다 'suffer harm' are the key collocations; 민폐 is a casual 'nuisance.'

T3-0361.ex: 화재 발생 시에는 엘리베이터를 이용하지 마세요.
T3-0361.x: In case of fire, do not use the elevator.

T3-0362.m: to occur, to happen, to break out
T3-0362.x: A major traffic accident occurred on the highway last night.
T3-0362.t: 발생하다 is formal, typical in news; in conversation use 생기다 or 일어나다.

T3-0363.ex: 경찰은 아직 사고 원인을 찾지 못했어요.
T3-0363.x: The police haven't found the cause of the accident yet.
T3-0363.t: 원인 is the cause of an event; 이유 is a person's reason for doing something.

T3-0364.ex: 시험 결과는 다음 주 월요일에 나와요.
T3-0364.x: The test results come out next Monday.

T3-0365.ex: 그 배우는 인터뷰에서 새 영화에 대해 이야기했어요.
T3-0365.x: The actor talked about the new movie in an interview.
T3-0365.t: For job interviews, Koreans usually say 면접; 인터뷰 is mostly for media interviews.

T3-0366.x: We conducted a survey of 300 students.
T3-0366.e: Literally 'examine and inspect.' Homonym 조사 means grammatical particle.

T3-0367.m: to investigate, to look into, to research
T3-0367.ex: 숙제 때문에 한국의 전통 음식에 대해 조사했어요.
T3-0367.x: I researched traditional Korean food for my homework.

T3-0368.x: I have to prepare the presentation materials by tomorrow.

T3-0369.x: The topic of this presentation is environmental problems.
T3-0369.t: 주제 is what something is about; 제목 is the title written at the top.

T3-0370.ex: 요즘은 스마트폰 같은 전자 기기를 모두 가지고 있어요.
T3-0370.x: These days everyone has electronic devices like smartphones.

T3-0371.e: Literally 'community gathering.' Homonym 사회 means hosting or emceeing an event.
T3-0371.t: 사회생활 usually means life in the working world, not your social life.

T3-0372.x: The state must protect the safety of its people.
T3-0372.e: Literally 'country-house': the nation as one family. Homonym 국가 means national anthem.
T3-0372.t: Pronounced [국까]. 국가 is formal; in everyday speech 나라 is more common.

T3-0373.x: The government announced a new transportation policy.

T3-0374.x: I'm not very interested in politics.

T3-0375.x: In Korea, citizens directly elect the president every five years.
T3-0375.t: Pronounced [대통녕]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ. For a company president, use 사장 or 회장.

T3-0376.x: There's a National Assembly election next month.

T3-0377.ex: 선거 날에는 꼭 투표를 하러 가세요.
T3-0377.x: Be sure to go vote on election day.

T3-0378.x: Everyone has to obey the law.
T3-0378.t: V-는 법 means 'how to': 김치 만드는 법 'how to make kimchi.'

T3-0379.ex: 모든 아이는 교육을 받을 권리가 있습니다.
T3-0379.x: Every child has the right to receive an education.
T3-0379.t: Pronounced [궐리]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ. Pattern: V-(으)ㄹ 권리가 있다.

T3-0380.ex: 한국 남자들은 군대에 갈 의무가 있어요.
T3-0380.x: Korean men have a duty to serve in the military.

T3-0381.ex: 이번 일은 제 책임이니까 제가 해결할게요.
T3-0381.x: This is my responsibility, so I'll take care of it.
T3-0381.t: 책임을 지다 or 책임지다 means 'to take responsibility'; 책임자 is the person in charge.

T3-0382.ex: 그 친구는 책임감이 강해서 일을 믿고 맡길 수 있어요.
T3-0382.x: That friend has a strong sense of responsibility, so I can trust them with work.
T3-0382.e: -감 = a feeling or sense of: 책임감, 자신감, 만족감.

T3-0383.x: You have to follow the rules carefully in the dorm.

T3-0384.x: The government created a new education system.
T3-0384.t: 제도 is a social or legal system; a computer or technical system is 시스템.

T3-0385.m: to break (a rule, promise, law), to violate
T3-0385.ex: 친구가 또 약속을 어겨서 화가 났어요.
T3-0385.x: I got angry because my friend broke a promise again.
T3-0385.t: The opposite is 지키다: 약속을 지키다 'keep a promise' vs. 약속을 어기다 'break a promise.'

T3-0386.x: Yesterday I paid a fine for running a red light.
T3-0386.t: Common in traffic: 신호 위반 'running a light,' 속도 위반 'speeding,' 주차 위반 'parking violation.'

T3-0387.x: If you park here, you'll have to pay a fine.

T3-0388.ex: 이 동네는 범죄가 거의 없어서 안전해요.
T3-0388.x: This neighborhood is safe because there's almost no crime.
T3-0388.t: Use 범죄를 저지르다 for 'to commit a crime'; 범인 is the culprit.

T3-0389.ex: 어젯밤에 옆집에 도둑이 들어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T3-0389.x: I was shocked that a burglar broke into the house next door last night.
T3-0389.t: 도둑맞다 means 'to get something stolen': 지갑을 도둑맞았어요 'My wallet was stolen.'

T3-0390.x: I went on the trip after getting my parents' permission.
T3-0390.t: 허락을 받다 'get permission' and 허락을 구하다 'ask permission' are the key collocations.

T3-0391.m: to allow, to permit, to give permission
T3-0391.ex: 부모님이 혼자 여행 가는 것을 허락하셨어요.
T3-0391.x: My parents allowed me to travel alone.
T3-0391.t: Pronounced [허라카다]; use 허락을 받다 for 'get permission' from someone.

T3-0392.x: Taking photos is prohibited inside the museum.
T3-0392.t: Signs often use it as a suffix: 주차 금지 (no parking), 출입 금지 (no entry).

T3-0393.m: to prohibit, to ban, to forbid
T3-0393.ex: 정부는 공원에서 담배 피우는 것을 금지했습니다.
T3-0393.x: The government banned smoking in parks.

T3-0394.x: Please drive slowly for the children's safety.
T3-0394.e: Literally 'peaceful and whole' — nothing broken, nothing harmed.
T3-0394.t: Add 하다 for the adjective: 안전해요 means 'it's safe.'

T3-0395.x: There are many dangers in the mountains in winter, so be careful.
T3-0395.t: 위험해요! is the everyday way to shout 'Watch out, it's dangerous!'

T3-0396.ex: 눈이 와서 길이 미끄러우니까 주의가 필요해요.
T3-0396.x: It snowed and the roads are slippery, so you need to be careful.
T3-0396.t: Usually pronounced [주이]; don't confuse with 주의 主義 '-ism,' as in 민주주의.

T3-0397.m: to be careful, to pay attention, to watch out
T3-0397.x: Take care of your health so you don't catch a cold.
T3-0397.t: Takes 에: 건강에 주의하다, 차에 주의하다 — slightly more formal than 조심하다.

T3-0398.x: People lined up in an orderly way.
T3-0398.t: Pronounced [질써]; the set phrase is 질서를 지키다 (keep order).

T3-0399.x: I gave my seat to an elderly woman on the subway.
T3-0399.e: Literally 'yield a step' — stepping back so someone else goes first.
T3-0399.t: 자리를 양보하다 (give up your seat) is the classic collocation.

T3-0400.x: Being considerate of other people is important.
T3-0400.e: Literally 'sharing out your concern' to others.

T3-0401.m: to be considerate of, to care about (others)
T3-0401.ex: 제 친구는 항상 다른 사람을 배려해요.
T3-0401.x: My friend is always considerate of others.
T3-0401.e: Literally 'share out your concern' to others.
T3-0401.t: Takes a direct object: 친구를 배려하다, not 친구에게.

T3-0402.x: Gender equality is an important issue.
T3-0402.e: Literally 'even rank' — everyone on the same level.

T3-0403.x: Discrimination based on gender should disappear.
T3-0403.t: 차별 is unfair treatment; for a neutral 'difference,' use 차이.

T3-0404.x: I like weekends because I have a lot of free time.
T3-0404.e: Literally 'coming from oneself' — acting by your own will.
T3-0404.t: 'Free' as in no cost is 무료, not 자유.

T3-0405.m: to be free, to be unrestricted
T3-0405.ex: 방학에는 시간이 자유로워서 여행을 자주 가요.
T3-0405.x: During vacation my time is free, so I travel often.
T3-0405.e: 자유 (freedom) + -롭다, a native suffix meaning 'full of.'

T3-0406.ex: 세계 평화를 위해 많은 사람들이 노력하고 있어요.
T3-0406.x: Many people are working hard for world peace.

T3-0407.x: My grandfather left his hometown during the war.
T3-0407.t: War 'breaks out' with 나다: 전쟁이 났어요.

T3-0408.forms: 국제 + noun: 국제 회의 · 국제공항 · 국제 전화
T3-0408.ex: 다음 달에 서울에서 국제 회의가 열려요.
T3-0408.x: An international conference will be held in Seoul next month.
T3-0408.t: Pronounced [국쩨]; almost always works like an adjective before a noun: 국제 전화, 국제공항.

T3-0409.x: That singer is now famous worldwide.
T3-0409.e: -적 = '-ic/-al,' a hugely productive suffix: 세계적, 국제적, 경제적.
T3-0409.t: Use 세계적인 before a noun (세계적인 회사) and 세계적으로 before a verb or adjective.

T3-0410.ex: 서울의 인구는 천만 명이 조금 안 돼요.
T3-0410.x: Seoul's population is a little under ten million.
T3-0410.e: Literally 'people mouths' — counting the mouths to feed.

T3-0411.x: These days it's hard for young people to find jobs.
T3-0411.e: Literally 'green years' — life in its fresh, green stage.
T3-0411.t: 청년 means young adults; for teenagers use 청소년.

T3-0412.ex: 정부가 어려운 가족에게 생활비 지원을 해 줘요.
T3-0412.x: The government gives living-cost support to families in need.
T3-0412.t: Homonym alert: 지원 志願 means 'applying,' as in 회사에 지원하다 (apply to a company).

T3-0413.ex: 매달 어린이 단체에 기부를 하고 있어요.
T3-0413.x: I donate to a children's organization every month.
T3-0413.e: Literally 'entrust and hand over' to others.

T3-0414.ex: 이 계획의 문제점이 무엇인지 이야기해 봅시다.
T3-0414.x: Let's talk about what the problems with this plan are.
T3-0414.e: -점 = point or aspect, reused often: 문제점, 장점, 단점.
T3-0414.t: Pronounced [문제쩜]; 문제점 is a specific flaw, while 문제 is the problem itself.

T3-0415.ex: 혼자 사는 사람이 늘어나는 현상이 계속되고 있어요.
T3-0415.x: The trend of more people living alone is continuing.
T3-0415.e: Literally 'appearing shape' — something you can observe happening.

T3-0416.ex: 지금 상황이 좋지 않아서 여행을 미뤘어요.
T3-0416.x: The situation isn't good right now, so I postponed the trip.

T3-0417.ex: 지난 10년 동안 이 동네에 큰 변화가 있었어요.
T3-0417.x: This neighborhood has changed a lot over the past ten years.

T3-0418.ex: 한국은 짧은 시간에 큰 경제 발전을 이루었어요.
T3-0418.x: Korea achieved great economic development in a short time.
T3-0418.t: Pronounced [발쩐]; homonym 발전 發電 means 'power generation,' as in 발전소 (power plant).

T3-0419.m: to develop, to progress, to advance
T3-0419.ex: 요즘 기술이 아주 빠르게 발전하고 있어요.
T3-0419.x: Technology is advancing very quickly these days.

T3-0420.x: Thanks to the development of the internet, life has become much easier.
T3-0420.e: Literally 'set out and reach' a higher stage.
T3-0420.t: Pronounced [발딸]; 발달 is natural growth (body, technology), while 발전 stresses progress toward a better state.

T3-0421.ex: 올해는 관광객 수의 증가가 눈에 띄어요.
T3-0421.x: This year the rise in the number of tourists is noticeable.

T3-0422.ex: 혼자 사는 사람이 계속 증가하고 있습니다.
T3-0422.x: The number of people living alone keeps increasing.
T3-0422.t: Formal, common in news and reports; in conversation 늘어나다 sounds more natural.

T3-0423.ex: 아이를 낳는 사람이 줄어서 인구 감소가 걱정이에요.
T3-0423.x: Fewer people are having children, so population decline is a worry.

T3-0424.m: to increase, to grow, to stretch out
T3-0424.ex: 요즘 자전거를 타는 사람이 많이 늘어났어요.
T3-0424.x: Lately the number of people riding bikes has grown a lot.
T3-0424.e: 늘다 (to increase) + 나다 (to come out): growing outward.

T3-0425.forms: 줄어들어요 · 줄어들었어요 · 줄어들 거예요 · 줄어드는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T3-0425.m: to decrease, to shrink, to diminish
T3-0425.ex: 시골에 사는 젊은 사람이 점점 줄어들고 있어요.
T3-0425.x: The number of young people living in the countryside is gradually shrinking.
T3-0425.e: 줄다 (to decrease) + 들다 (to go in): shrinking inward.

T3-0426.m: to become higher, to rise, to increase
T3-0426.x: When summer comes, the temperature rises a lot.
T3-0426.t: Pronounced [노파지다]: the final ㅍ of 높 carries over to the next syllable.

T3-0427.m: to become lower, to drop, to fall
T3-0427.x: As night fell, the temperature dropped a lot.

T3-0428.ex: 요즘 경제가 어려워서 다들 돈을 아껴요.
T3-0428.x: The economy is tough these days, so everyone is saving money.
T3-0428.e: Short for an old phrase, 'govern the world and relieve the people.'

T3-0429.ex: 요즘 물가가 너무 올라서 장보기가 무서워요.
T3-0429.x: Prices have gone up so much lately that grocery shopping is scary.
T3-0429.t: Pronounced [물까]; said [물가] without the tense sound, it means 'waterside.'

T3-0430.x: The trip cost more than I expected.
T3-0430.t: Costs 'go in' with 들다: 비용이 많이 들어요 = it costs a lot.

T3-0431.ex: 전기 소비를 줄이려면 불을 꼭 끄세요.
T3-0431.x: To cut down on electricity use, be sure to turn off the lights.

T3-0432.ex: 소비자들은 싸고 품질이 좋은 물건을 원해요.
T3-0432.x: Consumers want things that are cheap and good quality.
T3-0432.e: -자 = person who does it: 소비자, 과학자, 운전자.

T3-0433.m: to save, to economize, to conserve
T3-0433.ex: 물을 절약하기 위해 샤워 시간을 줄였어요.
T3-0433.x: I cut my shower time to save water.
T3-0433.t: Pronounced [저랴카다]; 절약 is using less, while 저축 is putting money away.

T3-0434.m: to save, to use sparingly; to cherish, to treasure
T3-0434.ex: 용돈을 아껴서 친구 생일 선물을 샀어요.
T3-0434.x: I saved my allowance and bought a birthday present for my friend.
T3-0434.e: Two senses share one idea — not wanting to lose something: 돈을 아끼다, 아끼는 사람.
T3-0434.t: 제가 아끼는 후배 means 'a junior I really care about' — not about money at all.

T3-0435.ex: 하루 종일 게임만 하는 건 시간 낭비예요.
T3-0435.x: Playing games all day is a waste of time.

T3-0436.ex: 그는 어릴 때 가난 때문에 학교를 그만뒀어요.
T3-0436.x: He quit school as a child because of poverty.
T3-0436.e: Probably from an old Sino-Korean word for 'hardship'; add 하다 for 'poor': 가난하다.

T3-0437.x: I went deep into debt buying a house.
T3-0437.t: Alone it's [빋], but before a vowel the ㅈ returns: 빚이 [비지], 빚을 [비즐].

T3-0438.x: This bag is expensive, but the quality is good.

T3-0439.x: I bought a used bike to save money.
T3-0439.t: Usually goes before a noun: 중고차, 중고 책, 중고 거래 (secondhand trading).

T3-0440.x: This store sells only organic vegetables.
T3-0440.t: 판매하다 is the formal, business word; in daily talk just say 팔다.

T3-0441.ex: 인터넷으로 주문한 옷이 아직 배송 중이에요.
T3-0441.x: The clothes I ordered online are still being shipped.
T3-0441.t: 배송 is for shipped goods; food brought to your door is 배달.

T3-0442.ex: 환경 오염 때문에 많은 동물들이 살 곳을 잃었어요.
T3-0442.x: Because of environmental pollution, many animals have lost their homes.

T3-0443.x: The river pollution got worse because of the factory.

T3-0444.m: to be polluted, to be contaminated
T3-0444.ex: 공장에서 나온 물 때문에 바다가 오염됐어요.
T3-0444.x: The sea was polluted by water from the factory.
T3-0444.t: For 'X pollutes Y,' use 오염시키다: 공장이 강을 오염시켰어요.

T3-0445.ex: 오늘은 미세 먼지가 많으니까 마스크를 쓰세요.
T3-0445.x: There's a lot of fine dust today, so wear a mask.
T3-0445.t: Koreans check daily 미세 먼지 forecasts; 미세 먼지가 나쁨 means air quality is bad.

T3-0446.ex: 오랫동안 청소를 안 해서 책상에 먼지가 쌓였어요.
T3-0446.x: I haven't cleaned in a long time, so dust has piled up on my desk.

T3-0447.ex: 봄에는 황사 때문에 하늘이 노랗게 보여요.
T3-0447.x: In spring the sky looks yellow because of yellow dust.
T3-0447.e: Literally 'yellow sand,' blown in from deserts each spring.

T3-0448.ex: 우리 모두 지구를 지키기 위해 노력해야 해요.
T3-0448.x: We all need to work hard to protect the earth.
T3-0448.t: Homonym: 지구 地區 means 'district, zone,' as in 개발 지구.

T3-0449.x: Because of warming, sea temperatures are rising.

T3-0450.ex: 제주도는 기후가 따뜻해서 겨울에도 살기 좋아요.
T3-0450.x: Jeju Island has a warm climate, so it's nice to live there even in winter.
T3-0450.t: 기후 is long-term climate; today's conditions are 날씨.

T3-0451.x: Korea lacks natural resources, so it imports oil.
T3-0451.t: Homonym: 자원 自願 'volunteering,' as in 자원봉사 (volunteer work).

T3-0452.ex: 에너지를 아끼려면 안 쓰는 전기 제품은 꺼 두세요.
T3-0452.x: To save energy, turn off electronics you aren't using.
T3-0452.e: From English 'energy'; note the ㅈ for the 'g' sound.

T3-0453.ex: 태양에서 나오는 에너지로 전기를 만들 수 있어요.
T3-0453.x: We can make electricity with energy from the sun.
T3-0453.e: Literally 'the great yang' — the ultimate source of light and warmth.
T3-0453.t: In daily talk Koreans say 해; 태양 sounds scientific or poetic.

T3-0454.x: Cafés are reducing the use of disposable items.

T3-0455.ex: 바다에 버려진 플라스틱이 큰 문제가 되고 있어요.
T3-0455.x: Plastic dumped in the ocean is becoming a big problem.
T3-0455.e: From English 'plastic'; Korean adds vowels, giving four syllables: peul-la-seu-tik.
T3-0455.t: A plastic bag is not 플라스틱 but 비닐봉지 — a Konglish surprise.

T3-0456.ex: 자연 보호를 위해 쓰레기를 가져가 주세요.
T3-0456.x: Please take your trash with you to protect nature.

T3-0457.x: Sunscreen protects your skin from sunlight.
T3-0457.t: Pattern: A로부터 B를 보호하다 = protect B from A.

T3-0458.ex: 새 약의 개발에는 시간이 오래 걸려요.
T3-0458.x: Developing a new medicine takes a long time.
T3-0458.t: 개발 is actively creating or building something; 발전 is the progress that results.

T3-0459.m: to develop, to create (products, land, skills)
T3-0459.x: That company developed a new cell phone.

T3-0460.x: I prepared an emergency bag in case of natural disasters.

T3-0461.ex: 비가 일주일 동안 내려서 홍수가 났어요.
T3-0461.x: It rained for a week, and there was a flood.
T3-0461.t: Disasters 'happen' with 나다: 홍수가 나다, 지진이 나다, 불이 나다.

T3-0462.x: The drought is severe this summer, so farmers are having a hard time.
T3-0462.e: From 가물다 'to be dry (without rain)' + -ㅁ, a noun-making ending.

T3-0463.ex: 어젯밤에 작은 지진이 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T3-0463.x: There was a small earthquake last night, and I was startled.

T3-0464.x: A big fire broke out at the market yesterday.
T3-0464.t: News says 화재가 발생했다; in conversation people say 불이 났어요.

T3-0465.ex: 봄이 되면 들에 예쁜 꽃이 많이 피어요.
T3-0465.x: When spring comes, lots of pretty flowers bloom in the fields.
T3-0465.e: Homonym warning: not the plural ending -들, as in 사람들. Also seen in 들판 and 들꽃.
T3-0465.t: 산과 들 (mountains and fields) is a common pairing for the countryside.

T3-0466.ex: 우리 집은 언덕 위에 있어서 경치가 좋아요.
T3-0466.x: Our house is on top of a hill, so the view is nice.

T3-0467.x: The children are playing with dirt at the playground.
T3-0467.t: Alone it's pronounced [흑], but 흙이 [흘기], 흙을 [흘글].

T3-0468.x: If you grow plants in your room, the air gets better.
T3-0468.e: Literally 'planted thing'; its partner is 동물, 'moving thing.'
T3-0468.t: Pronounced [싱물] — nasalization of ㄱ before ㅁ.

T3-0469.x: This plant has very big leaves.
T3-0469.e: Often combined as 나뭇잎 (tree leaf) and 꽃잎 (flower petal).
T3-0469.t: 잎이 is pronounced [이피], but 잎 alone and before consonants sounds like [입].

T3-0470.x: In summer, bugs often come into the room.
T3-0470.e: Everyday word for any creepy-crawly; 곤충 is the scientific 'insect'.

T3-0471.ex: 요즘 농촌에는 젊은 사람이 많지 않아요.
T3-0471.x: These days there aren't many young people in rural areas.

T3-0472.ex: 한국 부모들은 자녀 교육에 관심이 많아요.
T3-0472.x: Korean parents care a lot about their children's education.

T3-0473.m: to educate, to teach, to train
T3-0473.ex: 회사에서 신입 사원을 한 달 동안 교육해요.
T3-0473.x: The company trains new employees for a month.
T3-0473.t: Pronounced [교유카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ merges into an aspirated ㅋ.

T3-0474.ex: 졸업 후에 대학원에 가서 공부를 더 하고 싶어요.
T3-0474.x: After graduating, I want to go to grad school and study more.
T3-0474.e: Literally 'university institute' — the institute above 대학 (college).

T3-0475.ex: 동생은 일주일에 두 번 수학 과외를 받아요.
T3-0475.x: My younger sibling gets math tutoring twice a week.
T3-0475.e: Literally 'outside the lessons' — extra study beyond regular class.
T3-0475.t: Use 과외를 받다 for getting tutored and 과외를 하다 for giving it.

T3-0476.ex: 이번 학기에 학점을 잘 받아서 기분이 좋아요.
T3-0476.x: I'm happy because I got good grades this semester.
T3-0476.t: Pronounced [학쩜]; it means both course credits (3학점) and your overall grades.

T3-0477.x: I'm a junior in the business department at my university.

T3-0478.m: Korean (as a school subject); national language
T3-0478.ex: 저는 학교에서 국어 시간을 제일 좋아했어요.
T3-0478.x: I liked Korean class the most in school.
T3-0478.t: Koreans call their own school subject 국어; foreigners learn 한국어.

T3-0479.x: We played soccer in PE today.

T3-0480.ex: 우리 학원 영어 강사는 미국에서 왔어요.
T3-0480.x: The English instructor at our academy came from the US.
T3-0480.t: Used for academy, part-time college, or fitness instructors — not regular school teachers.

T3-0481.ex: 제 꿈은 초등학교 교사가 되는 거예요.
T3-0481.x: My dream is to become an elementary school teacher.

T3-0482.m: homeroom teacher; being in charge of a class
T3-0482.x: This year's homeroom teacher is very kind.
T3-0482.e: Literally 'carrying the duty' — the teacher responsible for a class.

T3-0483.m: classmate (same year), peer who started at the same time
T3-0483.x: I still often meet my college classmates.
T3-0483.e: Literally 'same period' — people who entered school or a company together.
T3-0483.t: Homonym warning: 동기 (動機) also means 'motive'.

T3-0484.x: I have a high school reunion this weekend.
T3-0484.e: Literally 'same window' — studying under the same school window.

T3-0485.x: This research was carried out over five years.
T3-0485.e: Literally 'grind and investigate' — digging deep into a subject.

T3-0487.x: We did a fun experiment in science class.
T3-0487.e: Literally 'real test' — checking an idea in practice.
T3-0487.t: Don't mix up with 시험 (exam); 실험 is a lab experiment.

T3-0488.ex: 수업 시간에 환경 문제에 대해 토론을 했어요.
T3-0488.x: We had a discussion about environmental issues in class.

T3-0489.x: The students debated the death penalty.
T3-0489.t: Use N에 대해 토론하다 for 'to debate about N'.

T3-0490.ex: 교수님이 수업 시작 전에 출석을 부르세요.
T3-0490.x: The professor takes attendance before class starts.
T3-0490.t: 출석을 부르다 means 'to call the roll'.

T3-0491.ex: 저는 한 번도 빠지지 않고 수업에 출석했어요.
T3-0491.x: I attended class without missing it even once.
T3-0491.e: Literally 'come out to your seat' plus -하다.

T3-0492.ex: 감기 때문에 이틀 동안 결석을 했어요.
T3-0492.x: I was absent for two days because of a cold.
T3-0492.e: Literally 'missing seat' — your seat is empty.

T3-0493.x: I overslept and was late for work today.
T3-0493.t: Homonym warning: 지각 (知覺) also means 'perception', but 'lateness' is far more common.

T3-0494.x: I traveled during my leave of absence from school.

T3-0495.ex: 집에 가서 오늘 배운 단어를 복습하세요.
T3-0495.x: Go home and review the words you learned today.

T3-0496.x: I'm not good at memorizing vocabulary.
T3-0496.e: Literally 'recording in the dark' — keeping it in your head without looking.
T3-0496.t: In conversation, people usually say 외우다; 암기 sounds more like study talk.

T3-0497.forms: 깨달아요 · 깨달았어요 · 깨달을 거예요 · 깨달으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
T3-0497.m: to realize, to come to understand
T3-0497.x: Living abroad, I realized how precious my family is.
T3-0497.e: The ㄷ becomes ㄹ before vowels: 깨닫다 → 깨달아요, like 듣다 → 들어요.
T3-0497.t: Often used as -다는 것을 깨닫다: 'to realize that …'.

T3-0498.x: Reading a lot of books broadens your knowledge.

T3-0499.x: Greeting your elders is basic common sense.
T3-0499.e: Literally 'ordinary knowledge' — what everyone is expected to know.
T3-0499.t: 상식이 없다 means someone lacks common sense — fairly harsh criticism.

T3-0500.x: I'm studying Korean with this textbook.

T3-0501.x: Jot down the important points so you don't forget.
T3-0501.e: From English 'memo'; 메모하다 means 'to jot down', not to send an office memo.
T3-0501.t: 메모를 남기다 means 'to leave a note' for someone.

T3-0502.ex: 한국 드라마를 보면 어휘를 늘릴 수 있어요.
T3-0502.x: Watching Korean dramas can help you build your vocabulary.
T3-0502.t: 어휘 is the whole vocabulary; a single word is 단어.

T3-0503.x: It's hard to express my feelings in Korean.

T3-0504.x: In work life, relationships with people are really important.

T3-0505.x: I'm very close with my classmates.
T3-0505.t: It's an adjective, so use N하고/과 친하다; 'to get close' is 친해지다.

T3-0506.m: to become close, to make friends
T3-0506.ex: 같이 여행을 가서 그 친구와 친해졌어요.
T3-0506.x: I got close with that friend after we traveled together.

T3-0507.x: That drama is a love story.

T3-0508.x: He worked up the courage and confessed his feelings to her.
T3-0508.t: In dating culture, 고백 is asking someone to be your boyfriend or girlfriend.

T3-0509.ex: 사랑하는 사람과의 이별은 언제나 슬프고 힘들어요.
T3-0509.x: Parting from someone you love is always sad and hard.

T3-0510.m: blind date (set up by a friend)
T3-0510.x: My friend set me up on a blind date this weekend.
T3-0510.t: 소개팅 is one-on-one; 미팅 in Konglish is a group blind date.

T3-0511.ex: 요즘은 이혼하는 부부가 점점 늘고 있습니다.
T3-0511.x: These days, more and more couples are getting divorced.

T3-0512.x: Excuse me, but how many children do you have?
T3-0512.t: 자녀 is polite and formal; use it when asking about someone else's children.

T3-0513.ex: 부모님은 자식이 몇 살이 되어도 걱정하세요.
T3-0513.x: Parents worry about their children no matter how old they get.
T3-0513.t: Careful: 이 자식 or 저 자식 is an insult like 'this jerk'; for others' kids, say 자녀.

T3-0514.x: These days dads are also very involved in childcare.

T3-0515.m: to take care of, to look after
T3-0515.ex: 주말에는 제가 집에서 어린 조카를 돌봐요.
T3-0515.x: On weekends, I look after my little niece at home.
T3-0515.e: Probably 돌다 (turn around) + 보다 (look) — keep turning to look after someone.

T3-0516.m: filial piety, being a good son or daughter
T3-0516.ex: 부모님께 효도하고 싶어서 여행을 보내 드렸어요.
T3-0516.x: I wanted to do something for my parents, so I sent them on a trip.
T3-0516.e: Literally 'the way of filial piety' — a core Confucian value in Korea.
T3-0516.t: 효도하다 is used for any act of caring for parents, like a gift or a call.

T3-0517.x: Conflict arose because my parents and I think differently.
T3-0517.e: Literally 'arrowroot and wisteria' — two vines twisting around each other in opposite directions.
T3-0517.t: Pronounced [갈뜽] with a tense ㄸ sound.

T3-0518.ex: 제 말을 오해하지 말고 끝까지 들어 주세요.
T3-0518.x: Please don't misunderstand me, and hear me out.
T3-0518.t: To clear up a misunderstanding, say 오해를 풀다.

T3-0519.x: Today I made up with the friend I fought with yesterday.
T3-0519.t: Not related to 화 (anger); use N와/과 화해하다 for 'make up with N'.

T3-0520.ex: 설명을 들어도 이해가 잘 안 돼요.
T3-0520.x: Even after hearing the explanation, I don't really get it.
T3-0520.t: 이해가 안 돼요 ('I don't get it') is more natural than 이해 못 해요 in many situations.

T3-0521.x: Between friends, trust is the most important thing.
T3-0521.e: From 믿다 (to believe) + -음, which turns a verb into a noun.
