T3-0522.ex: 한 번 잃은 신뢰는 다시 얻기 어렵습니다.
T3-0522.x: Trust, once lost, is hard to win back.

T3-0523.x: I listened to my senior's advice and changed my plan.
T3-0523.e: Literally 'loyal telling' — honest words for someone's own good.
T3-0523.t: 충고 often points out a fault; 조언 is softer, helpful advice.

T3-0524.ex: 취업 준비에 대해 교수님께 조언을 구했어요.
T3-0524.x: I asked my professor for advice on job hunting.
T3-0524.t: Common pairs: 조언을 구하다 (ask for advice) and 조언을 해 주다 (give advice).

T3-0525.x: I had a consultation with my teacher about my career path.

T3-0526.x: I talked over the move with my family.
T3-0526.t: 의 at the start of a word is pronounced [의]; casual speech often blurs it toward [이].

T3-0527.m: to consult, to talk over (with someone)
T3-0527.x: Talk important matters over with your parents first.
T3-0527.t: Homonym warning: 상의 (上衣) also means 'top, upper garment'.

T3-0528.m: to get scolded, to get in trouble; to have a hard time
T3-0528.x: I got scolded by the teacher for not doing my homework.
T3-0528.e: Probably 혼 (soul) + 나다 (go out) — so scared your soul leaves you.
T3-0528.t: The person scolding takes 한테 or 께: 엄마한테 혼났어요. The active form is 혼내다.

T3-0529.x: I warmly comforted my friend who failed the exam.

T3-0530.x: The coach encouraged the players in a loud voice.
T3-0530.t: Pronounced [경녀하다] — nasalization changes both ㄱ and ㄹ.

T3-0531.m: fate, destiny (bringing people together); connection, tie
T3-0531.x: It must be fate that we met here.
T3-0531.e: A Buddhist idea: causes and bonds that bring people together.
T3-0531.t: Pronounced [이년]; 인연이 아니다 is a gentle way to say 'it wasn't meant to be'.

T3-0532.x: Even families need to communicate well.
T3-0532.e: Literally 'clearing a channel so things pass through'.

T3-0533.ex: 그 학생은 수업 태도가 아주 좋아요.
T3-0533.x: That student has a very good attitude in class.
T3-0533.e: Literally 'manner and degree' — how you carry yourself.

T3-0534.x: I have a habit of biting my nails.
T3-0534.e: Native word; 버릇없다 (no manners) describes rude, spoiled behavior.

T3-0535.ex: 제 동료는 일을 아주 꼼꼼하게 해요.
T3-0535.x: My coworker does things very meticulously.
T3-0535.e: Doubled 꼼꼼 sounds like careful, step-by-step checking.

T3-0536.ex: 언니는 성격이 차분해서 화를 잘 안 내요.
T3-0536.x: My older sister has a calm personality, so she rarely gets angry.
T3-0536.e: Describes a quiet, settled nature; also used for calm colors or atmosphere.
T3-0536.t: 차분하다 is a calm personality or mood; 침착하다 is staying cool in a crisis.

T3-0537.ex: 불이 났을 때 침착하게 행동해야 해요.
T3-0537.x: When there's a fire, you need to act calmly.
T3-0537.e: Literally 'sunk and settled' — not shaken up.
T3-0537.t: Pronounced [침차카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0538.ex: 그 학생은 수업에 아주 적극적으로 참여해요.
T3-0538.x: That student participates very actively in class.
T3-0538.e: Literally 'piling up to the extreme'. -적 = '-ic/-ive': 긍정적, 부정적.
T3-0538.t: Pronounced [적끅쩍]; use 적극적인 before nouns and 적극적으로 as an adverb.

T3-0539.ex: 저는 처음 만난 사람 앞에서 좀 소극적이에요.
T3-0539.x: I'm a bit reserved around people I've just met.
T3-0539.e: Opposite of 적극적: 'fading from the extreme'.

T3-0540.x: Even when things are hard, I try to think positively.

T3-0541.ex: 너무 부정적인 생각은 건강에 안 좋아요.
T3-0541.x: Overly negative thoughts are bad for your health.
T3-0541.t: Homonym warning: 부정 (不正) also means 'injustice, cheating', as in 부정행위.

T3-0542.ex: 제 동생은 외향적이라서 친구가 정말 많아요.
T3-0542.x: My younger sibling is outgoing, so they have lots of friends.

T3-0543.x: I'm introverted, so giving presentations is hard for me.

T3-0544.ex: 그 사람은 정직해서 거짓말을 하지 않아요.
T3-0544.x: That person is honest, so they don't lie.
T3-0544.t: Pronounced [정지카다]; 정직하다 is morally honest, 솔직하다 is frank about feelings.

T3-0545.x: That athlete is famous but always humble.

T3-0547.ex: 제 동생은 고집이 세서 절대 양보하지 않아요.
T3-0547.x: My younger brother is so stubborn that he never gives in.
T3-0547.e: 고집 is literally 'holding firmly'; 세다 means 'strong'.

T3-0548.x: My father is very picky about food.
T3-0548.e: Works for people (picky) and for tasks or rules (tricky).
T3-0548.t: Use N에 까다롭다 for 'picky about N': 음식에 까다롭다, 옷에 까다롭다.

T3-0549.x: I get a little touchy before exams.
T3-0549.e: Literally 'sharp and quick': nerves or senses that react fast.
T3-0549.t: 예민하다 often means irritable or on edge, not 'sensitive' in the caring sense.

T3-0550.e: Literally 'much affection': full of warmth toward others.
T3-0550.t: 다정하다 is warmth toward people close to you; 친절하다 is polite kindness, even to strangers.

T3-0551.ex: 그 가게 직원은 손님에게 아주 상냥해요.
T3-0551.x: The clerk at that store is very friendly to customers.

T3-0552.x: Our school's rules are very strict.
T3-0552.t: 엄격하다 fits rules, systems and people; 엄하다 is mostly used for strict parents or teachers.

T3-0553.x: The harder things get, the more wisely you need to judge.

T3-0554.ex: 그 소방관은 정말 용감하게 아이를 구했어요.
T3-0554.x: That firefighter very bravely saved the child.

T3-0555.x: You need patience when you teach children.
T3-0555.e: Literally 'a heart that endures and bears'.

T3-0556.ex: 제 남자 친구는 유머 감각이 있어서 재미있어요.
T3-0556.x: My boyfriend is fun to be with because he has a sense of humor.

T3-0557.ex: 욕심을 너무 많이 부리면 안 돼요.
T3-0557.t: 욕심 can be positive too: 일에 욕심이 있다 means 'ambitious about work'.

T3-0558.m: to be excited, to flutter (with anticipation)
T3-0558.ex: 내일 여행을 떠날 생각에 마음이 설레요.
T3-0558.x: My heart flutters at the thought of leaving on a trip tomorrow.
T3-0558.e: Noun form 설렘 is the fluttery, happy-nervous feeling before something good.
T3-0558.t: Say 설레요, not 설레여요; 설레이다 is a common nonstandard form.

T3-0559.x: I feel really proud that I finished a difficult task.
T3-0559.e: Originally 'full to bursting': picture your chest swelling with satisfaction.
T3-0559.t: Pronounced [뿌드타다]: the final ㅅ (sounding ㄷ) plus ㅎ becomes ㅌ.

T3-0560.m: reward, worthwhileness (the feeling that effort paid off)
T3-0560.x: I feel rewarded when I do volunteer work.
T3-0560.e: Builds 보람 있다 and 보람차다, both meaning 'rewarding, worthwhile'.
T3-0560.t: 보람 has no exact English match: it's the satisfying sense that your effort was worth it.

T3-0561.ex: 저희 회사는 고객의 만족을 가장 중요하게 생각합니다.
T3-0561.x: Our company considers customer satisfaction the most important thing.

T3-0562.x: I'm very pleased with the results of this exam.
T3-0562.e: -스럽다 turns a noun into 'feeling like N': 만족스럽다, 자랑스럽다.

T3-0563.x: Customers have a lot of complaints about the service.
T3-0563.t: 불만 is the feeling; to voice it, say 불만을 말하다 or 불평하다.

T3-0564.ex: 그 영화를 보고 큰 감동을 받았어요.
T3-0564.x: I was deeply moved after watching that movie.
T3-0564.t: 감동을 받다 means 'to be moved'; 감동을 주다 means 'to move someone'.

T3-0565.x: The story my grandmother told us was really moving.

T3-0566.m: to be flustered, to be thrown off, to panic
T3-0566.x: I was really flustered because I got a question out of nowhere.
T3-0566.t: 당황하다 is being caught off guard, not shame; for shame use 창피하다.

T3-0567.x: I was taken aback when my friend suddenly got angry.

T3-0568.ex: 저는 잘못이 없는데 혼나서 너무 억울해요.
T3-0568.x: I did nothing wrong but got scolded, so it feels so unfair.
T3-0568.e: Literally 'pressed-down gloom': the frustration of unfair blame.
T3-0568.t: No single English equivalent: use it when you are blamed or punished unfairly.

T3-0569.m: hurt, let down, sad (especially by someone close)
T3-0569.x: I felt hurt because my friend forgot my birthday.
T3-0569.e: Close in meaning to 섭섭하다; both describe hurt feelings toward someone close.
T3-0569.t: Also used at goodbyes: 떠나신다니 서운해요 'I'm sad you're leaving.'

T3-0570.ex: 그 선수가 경기 중에 다쳐서 정말 안타까워요.
T3-0570.x: It's really heartbreaking that the player got hurt during the game.

T3-0571.x: It feels a bit lonely when I eat dinner alone.
T3-0571.t: 외롭다 is about missing people; 쓸쓸하다 also describes empty, bleak places or late autumn.

T3-0572.x: I feel down on rainy days.

T3-0573.forms: 짜증 나요 · 짜증 났어요 · 짜증 날 거예요 · 짜증 나는 (+noun)
T3-0573.m: to be annoyed, irritated; to be annoying
T3-0573.ex: 버스가 계속 안 와서 너무 짜증 나요.
T3-0573.x: I'm so annoyed because the bus just won't come.
T3-0573.e: 짜증 'irritation' + 나다 'to arise': irritation wells up.
T3-0573.t: 짜증 나다 is feeling annoyed; 짜증을 내다 is showing it by snapping at someone.

T3-0574.m: to get angry, to be mad
T3-0574.x: I got mad because my brother broke my stuff.
T3-0574.e: Literally 'fire comes out': anger pictured as rising fire.
T3-0574.t: 화나다 is feeling angry; 화를 내다 (화내다) is expressing anger at someone.

T3-0575.m: to be worried, to feel anxious
T3-0575.ex: 내일 있을 면접이 너무 걱정돼서 잠이 안 와요.
T3-0575.x: I'm so worried about tomorrow's interview that I can't sleep.
T3-0575.e: 걱정 'worry' + 되다; 걱정 is a native word, not Sino-Korean.
T3-0575.t: 걱정돼요 is 'I'm worried'; 걱정하지 마세요 is the usual 'Don't worry.'

T3-0576.ex: 미래에 대한 불안 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
T3-0576.x: I can't sleep because of anxiety about the future.
T3-0576.t: Pronounced [부란]: the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

T3-0577.x: I always get nervous before a presentation.
T3-0577.e: Literally 'tight stretch', like a drawn bowstring.

T3-0578.ex: 결과를 기다리면서 초조해서 계속 시계를 봤어요.
T3-0578.x: Waiting for the results, I was so on edge that I kept checking the clock.
T3-0578.e: Literally 'scorched and dry': burning with impatience.

T3-0579.ex: 실패하는 것이 두려워서 시작을 못 했어요.
T3-0579.x: I was afraid of failing, so I couldn't start.
T3-0579.t: 무섭다 is fear of something scary; 두렵다 is deeper, often about failure or the future.

T3-0580.x: I was so embarrassed because I fell in front of people.
T3-0580.e: Sino-Korean, but the syllables don't help here; learn it as a whole.
T3-0580.t: 창피하다 is public embarrassment; 부끄럽다 can also mean shy or ashamed of yourself.

T3-0581.ex: 제가 새 옷을 사면 동생이 질투를 해요.
T3-0581.x: When I buy new clothes, my younger sister gets jealous.
T3-0581.e: Both syllables mean 'jealous', doubled for emphasis.
T3-0581.t: 부럽다 is harmless 'envious'; 질투 has a negative, resentful edge.

T3-0582.ex: 최선을 다했으니까 이번 일에 후회는 없어요.
T3-0582.x: I did my best, so I have no regrets about this.
T3-0582.t: Common pattern: -(으)ㄴ 것을 후회하다 'to regret having done'.

T3-0583.x: After making a mistake, you need to reflect on it.
T3-0583.t: 반성 means learning from mistakes; 후회 just means wishing you hadn't.

T3-0584.m: to reflect on (one's mistakes), to be sorry for
T3-0584.x: I'm deeply reflecting on my mistake.

T3-0585.x: Some people are unhappy even if they have a lot of money.

T3-0586.x: Don't lose hope, even in a hard situation.
T3-0586.t: Pronounced [히망]: 희 is said like 히.

T3-0587.x: I was very disappointed when I saw my test results.

T3-0588.forms: 포기해요 · 포기했어요 · 포기할 거예요 · 포기하지 마세요
T3-0588.x: No matter how hard it gets, don't give up on your dream.
T3-0588.t: 포기하지 마! 'Don't give up!' is a very common word of encouragement.

T3-0589.x: When my teacher praises me, I gain confidence.

T3-0590.ex: 그는 자존심이 강해서 도움을 받지 않아요.
T3-0590.x: He has strong pride, so he doesn't accept help.
T3-0590.t: 자존심 is pride you protect; 자존감 is healthy self-esteem.

T3-0591.m: to boast, to show off, to brag about
T3-0591.ex: 친구가 저에게 새로 산 휴대폰을 자랑했어요.
T3-0591.x: My friend showed off his new phone to me.
T3-0591.e: 자랑 'something to be proud of' + 하다; also gives 자랑스럽다 'proud'.

T3-0592.x: I'm really proud of my daughter.
T3-0592.t: 자랑스럽다 is pride in someone or something; 뿌듯하다 is the warm glow after your own achievement.

T3-0593.ex: 저는 어렸을 때부터 역사에 흥미가 많았어요.
T3-0593.x: I've been very interested in history since I was young.
T3-0593.t: 흥미 is interest or fun in a subject; 관심 is attention or concern, also toward people.

T3-0594.x: The content of that book was very interesting.
T3-0594.e: -롭다 makes adjectives from nouns: 흥미롭다, 자유롭다, 평화롭다.

T3-0595.x: Parents have a big influence on their children.
T3-0595.e: Literally 'shadow and echo': what follows something wherever it goes.
T3-0595.t: 영향을 주다 or 영향을 미치다 means 'to influence'; 영향을 받다 means 'to be influenced'.

T3-0596.x: Everyone's way of studying is a little different.
T3-0596.t: 방법 is a specific way to do something; 방식 is a general style or system.

T3-0597.ex: 결과보다 과정이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
T3-0597.x: Sometimes the process matters more than the result.
T3-0597.t: A homonym 과정 means 'course of study', as in 석사 과정 'master's program'.

T3-0598.ex: 이번 여행의 가장 큰 목적은 휴식이에요.
T3-0598.x: The main purpose of this trip is to rest.
T3-0598.t: 목적 is the reason behind an action; 목표 is a concrete target you aim to reach.

T3-0599.x: Each company has different criteria for hiring employees.

T3-0600.x: There's a high chance of rain tomorrow.
T3-0600.t: Pronounced [가능썽]: the ㅅ in -성 is usually tensed.

T3-0601.ex: 모두 운동의 필요성을 잘 알고 있어요.
T3-0601.x: Everyone knows well that exercise is necessary.

T3-0602.x: The older I get, the more I feel the importance of health.
T3-0602.e: Literally 'the quality of being weighty and important'.

T3-0603.ex: 엄마는 우리 집에서 중요한 역할을 해요.
T3-0603.x: Mom plays an important role in our family.
T3-0603.e: Literally 'divided duty': each person's share of the work.
T3-0603.t: Pronounced [여칼]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0604.x: This phone has a lot of convenient features.
T3-0604.e: Literally 'machine ability': what a device or organ can do.

T3-0605.ex: 제 입장에서는 그 결정을 이해하기 어려워요.
T3-0605.x: From my standpoint, that decision is hard to understand.
T3-0605.e: Literally 'standing place': where you stand on an issue.
T3-0605.t: A homonym 입장 means 'entrance, admission', as in 입장료 'admission fee'.

T3-0606.ex: 같은 문제도 관점에 따라 다르게 보여요.
T3-0606.x: The same problem looks different depending on your perspective.

T3-0607.x: That person's claim has no basis.

T3-0608.m: to claim, to argue, to insist
T3-0608.x: He kept insisting that he was right.
T3-0608.t: Usually used with -다고: 옳다고 주장하다 'to insist that one is right'.

T3-0609.ex: 이 책에는 다양한 성공 사례가 나와요.
T3-0609.x: This book contains various success stories.
T3-0609.t: A homonym 사례 means 'thanks, reward', as in 사례금 'reward money'.

T3-0610.ex: 요즘 환경과 관련이 있는 책을 읽고 있어요.
T3-0610.x: These days I'm reading books related to the environment.
T3-0610.t: Pronounced [괄련]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T3-0611.m: to be related, to be connected
T3-0611.ex: 이 일은 제 전공과 관련되어 있어요.
T3-0611.x: This job is related to my major.

T3-0612.x: There's a saying that failure is the mother of success.

T3-0613.ex: 실패를 두려워하지 말고 다시 해 보세요.
T3-0613.x: Don't be afraid of failure; try again.
T3-0613.t: 실수 is a small slip; 실패 is failing at a goal.

T3-0614.ex: 외국에서 일하는 것은 저에게 큰 도전이에요.
T3-0614.x: Working abroad is a big challenge for me.
T3-0614.e: Literally 'provoke a fight'; now any challenge you take on.

T3-0615.m: to challenge oneself, to take on, to try
T3-0615.ex: 올해는 처음으로 마라톤에 도전해 보려고 해요.
T3-0615.x: This year I'm going to try running a marathon for the first time.
T3-0615.e: Literally 'provoke a fight'; now taking on any challenge.

T3-0616.ex: 위기 극복을 위해 모두 함께 노력했어요.
T3-0616.x: Everyone worked together to overcome the crisis.

T3-0617.ex: 그녀는 어려운 환경을 극복하고 의사가 되었어요.
T3-0617.x: She overcame difficult circumstances and became a doctor.
T3-0617.t: Pronounced [극뽀카다]: the ㅂ is tensed, and ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0618.m: to achieve, to accomplish; to form, to make up
T3-0618.x: I worked hard and finally achieved my dream.
T3-0618.e: Its passive 이루어지다 means 'to come true': 꿈이 이루어지다.
T3-0618.t: Common collocations: 꿈을 이루다 'achieve a dream' and 목표를 이루다 'reach a goal'.

T3-0619.m: to put into practice, to act on
T3-0619.ex: 환경을 위해 작은 일부터 실천해 보세요.
T3-0619.x: Try putting small things into practice for the environment.
T3-0619.e: Literally 'actually tread': turning words into action.

T3-0620.x: Actions are much more important than words.

T3-0621.m: to decide, to make up one's mind, to resolve
T3-0621.x: I've resolved to quit smoking starting this year.
T3-0621.t: 결심하다 is a personal resolution, usually with -기로: 운동하기로 결심하다.

T3-0622.ex: 중요한 결정은 천천히 하는 게 좋아요.
T3-0622.x: It's better to make important decisions slowly.
T3-0622.t: Pronounced [결쩡]: the ㅈ is tensed after ㄹ.

T3-0623.x: Which path you take is your choice.

T3-0624.ex: 사람을 겉모습만 보고 판단하면 안 돼요.
T3-0624.x: You shouldn't judge people only by their appearance.

T3-0625.m: to evaluate, to assess, to rate
T3-0625.x: The teacher evaluated the students' presentations today.

T3-0626.ex: 출발하기 전에 비행기 시간 확인을 꼭 하세요.
T3-0626.x: Be sure to check your flight time before you leave.
T3-0626.t: Pronounced [화긴] — the ㄱ batchim slides into the next vowel.

T3-0627.m: to admit, to acknowledge; to recognize (as valid)
T3-0627.e: Literally 'recognize and settle' — accept something as fact.

T3-0628.x: I completely agree with that opinion.
T3-0628.t: Use -에 for what you agree with: 그 의견에 동의해요 'I agree with that opinion.'

T3-0629.x: The plan was canceled because many people opposed it.
T3-0629.t: 반대 also means 'opposite': 반대 방향 'the opposite direction', 반대말 'antonym.'

T3-0630.x: My friend suggested that we go hiking together this weekend.

T3-0631.x: The employees demanded a raise from the company.
T3-0631.e: Literally 'need and seek' — asking firmly for something.
T3-0631.t: 요구하다 is stronger than 요청하다; it sounds like a demand, not a polite request.

T3-0632.x: I got lost, so I asked the police for help.

T3-0633.m: to provide, to offer, to supply
T3-0633.ex: 이 호텔은 손님들에게 아침 식사를 무료로 제공합니다.
T3-0633.x: This hotel provides breakfast to guests free of charge.

T3-0634.ex: 이 도서관은 한 번에 빌릴 수 있는 책을 다섯 권으로 제한해요.
T3-0634.x: This library limits you to borrowing five books at a time.
T3-0634.t: 나이 제한 'age limit' and 속도 제한 'speed limit' are everyday collocations.

T3-0635.ex: 이 그림은 역사적으로 가치가 아주 높아요.
T3-0635.x: This painting has great historical value.
T3-0635.e: Literally 'value and worth' — two syllables with the same meaning.
T3-0635.t: V-(으)ㄹ 가치가 있다 means 'worth doing': 볼 가치가 있어요 'It's worth seeing.'

T3-0636.ex: 이 문제는 개인이 혼자 해결하기 어려워요.
T3-0636.x: This problem is hard for an individual to solve alone.

T3-0637.ex: 개인적으로 저는 이 영화가 더 좋아요.
T3-0637.x: Personally, I like this movie better.
T3-0637.e: -적 turns a noun into '-al/-ic': 개인적, 사회적, 경제적.
T3-0637.t: Mostly used as 개인적으로 'personally' or 개인적인 + noun 'personal ...'.

T3-0638.x: We went on a field trip to the museum as a group.

T3-0639.ex: 이 영어 프로그램은 초등학생을 대상으로 합니다.
T3-0639.x: This English program is aimed at elementary school students.
T3-0639.e: Literally 'the image you face' — whatever something is aimed at.
T3-0639.t: Key pattern: N을/를 대상으로 'aimed at N, for N' — very common in notices.

T3-0640.x: I'm worried because the exam covers so much material.
T3-0640.e: Literally 'the frame that surrounds' — the boundary of something.

T3-0641.x: This lake is about ten meters deep.
T3-0641.e: From 깊다 'deep' + -이; as an adverb, 깊이 also means 'deeply'.
T3-0641.t: Pronounced [기피]; the same -이 pattern makes 높이 'height' and 길이 'length.'

T3-0642.ex: 비가 많이 오니까 속도를 좀 줄이세요.
T3-0642.x: It's raining hard, so please slow down.
T3-0642.t: Pronounced [속또] — the ㄷ tenses after ㄱ.

T3-0643.x: How far is it from your house to school?
T3-0643.e: Homonym warning: 거리 also means 'street' and 'material' (일거리); context tells which.

T3-0644.x: Now is a good time to travel to Jeju Island.
T3-0644.t: 시기 is a point or phase (the right time); 기간 is a length of time.

T3-0645.ex: 그 사람을 본 순간 사랑에 빠졌어요.
T3-0645.x: I fell in love the moment I saw that person.
T3-0645.t: V-(으)ㄴ 순간 means 'the moment (someone) did': 문을 연 순간 'the moment I opened the door.'

T3-0646.m: at that time, back then, those days
T3-0646.x: Back then, we didn't have a cell phone at home.

T3-0647.ex: 졸업 이후에 한 번도 그 친구를 못 만났어요.
T3-0647.x: I haven't seen that friend even once since graduation.

T3-0648.x: The house I used to live in was far from school.
T3-0648.t: Don't confuse it with a different 이전 meaning 'relocation', as in 사무실 이전 'office move.'

T3-0649.x: Regardless of the result, I did my best.
T3-0649.t: Set phrase: 최선을 다하다 'to do one's best' — you'll hear 최선을 다하겠습니다 in many speeches.

T3-0650.x: In Korea, greeting people is the most basic part of good manners.

T3-0651.ex: 외국어는 처음에 기초를 잘 배워야 해요.
T3-0651.x: With a foreign language, you have to learn the basics well at the start.
T3-0651.e: Literally 'base stone' — the stone a pillar stands on.
T3-0651.t: 기초 suggests a starting level (기초 한국어 'beginner Korean'); 기본 means the standard essentials.

T3-0652.x: Seoul has long been the center of Korea's economy.

T3-0653.x: I heard that restaurant is good.

T3-0654.x: Dreams and reality are often different.

T3-0655.x: That movie was more fun than I imagined.
T3-0655.t: 상상도 못 했어요 means 'I never imagined it' — great for big surprises.

T3-0656.x: I tried imagining what I'll be like in ten years.

T3-0657.x: Far more people came than expected.

T3-0658.m: to expect, to predict, to anticipate
T3-0658.x: I expected this exam to be difficult.

T3-0659.m: opportunity, turning point, trigger (for a change)
T3-0659.ex: 이 여행을 계기로 한국어 공부를 시작했어요.
T3-0659.x: This trip was what got me started studying Korean.
T3-0659.e: The moment that sets something in motion.
T3-0659.t: N을 계기로 'with N as the turning point' is the key pattern.

T3-0660.x: This novel is set in Seoul in the 1950s.

T3-0661.m: pros and cons, strengths and weaknesses
T3-0661.ex: 도시 생활과 시골 생활에는 각각 장단점이 있어요.
T3-0661.x: City life and country life each have their pros and cons.
T3-0661.e: Literally 'long and short points' — strengths and weaknesses.
T3-0661.t: Pronounced [장단쩜] — the ㅈ tenses in this compound.

T3-0662.x: The company got through a major crisis.

T3-0663.ex: 내일 시험 잘 보세요. 행운을 빌어요!
T3-0663.x: Good luck on your test tomorrow. Fingers crossed!
T3-0663.t: 행운을 빌어요 is 'Good luck!'; casually, friends often just say 화이팅.

T3-0664.x: What a coincidence to run into you here!

T3-0665.x: I ran into a high school friend on the street by chance.

T3-0666.x: This class is required for all first-year students.
T3-0666.t: Pronounced [필쑤] — the ㅅ tenses after ㄹ.

T3-0667.x: After coming back from the trip, I went back to my daily routine.
T3-0667.t: Pronounced [일쌍] — the ㅅ tenses after ㄹ.

T3-0668.ex: 스마트폰은 일상생활에 꼭 필요한 물건이 됐어요.
T3-0668.x: Smartphones have become essential in everyday life.

T3-0669.x: The most important thing in life is health.
T3-0669.t: 인생 is life as a whole journey; 생활 is day-to-day living; 생명 is biological life.

T3-0670.ex: 그는 아이들을 위해 바쁜 삶을 살았어요.
T3-0670.x: He lived a busy life for his children.
T3-0670.e: From 살다 'to live' + -ㅁ, a noun-making ending.
T3-0670.t: Pronounced [삼]; the ㄹ in ㄻ is silent before a consonant or at the end.

T3-0671.ex: 의사는 사람의 생명을 구하는 일을 해요.
T3-0671.x: Doctors work to save people's lives.

T3-0672.x: Firefighters risk their lives to save people.
T3-0672.e: Probably 목 'throat' + 숨 'breath' — the breath of life.
T3-0672.t: 목숨을 걸다 'to risk one's life' is the most common collocation.

T3-0673.m: by oneself, on one's own; oneself
T3-0673.ex: 우리 아이는 이제 스스로 옷을 입어요.
T3-0673.x: My child now gets dressed on her own.
T3-0673.t: 스스로 stresses doing it without help; 혼자 stresses being alone.

T3-0674.m: the person in question, oneself; (formal) you
T3-0674.ex: 신청은 반드시 본인이 직접 하셔야 합니다.

T3-0675.m: the other person, the other party, counterpart
T3-0675.ex: 대화할 때는 상대방의 말을 잘 들어야 해요.
T3-0675.x: When you talk, you should listen carefully to the other person.

T3-0676.ex: 남의 말을 너무 신경 쓰지 마세요.
T3-0676.x: Don't worry too much about what others say.
T3-0676.e: Homonym warning: 남 also means 'south' and 'male'; context tells which.

T3-0677.ex: 점심은 각자 먹고 한 시에 다시 만나요.
T3-0677.x: Let's each have lunch on our own and meet again at one.

T3-0678.ex: 내일 축구 시합이 있어서 일찍 자야 해요.
T3-0678.x: I have a soccer match tomorrow, so I need to go to bed early.
T3-0678.e: Literally 'test by meeting' — testing strength against each other.
T3-0678.t: 시합 sounds a bit more everyday; news reports usually say 경기 for sports games.

T3-0679.ex: 우리 학교 팀이 드디어 우승을 차지했어요.
T3-0679.x: Our school team finally won the championship.

T3-0680.m: to win (a championship), to take first place
T3-0680.ex: 한국 축구 팀이 이번 대회에서 우승했습니다.
T3-0680.x: The Korean soccer team won this tournament.
T3-0680.t: 이기다 means beating an opponent; 우승하다 means winning the whole tournament.

T3-0681.x: Seoul hosted the Summer Olympics in 1988.
T3-0681.t: 개최하다 is news style; in conversation, 열다 or just 하다 is more natural.

T3-0682.m: to proceed, to carry out; to host (a show)
T3-0682.ex: 회의는 예정대로 오후 세 시에 진행하겠습니다.
T3-0682.x: The meeting will go ahead as planned at 3 p.m.

T3-0683.ex: 결혼식 사회자는 신랑의 친한 친구가 맡았어요.
T3-0683.x: The groom's close friend was the MC at the wedding.
T3-0683.e: Literally 'person managing the meeting'; unrelated to the 사회 meaning 'society'.
T3-0683.t: To be the MC is 사회를 보다: 제가 사회를 볼게요 'I'll MC.'

T3-0684.ex: 회의 참석 여부를 오늘까지 알려 주세요.
T3-0684.x: Please let us know by today whether you'll attend the meeting.
T3-0684.e: Literally 'join a seat' — take your seat at an event.
T3-0684.t: 참석 is attending (a meeting, a wedding); 참가 is actively taking part (a contest).

T3-0685.m: to postpone, to put off, to delay
T3-0685.ex: 회사는 비 때문에 행사를 다음 주로 연기했어요.
T3-0685.x: The company postponed the event to next week because of the rain.
T3-0685.e: Literally 'extend the date'. Homonyms: 연기 also means 'acting' and 'smoke'.
T3-0685.t: 연기하다 sounds formal; in daily speech, 미루다 is more common.

T3-0686.m: to put off, to postpone; to push (work) onto someone
T3-0686.ex: 오늘 할 일을 내일로 미루지 마세요.
T3-0686.x: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
T3-0686.e: Probably related to 밀다 'to push' — pushing a task later.
T3-0686.t: 남에게 일을 미루다 means 'to push your work onto someone else.'

T3-0687.x: Sorry, there's been a sudden change in the schedule.

T3-0688.m: to change, to alter, to modify
T3-0688.x: To change your password, press this button.
T3-0688.t: 변경하다 is notice-style; in conversation, 바꾸다 sounds more natural.

T3-0689.m: to inform, to let (someone) know, to announce
T3-0689.ex: 시간이 정해지면 저에게 꼭 알려 주세요.
T3-0689.x: Please be sure to let me know once the time is set.
T3-0689.e: Causative of 알다 'to know' — literally 'make someone know'.

T3-0690.m: to deliver, to pass on, to convey
T3-0690.ex: 선생님의 말씀을 반 친구들에게 잘 전달했어요.
T3-0690.x: I passed the teacher's message on to my classmates.

T3-0691.ex: 다음 주에 떠나는 동료의 송별회를 열었어요.
T3-0691.x: We threw a farewell party for a coworker leaving next week.

T3-0692.x: There's a welcome party for new students on Friday.

T3-0693.m: to prepare, to arrange, to get ready; to raise (money)
T3-0693.ex: 부모님 생신 선물을 마련하려고 돈을 모았어요.
T3-0693.x: I saved money to get my parents a birthday present.
T3-0693.t: Common collocations: 돈을 마련하다 'raise money', 자리를 마련하다 'arrange a get-together.'

T3-0694.ex: 서울에서는 대중교통이 편리해서 차가 없어도 돼요.
T3-0694.x: Public transportation in Seoul is so convenient that you don't need a car.
T3-0694.e: Literally 'traffic for the big crowd' — transport for the general public.

T3-0695.ex: 출근 시간에는 교통 체증이 아주 심해요.
T3-0695.x: Traffic is really bad during the morning rush hour.
T3-0695.e: Literally 'traffic stuck-symptom'; 체증 on its own also means indigestion.
T3-0695.t: In conversation people usually say 차가 막혀요; 교통 체증 sounds like news or writing.

T3-0696.forms: 차가 막혀요 · 차가 막혔어요 (casual: 차 막혀)
T3-0696.m: traffic is heavy, to be stuck in traffic
T3-0696.ex: 금요일 저녁에는 차가 막혀서 지하철을 타요.
T3-0696.x: Traffic is bad on Friday evenings, so I take the subway.
T3-0696.e: Literally 'the cars are blocked'; 막히다 is the passive of 막다 'to block'.
T3-0696.t: Pronounced [마키다] — ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0697.x: Always fasten your seat belt when you get in the car.
T3-0697.t: You 매다 a seat belt (안전벨트를 매다) and 풀다 to unfasten it.

T3-0698.x: I got my driver's license last summer.
T3-0698.t: 'To get a license' is 운전면허를 따다, not 받다.

T3-0699.ex: 버스에 승객이 너무 많아서 앉을 수 없었어요.
T3-0699.x: There were so many passengers on the bus that I couldn't sit down.

T3-0700.x: Get off at the next station and transfer to Line 2.
T3-0700.t: In casual speech people say 갈아타다; 환승 appears on signs and announcements.

T3-0701.x: I bought a round-trip train ticket from Seoul to Busan.

T3-0702.ex: 편도로 가는 비행기 표가 더 비쌀 때도 있어요.
T3-0702.x: Sometimes a one-way plane ticket is even more expensive.
T3-0702.t: Homonym: 편도 also means 'tonsils', as in 편도선.

T3-0703.x: Boarding for the plane begins 30 minutes before departure.

T3-0704.m: to board, to get on (a plane, ship, etc.)
T3-0704.ex: 승객 여러분은 지금 비행기에 탑승해 주시기 바랍니다.
T3-0704.x: All passengers, please board the plane now.
T3-0704.t: A formal word for announcements and signs; in everyday talk, people just say 비행기를 타요.

T3-0705.m: departure (from a country), leaving the country
T3-0705.x: Be sure to check your passport before leaving the country.

T3-0706.x: I got in line to go through immigration.

T3-0707.x: I bought presents for my parents at the airport duty-free shop.

T3-0708.ex: 한국과 미국은 시차가 커서 전화하기 힘들어요.
T3-0708.x: There's a big time difference between Korea and the US, so it's hard to call.
T3-0708.t: For jet lag, say 시차 적응이 안 돼요, literally 'I can't adjust to the time difference.'

T3-0709.forms: 점차 + change verb: 점차 늘어나다, 점차 좋아지다
T3-0709.ex: 봄이 오면서 날씨가 점차 따뜻해지고 있어요.
T3-0709.x: With spring coming, the weather is gradually getting warmer.
T3-0709.t: 점차 sounds a bit more formal than 점점; both pair with verbs of change like -아/어지다.

T3-0710.x: After preparing for three years, I finally passed the exam.
T3-0710.e: Related to 마치다 'to finish': the point where something is finished.
T3-0710.t: Like 드디어, it marks a long-awaited result; 결국 can also mean an unwanted outcome.

T3-0711.forms: 겨우 + verb (barely): 겨우 도착했어요; 겨우 + amount (only): 겨우 천 원
T3-0711.x: I woke up late and barely caught the bus.
T3-0711.t: Before a number, 겨우 means 'only, a mere': 겨우 다섯 명 'only five people'.

T3-0712.ex: 길이 막혀서 간신히 비행기 시간에 맞췄어요.
T3-0712.x: The roads were jammed, so I barely made my flight.

T3-0713.forms: 즉시 + action: 즉시 연락하다, 즉시 출발하다
T3-0713.ex: 문제가 생기면 즉시 저에게 연락해 주세요.
T3-0713.x: If a problem comes up, please contact me immediately.

T3-0714.m: right now, right away, immediately; for the time being
T3-0714.ex: 엄마가 지금 당장 집으로 돌아오라고 하셨어요.
T3-0714.x: Mom told me to come home right now.
T3-0714.t: With 은, it means 'for now': 당장은 돈이 없어요 'I don't have money right now.'

T3-0715.ex: 제가 도착했을 때 영화는 이미 시작했어요.
T3-0715.x: When I arrived, the movie had already started.
T3-0715.t: 벌써 adds surprise that something happened early; 이미 just states it's already done.

T3-0716.forms: 일단 + action (first, for now): 일단 먹자; 일단 -(으)면 (once ...)
T3-0716.m: first, for now, for the moment; once
T3-0716.x: I'm hungry, so let's eat first and then talk.
T3-0716.e: Hanja reads 'one morning'; in use it means 'first of all' or 'once'.
T3-0716.t: Very common in speech to propose a first step: 일단 가 보자 'Let's just go and see.'

T3-0717.m: often, from time to time, now and then
T3-0717.x: On weekends, I often go hiking with my friends.
T3-0717.e: The hanja once meant 'all sorts'; today it simply means 'now and then'.

T3-0718.x: Ten years have passed, but that restaurant is still delicious.
rel: to be the same as ever

T3-0719.m: for a while, for some time
T3-0719.ex: 이사한 후에 한동안 친구들을 못 만났어요.
T3-0719.x: After moving, I couldn't see my friends for a while.
T3-0719.e: 한 'one' + 동안 'period': one stretch of time.

T3-0720.m: one's whole life, lifetime; all one's life
T3-0720.x: My grandfather lived in this village his whole life.
T3-0720.e: Literally 'one's ordinary life', the span of a whole life.
T3-0720.t: Often used alone like an adverb: 평생 잊지 않을게요 'I'll never forget it as long as I live.'

T3-0721.ex: 이 순간을 영원히 잊지 못할 거예요.
T3-0721.x: I will never forget this moment.

T3-0722.x: The two people raised their hands at the same time.

T3-0723.x: This exam was quite a bit harder than the last one.
T3-0723.e: Literally 'matching up', so a considerable amount.

T3-0724.x: The performance I saw yesterday was incredibly fun.

T3-0725.ex: 이 지역은 여름에 대체로 덥고 습해요.
T3-0725.x: This region is generally hot and humid in the summer.
T3-0725.e: Literally 'by the main body', so on the whole.

T3-0726.forms: 충분히 + verb: 충분히 쉬세요; 충분히 -(으)ㄹ 수 있다
T3-0726.ex: 감기에 걸리면 물을 충분히 마셔야 해요.
T3-0726.x: When you have a cold, you need to drink enough water.
T3-0726.t: 충분히 -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 means 'you can definitely do it': 충분히 할 수 있어요!

T3-0727.x: I'm really sorry I completely forgot our appointment.

T3-0728.forms: 전혀 + negative: 전혀 몰라요, 전혀 안 아파요
T3-0728.x: I don't know that person at all.
T3-0728.e: From 'whole': wholly, used to mean 'not at all' with negatives.
T3-0728.t: Always pair 전혀 with a negative like 안, 못, 없다, or 모르다.

T3-0729.ex: 저는 결코 꿈을 포기하지 않을 거예요.
T3-0729.x: I will never give up on my dream.
T3-0729.t: 결코 sounds stronger and more formal than 절대; it almost always takes a negative.

T3-0730.x: Even though we don't have money, we're happy.

T3-0731.ex: 만약 내일 비가 오면 소풍을 취소할 거예요.
T3-0731.x: If it rains tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
T3-0731.e: The first syllable means 'ten thousand', hinting at a slim chance, like 만일.
T3-0731.t: 만약 only sets up the condition; the verb still needs -(으)면 or -는다면.

T3-0732.m: as if, as though, just like
T3-0732.x: That child talks just like an adult.
T3-0732.e: Not related to 마치다 'to finish'; it's a separate word.
T3-0732.t: 마치 almost always teams up with 처럼, 같다, or 듯이 later in the sentence.

T3-0733.forms: 오히려 + unexpected result: 오히려 더 좋아요
T3-0733.x: I took medicine, but instead I got even sicker.

T3-0734.forms: 차라리 -는 게 낫다 (would rather / might as well)
T3-0734.m: rather, would rather, might as well
T3-0734.ex: 이렇게 기다릴 바에는 차라리 걸어가는 게 나아요.
T3-0734.x: Rather than waiting like this, we might as well walk.
T3-0734.t: Choosing the lesser of two evils: 차라리 ... 낫다 means 'it'd be better to just ...'.

T3-0735.forms: 그대로 두다 (leave as is); 그대로이다 (be the same)
T3-0735.m: as it is, as is, just like that; unchanged
T3-0735.ex: 제 방은 어렸을 때 모습 그대로예요.
T3-0735.x: My room is just the way it was when I was little.

T3-0736.forms: 정확히 + verb: 정확히 말하다, 정확히 몰라요
T3-0736.x: What time exactly does the meeting start?
T3-0736.t: Pronounced [정화키]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0737.ex: 저는 집을 나올 때 분명히 문을 잠갔어요.
T3-0737.x: I definitely locked the door when I left the house.
T3-0737.e: Literally 'divided and bright', so clearly distinguished.

T3-0738.ex: 운동을 시작한 후에 확실히 더 건강해졌어요.
T3-0738.x: After I started exercising, I definitely got healthier.

T3-0739.forms: 솔직히 말하면 (to be honest); 솔직히 + opinion
T3-0739.x: To be honest, that movie wasn't great.
T3-0739.t: Pronounced [솔찌키]; 솔직히 말하면 is a very common opener for an honest opinion.

T3-0740.ex: 사진보다 실제로 보니까 훨씬 더 예뻐요.
T3-0740.x: It's much prettier in person than in the photos.

T3-0741.x: The fridge is full of food.

T3-0742.ex: 하루에 적어도 물을 여덟 잔 마시세요.
T3-0742.x: Drink at least eight glasses of water a day.
T3-0742.e: From 적다 'to be few' + -어도 'even if': even if it's few.

T3-0743.ex: 운동은 건강에 좋습니다. 그러므로 매일 운동해야 합니다.
T3-0743.x: Exercise is good for your health. Therefore, you should exercise every day.
T3-0743.e: 그러하다 'to be so' + -므로 'because': because it is so.
T3-0743.t: Mostly used in writing, speeches, and essays; in conversation, 그래서 sounds natural.

T3-0744.forms: A, 즉 B (A, that is, B)
T3-0744.m: that is, namely, in other words
T3-0744.ex: 제 동생의 딸, 즉 제 조카가 오늘 왔어요.
T3-0744.x: My younger sibling's daughter, that is, my niece, came today.

T3-0745.ex: 저는 과일을 좋아해요. 예를 들어 사과나 딸기요.
T3-0745.x: I like fruit. For example, apples or strawberries.
T3-0745.e: Literally 'raising an example', from 들다 'to lift, to raise'.

T3-0746.m: the other side; whereas, on the other hand
T3-0746.ex: 이 집은 넓은 반면 교통이 불편해요.
T3-0746.x: This house is spacious, but on the other hand, transportation is inconvenient.
T3-0746.t: Attach it to a modifier to contrast two facts: -(으)ㄴ/는 반면(에).

T3-0747.forms: Sentence start: 반면에 ...; after a verb: -는 반면에
T3-0747.m: on the other hand, whereas, in contrast
T3-0747.ex: 형은 조용해요. 반면에 동생은 아주 활발해요.
T3-0747.x: The older brother is quiet. On the other hand, the younger one is very lively.

T3-0748.forms: 한편이 · 한편을; 한편(으로는) (meanwhile, on the other hand)
T3-0748.m: one side; meanwhile, on the other hand
T3-0748.ex: 서울은 맑습니다. 한편 부산에는 비가 내리고 있습니다.
T3-0748.x: It's clear in Seoul. Meanwhile, it's raining in Busan.
T3-0748.e: 한 'one' + 편 'side': one side, then the other.
T3-0748.t: News anchors use 한편 to switch topics, like 'Meanwhile, ...' in English.

T3-0749.ex: 그 식당은 맛있을 뿐만 아니라 값도 싸요.
T3-0749.x: That restaurant is not only tasty but also cheap.
T3-0749.e: 뿐 'only' + 만 'just' + 아니라 'it is not': it's not just that.

T3-0750.ex: 시간이 없으니까 아무튼 내일 다시 이야기해요.
T3-0750.x: We're out of time, so anyway, let's talk again tomorrow.
T3-0750.e: Probably shortened from 아무러하든 'however it may be'.

T3-0751.m: anyway, in any case, at any rate
T3-0751.ex: 길이 막혀서 늦었지만 어쨌든 도착해서 다행이에요.
T3-0751.x: Traffic made us late, but anyway, I'm glad we arrived.
T3-0751.e: Short for 어찌했든 'however it was done'.

T3-0752.m: to point at, to point to; to indicate, to refer to
T3-0752.x: The child pointed at the sky with a tiny finger.
T3-0752.t: Don't confuse 가리키다 'to point' with 가르치다 'to teach'; even natives mix them up.

T3-0753.m: to have, to possess, to be equipped with; to prepare
T3-0753.ex: 이 호텔은 좋은 시설을 갖추고 있어요.
T3-0753.e: Probably related to 갖다 'to have': having everything needed in place.
T3-0753.t: Common collocations: 자격을 갖추다 'to be qualified', 시설을 갖추다 'to be equipped'.

T3-0754.m: to hide, to conceal, to keep secret
T3-0754.ex: 동생이 제 과자를 침대 밑에 숨겼어요.
T3-0754.x: My younger sibling hid my snacks under the bed.
T3-0754.e: Causative of 숨다 'to hide (oneself)': to make something hide.

T3-0755.m: to go through, to experience, to suffer
T3-0755.ex: 유학 생활 동안 많은 어려움을 겪었어요.
T3-0755.x: I went through a lot of hardships while studying abroad.
T3-0755.t: Usually used for difficulties: 어려움을 겪다, 고생을 겪다; for fun experiences, use 경험하다.

T3-0756.m: to endure, to bear, to stand, to withstand
T3-0756.x: It's so hard to endure the summer heat.
T3-0756.t: 참다 is holding back a feeling or urge; 견디다 is lasting through a hard situation over time.

T3-0757.m: to manage, to take care of, to maintain
T3-0757.x: I exercise every day to take good care of my health.
T3-0757.t: Pronounced [괄리하다]: ㄴ next to ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T3-0758.m: to distinguish, to tell apart; to divide, to classify
T3-0758.x: They're twins, so it's hard to tell the two apart.

T3-0759.m: to record, to write down, to document
T3-0759.ex: 저는 매일 일기에 하루 일을 기록해요.
T3-0759.x: I record what happened each day in my diary.
T3-0759.t: Pronounced [기로카다]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0760.ex: 그 선수가 마라톤에서 새로운 기록을 세웠어요.
T3-0760.x: That athlete set a new record in the marathon.

T3-0761.m: to show, to express, to represent, to indicate
T3-0761.x: This graph shows the change in population.
T3-0761.e: From 나타나다 'to appear': to make something appear.

T3-0762.m: to increase, to expand, to extend
T3-0762.x: The company increased its number of employees this year.
T3-0762.e: Causative of 늘다 'to grow, to increase': to make something grow.
T3-0762.t: Don't confuse it with 늘이다, which means to physically stretch something longer.

T3-0763.m: to reduce, to cut down, to decrease; to shorten
T3-0763.x: I'm cutting down on sugar for my health.
T3-0763.e: Causative of 줄다 'to decrease': to make something decrease.

T3-0764.m: to treat (someone), to deal with; to face
T3-0764.x: That teacher treats the students kindly.
T3-0764.e: Literally 'to face'; treating someone is how you face them.
T3-0764.t: N에 대해(서) means 'about N': 한국 문화에 대해 알고 싶어요.

T3-0765.m: to turn, to spin, to rotate; to hand out; to run (a machine)
T3-0765.ex: 주말 아침에 세탁기를 돌리고 청소를 했어요.
T3-0765.x: On the weekend morning, I ran the washing machine and cleaned up.
T3-0765.e: Causative of 돌다 'to turn': to make something turn.

T3-0766.m: to fit, to adjust, to match; to set (an alarm); to put together
T3-0766.x: I set an alarm so I can get up early tomorrow.
T3-0766.e: Related to 맞다 'to fit, to be right': to make things fit.
T3-0766.t: For guessing a correct answer, standard Korean uses 맞히다: 정답을 맞히다.

T3-0767.forms: 머물러요 · 머물렀어요 · 머무를 거예요 · 머무르세요 (르 irregular)
T3-0767.ex: 여행 중에 작은 호텔에 일주일 동안 머물렀어요.
T3-0767.x: During the trip, I stayed at a small hotel for a week.
T3-0767.t: The short form 머물다 is just as common: 머물 거예요, 머물고 있어요.

T3-0768.m: to tie, to bind, to tie up
T3-0768.x: My hair is long, so I always tie it back.
T3-0768.t: 묶다 and 묵다 'to stay at lodging' sound identical, [묵따]; spelling and context tell them apart.

T3-0769.m: to look at, to gaze at; to view
T3-0769.x: We drank coffee while gazing at the ocean.
T3-0769.e: Probably 바라- 'toward, hoping' + 보다 'to see': to look toward.
rel: to look up at, to stare

T3-0770.ex: 새 단어를 여러 번 반복해서 외웠어요.
T3-0770.x: I memorized the new words by repeating them many times.
T3-0770.t: Pronounced [반보카다]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0771.x: Scientists discovered a new star in space.
T3-0771.t: 발견하다 is finding what already exists; 발명하다 is inventing something new.

T3-0772.x: This medicine was made through an accidental discovery.

T3-0773.m: to reveal, to make clear, to disclose; to light up
T3-0773.x: The police revealed the cause of the accident today.
T3-0773.e: Causative of 밝다 'to be bright': to bring something to light.
T3-0773.t: Pronounced [발키다]; very common in news: 원인을 밝히다 'to reveal the cause'.

T3-0774.m: to keep, to store, to look after
T3-0774.x: Be sure to keep the leftovers in the refrigerator.

T3-0775.m: to bump into, to crash into, to collide; to face (a problem)
T3-0775.x: I bumped into someone while looking at my phone on the street.
T3-0775.t: 부딪치다 means actively bumping into something; 부딪히다 means getting hit by something.
rel: to get bumped, to be hit

T3-0776.m: to empty, to clear; to leave (a place) vacant
T3-0776.ex: 이사하기 전에 방을 모두 비워야 해요.
T3-0776.x: I have to clear out the whole room before moving.
T3-0776.e: Causative of 비다 'to be empty': to make something empty.
rel: to step away from one's seat

T3-0777.m: to look over, to examine, to check carefully
T3-0777.x: Look over the contract carefully, then sign it.
T3-0777.e: 살피다 'to observe' + 보다 'to look': to look carefully.

T3-0778.m: to go bad, to spoil; to be hurt, to be damaged
T3-0778.x: The milk has gone bad, so it smells strange.
T3-0778.e: Literally 'to be harmed': food gets spoiled, feelings get hurt.
T3-0778.t: With feelings, 기분이 상했어요 means 'My feelings were hurt.'

T3-0779.m: to be fooled, to be deceived, to be tricked
T3-0779.ex: 인터넷 광고에 속아서 비싼 물건을 샀어요.
T3-0779.x: I was fooled by an internet ad and bought something expensive.
T3-0779.e: Its causative is 속이다 'to deceive': 속다 is being on the receiving end.
T3-0779.t: The request form is naturally negative: 속지 마세요 'Don't be fooled.'

T3-0780.m: to pile up, to be stacked, to accumulate
T3-0780.ex: 밤새 눈이 내려서 길에 많이 쌓였어요.
T3-0780.x: It snowed all night, so a lot piled up on the roads.
T3-0780.e: Passive of 쌓다 'to pile, to stack'.
T3-0780.t: Pronounced [싸이다]: the ㅎ is silent; common in 스트레스가 쌓이다 'stress builds up'.

T3-0781.m: to get rid of, to remove, to eliminate
T3-0781.x: I want to get rid of the bad smell in the room.
T3-0781.e: Built from 없다 'to not exist' plus a causative ending: literally 'make it not exist'.

T3-0782.m: to regard, to consider, to think of (as)
T3-0782.x: I think of that friend as family.
T3-0782.e: Unrelated to 여기 'here', despite the identical spelling of the stem.
T3-0782.t: Common patterns: N을/를 N(으)로 여기다 and A-게 여기다, as in 소중하게 여기다 'to treasure'.

T3-0783.x: I connected the computer to the internet.

T3-0784.m: to be connected, to be linked; to get through (on the phone)
T3-0784.x: The phone isn't getting through right now.
T3-0784.t: Spell the contraction 됐어요 (from 되었어요), never 됬어요.

T3-0785.x: Please hand in your homework by Friday.
T3-0785.e: Literally 'hold up and put out': you hand something in.

T3-0786.x: The deadline for submitting the report is tomorrow afternoon.

T3-0787.m: to fill, to fill up; to make up (a shortfall)
T3-0787.x: I filled the cup all the way with water.
T3-0787.e: Causative of 차다 'to be full': literally 'make it full'.
T3-0787.t: Its opposite is 비우다 'to empty': 잔을 비우다 'to empty one's glass'.

T3-0788.m: to go through, to pass; to get along, to communicate; to be understood
T3-0788.ex: 저는 그 친구와 말이 잘 통해요.
T3-0788.x: That friend and I really get each other.
T3-0788.e: Literally 'pass through': roads, air, and even ideas.
T3-0788.t: N을/를 통해(서) means 'through, via': 인터넷을 통해 알았어요 'I found out through the internet.'

T3-0789.m: to decorate; to dress up; to make up (a story)
T3-0789.x: We decorated the house nicely for Christmas.
T3-0789.e: Also means 'to fabricate': 꾸민 이야기 is a made-up story.

T3-0790.m: to argue, to quarrel; to compete (for)
T3-0790.x: Yesterday I argued with my little brother over a toy.
T3-0790.e: The noun is 다툼 'quarrel', made with the -ㅁ ending.
T3-0790.t: 다투다 sounds milder and more formal than 싸우다 and usually means a verbal argument.

T3-0791.ex: 그 학생은 수학 실력이 정말 뛰어나요.
T3-0791.x: That student is really outstanding at math.
T3-0791.e: Built from 뛰다 'to jump' + 나다 'to come out': someone who jumps out ahead.

T3-0792.m: to break, to get broken, to be ruined
T3-0792.x: My phone fell on the floor and broke.
T3-0792.e: Its transitive partner is 망가뜨리다 'to break something'.
T3-0792.t: 고장 나다 is mainly for machines; 망가지다 also works for toys, plans, or even health.

T3-0793.m: to stop, to halt, to come to a stop
T3-0793.x: Suddenly the bus stopped in the middle of the road.
T3-0793.e: The noun 멈춤 'stop' appears on signs and video players.

T3-0794.m: to pull; to move up (a date); to crave (food)
T3-0794.x: Don't push this door; pull it.
T3-0794.e: Opposite of 밀다 'to push': door signs read 미세요 and 당기세요.
T3-0794.t: With food it means 'crave': 오늘은 매운 음식이 당겨요 'I'm craving something spicy today.'

T3-0795.m: to change, to be changed; to be switched
T3-0795.x: My life changed a lot after I moved.
T3-0795.e: Passive of 바꾸다 'to change, to exchange'.
T3-0795.t: You'll hear 바꼈어요 in speech, but the standard spelling is 바뀌었어요.

T3-0796.m: to pull out; to pick, to choose, to elect; to hire
T3-0796.x: My classmates chose me as class president.
T3-0796.e: Covers pulling out teeth or weeds and picking people, like drawing a name from a hat.
T3-0796.t: Pronounced [뽑따] — the ㄷ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T3-0797.m: to order (food); to make someone do, to tell someone to do
T3-0797.x: I was hungry, so I ordered chicken.
T3-0797.t: At restaurants 시키다 is the everyday word for 주문하다 'to order'; with people it means 'to make someone do'.

T3-0798.x: Write the appropriate word in the blank.
T3-0798.e: Contains 맞다 'to fit, to be right': think 'fits just right'.
T3-0798.t: It's an adjective, so the modifier is 알맞은, not 알맞는 — a very common mistake.

T3-0799.ex: 밖이 시끄러워서 공부에 집중할 수 없어요.
T3-0799.x: It's noisy outside, so I can't concentrate on studying.

T3-0800.ex: 저를 포함해서 모두 다섯 명이 왔어요.
T3-0800.x: Five people came in total, including me.

T3-0801.m: to be confused, to mix up, to be confusing
T3-0801.ex: 이 두 단어는 너무 비슷해서 헷갈려요.
T3-0801.x: These two words are so similar that I mix them up.
T3-0801.e: Both spellings 헷갈리다 and 헛갈리다 are standard.

T3-0802.x: You can pay by card at this restaurant.
T3-0802.t: 가능한 한 빨리 means 'as soon as possible'.

T3-0803.ex: 혼자서 이 일을 하루에 끝내는 것은 불가능해요.
T3-0803.x: It's impossible to finish this work in one day by yourself.
T3-0803.e: 불- = 'not', a prefix you'll reuse often: 불편, 불안, 불가능.
T3-0803.t: Before ㄷ or ㅈ this prefix becomes 부-, as in 부족 'lack' and 부당 'unfair'.

T3-0804.m: awkward, difficult, in a tough spot
T3-0804.x: That question is a bit hard for me to answer.
T3-0804.t: Pronounced [골란하다]; 그건 좀 곤란해요 is a soft, polite way to say no.

T3-0805.ex: 이 강은 얕아서 아이들도 놀 수 있어요.
T3-0805.x: This river is shallow, so even kids can play in it.

T3-0806.x: That person's memory is truly amazing.
T3-0806.e: Adjective made from 놀라다 'to be surprised', like 즐겁다 from 즐기다.
T3-0806.t: 놀라다 is how you feel ('I'm surprised'); 놀랍다 describes the thing that surprises you.

T3-0807.x: You studied hard, so of course you passed.
T3-0807.e: Literally 'properly so': just as it should be.
T3-0807.t: 당연하죠! is a friendly 'Of course!'; the adverb is 당연히.

T3-0808.ex: 혼자서 그 일을 다 하다니 정말 대단해요.
T3-0808.x: It's really impressive that you did all that by yourself.
T3-0808.t: 대단해요! is a common compliment when someone achieves something hard.

T3-0809.ex: 요즘은 손으로 편지를 쓰는 사람이 드물어요.
T3-0809.x: These days, people who write letters by hand are rare.

T3-0810.ex: 김 씨는 한국에서 아주 흔한 성이에요.
T3-0810.x: Kim is a very common family name in Korea.

T3-0811.x: Exercising every day is a desirable habit.
T3-0811.e: From 바라다 'to wish': literally 'worth wishing for'.

T3-0812.x: This fruit is rich in vitamins.

T3-0813.ex: 그 사람이 거짓말을 한 것이 분명해요.
T3-0813.e: Literally 'divided and bright': so distinct you can't mistake it.
T3-0813.t: 분명히 means 'clearly, surely': 분명히 말했어요 'I clearly told you.'

T3-0814.ex: 환경 오염 문제가 점점 심각해지고 있어요.
T3-0814.x: The problem of pollution is getting more and more serious.
T3-0814.e: Literally 'deeply carved': a matter that cuts deep.
T3-0814.t: Use 심각하다 for situations; for a serious, earnest person, say 진지하다.

T3-0815.x: What the teacher said is right.
T3-0815.t: Pronounced [올타]; in 옳아요 [오라요] the ㅎ goes silent.

T3-0816.x: His Korean pronunciation is almost perfect.
T3-0816.e: Literally 'a complete jade disc', from a Chinese story about returning a jade disc unbroken.

T3-0817.x: Please explain the directions in detail.
T3-0817.e: Literally 'careful and fine': down to the small details.
T3-0817.t: The adverb 자세히 is very common: 자세히 보세요 'look closely'.

T3-0818.ex: 상황에 적절한 말을 하는 것이 중요해요.
T3-0818.x: It's important to say what fits the situation.
T3-0818.t: 적절하다 means exactly appropriate; 적당하다 leans toward 'moderate, about right'.

T3-0819.x: I'm just an ordinary office worker.

T3-0820.x: The country village is quiet and peaceful.
T3-0820.e: -롭다 turns nouns into adjectives: 평화롭다, 자유롭다, 지혜롭다.

T3-0822.ex: 이 의자는 나무로 만들어서 아주 단단해요.
T3-0822.x: This chair is made of wood, so it's very sturdy.
T3-0822.e: A doubled-syllable word, like many Korean texture words.
T3-0822.t: 단단하다 is usually positive (solid, firm); 딱딱하다 often sounds negative (hard, stiff).

T3-0823.m: hard, stiff; formal, rigid (mood or tone)
T3-0823.x: The bread got hard because it's old.
T3-0823.e: Also describes a stiff, formal mood: 딱딱한 분위기.

T3-0824.x: I changed my eating habits for my health.

T3-0825.x: I bought milk in the grocery section of the supermarket.
T3-0825.t: 식품 is food as a product (labels, stores); 음식 is food you cook and eat.

T3-0826.x: I found a kimchi stew recipe online.

T3-0827.m: kimjang, making kimchi for the winter
T3-0827.x: In November my family gets together to make kimchi for the winter.
T3-0827.e: A late-fall tradition of making a winter's supply of kimchi together; UNESCO-listed in 2013.

T3-0828.ex: 패스트푸드를 너무 자주 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
T3-0828.x: Eating fast food too often isn't good for your health.
T3-0828.e: From English 'fast food'; Korean has no f sound, so f becomes ㅍ.

T3-0829.x: I have no appetite these days because of stress.
T3-0829.t: 식욕 is a bit formal; in daily talk people say 입맛이 없어요.

T3-0830.x: I have a cold, so I have no appetite.

T3-0831.forms: N이/가 입에 맞아요 · 입에 안 맞아요 · 입에 맞으세요?
T3-0831.m: to suit one's taste, to be to one's liking
T3-0831.t: Hosts politely ask guests 입에 맞으세요? 'Is the food to your liking?'

T3-0832.x: This soup isn't spicy; it's light and clean-tasting.
T3-0832.e: Literally 'light and plain': a compliment, unlike English 'bland'.
T3-0832.t: 담백하다 is praise; if food needs more salt, say 싱겁다.

T3-0833.m: greasy, oily, too rich; cheesy, sleazy (person)
T3-0833.ex: 피자를 많이 먹었더니 속이 좀 느끼해요.
T3-0833.x: I ate a lot of pizza, and now my stomach feels a bit greasy.
T3-0833.t: Also slang for a cheesy, sleazy person or line: 느끼한 말.

T3-0834.x: I bought fresh vegetables at the market.
T3-0834.t: 신선하다 also praises ideas: 신선한 아이디어 'a fresh idea'.

T3-0835.x: The milk's expiration date was yesterday.
T3-0835.e: Literally 'circulation period limit': how long it may be sold.
T3-0835.t: Often written 유통기한; since 2023 Korean labels mostly show 소비 기한 'use-by date' instead.

T3-0836.ex: 제 친구는 고기를 안 먹고 채식을 해요.
T3-0836.x: My friend doesn't eat meat; she's vegetarian.

T3-0837.m: to suppose, to assume, to hypothesize
T3-0837.ex: 내일 비가 온다고 가정하고 계획을 세웠어요.
T3-0837.x: We made plans assuming it will rain tomorrow.
T3-0837.e: Literally 'fix a supposition': set up a what-if.
T3-0837.t: Don't confuse it with 가정 'home, household', a different word with the same sound.

T3-0838.x: My parents meddle way too much.

T3-0839.x: Please don't meddle in my business.
T3-0839.t: It takes 에: N에 간섭하다; casual synonym 참견하다.

T3-0840.x: The teacher stressed pronunciation several times.

T3-0842.x: The company decided to improve working conditions.

T3-0843.m: to deal, to trade, to do business
T3-0843.ex: 저희 회사는 그 회사와 10년 동안 거래했어요.
T3-0843.x: Our company has done business with that company for ten years.
T3-0843.e: Literally 'go and come': goods and money moving back and forth.

T3-0844.m: to review, to examine, to look over

T3-0845.x: After a long meeting, we reached a conclusion.
T3-0845.t: Pronounced [결론]; to reach a conclusion is 결론을 내리다.

T3-0846.ex: 빨간 불에 길을 건너서 경찰에게 경고를 받았어요.
T3-0846.x: I crossed on a red light and got a warning from the police.

T3-0847.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들은 결혼을 늦게 하는 경향이 있어요.
T3-0847.x: Young people these days tend to marry late.

T3-0848.x: I went through a lot of trouble moving.
T3-0848.t: 고생 많으셨어요 thanks someone for their hard work; 고생하다 is the verb.

T3-0849.ex: 그 노래 가사에 많은 사람들이 공감을 느꼈어요.
T3-0849.x: Many people related to the lyrics of that song.

T3-0850.m: to empathize, to relate to; to agree
T3-0850.x: I agree with that opinion too.
T3-0850.t: It takes 에: N에 공감하다 'to relate to N'.

T3-0851.m: to make public, to reveal, to release
T3-0851.ex: 그 가수가 새 노래를 처음 공개했어요.
T3-0851.x: The singer revealed a new song for the first time.

T3-0852.ex: 두 사람은 음악이라는 공통 관심사가 있어요.
T3-0852.x: The two of them share an interest in music.

T3-0853.x: Observing insects is a fun way for kids to learn.

T3-0854.x: The children observed the ants closely.

T3-0855.ex: 이 책은 내용 구성이 아주 좋아요.
T3-0855.x: This book's content is very well structured.

T3-0856.m: to consist of, to be made up of, to be composed of
T3-0856.ex: 우리 팀은 다섯 명으로 구성되어 있어요.
T3-0856.x: Our team is made up of five people.
T3-0856.t: Pattern: N(으)로 구성되어 있다 'to consist of N'.

T3-0857.x: He contributed greatly to the company's growth.
T3-0857.t: It takes 에: N에 기여하다 'to contribute to N'.

T3-0858.x: My childhood memories are still vivid.
T3-0858.t: 기억이 나다 means 'to come to mind'; 기억하다 is 'to remember' actively.

T3-0859.m: to plan, to organize (a project or event)
T3-0859.t: 기획 is used for projects, events and products at work; for personal plans, use 계획.

T3-0860.x: In an emergency, call 119 right away.

T3-0861.ex: 이번 사고에 대한 정부의 대응이 너무 늦었습니다.
T3-0861.x: The government's response to this accident was too slow.

T3-0862.m: to respond (to), to deal with, to cope with
T3-0862.x: The company responded quickly to customer complaints.
T3-0862.e: Literally 'face and respond' — meet a situation head-on.
T3-0862.t: Pattern: N에 대응하다 'to respond to N', used for problems, crises and changes.

T3-0863.ex: 두 사람의 성격은 뚜렷한 대조를 이뤄요.
T3-0863.x: The two people's personalities form a clear contrast.
T3-0863.e: Literally 'hold side by side and compare'.

T3-0864.x: Kimchi is a food that represents Korea.

T3-0865.m: introduction (of a system or technology), adoption
T3-0865.ex: 새 제도의 도입으로 많은 것이 바뀌었어요.
T3-0865.x: A lot changed with the introduction of the new system.
T3-0865.t: 도입 is for introducing systems or technology; for introducing people, use 소개.

T3-0866.m: to introduce, to adopt, to bring in (a system or technology)
T3-0866.x: Our company introduced working from home this year.

T3-0867.x: Life changed a lot with the arrival of smartphones.

T3-0868.m: to appear, to make an entrance, to emerge
T3-0868.ex: 이 영화에는 유명한 배우가 많이 등장해요.
T3-0868.x: Lots of famous actors appear in this movie.

T3-0869.m: preparation, arrangement (of money, a home, etc.); being bound to (in -기 마련이다)
T3-0869.ex: 결혼 전에 집 마련이 가장 큰 고민이에요.
T3-0869.x: Getting a place to live is the biggest worry before marriage.
T3-0869.e: A native Korean word; mostly used as 마련하다 'to prepare, to arrange'.
T3-0869.t: -기 마련이다 means 'is bound to': 시간이 지나면 잊기 마련이에요.

T3-0870.forms: 매력이 있어요 · 매력이 있었어요 · 매력이 있는 (+noun)
T3-0870.m: to be attractive, to be charming, to have appeal
T3-0870.ex: 이 도시는 오래된 골목이 많아서 매력이 있어요.
T3-0870.x: This city is charming because it has lots of old alleys.

T3-0871.x: Soldiers must follow their superior's orders.
T3-0871.t: Pronounced [명녕] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-0872.m: to ignore, to disregard; to look down on
T3-0872.e: Literally 'not look' — act as if you don't see it.
T3-0872.t: It also means 'to look down on someone': 어리다고 무시하면 안 돼요.

T3-0873.m: to describe, to depict, to portray
T3-0873.x: The writer described the scenery of his hometown beautifully.
T3-0873.e: Literally 'draw and copy' — paint a picture in words.

T3-0874.x: The audience's reaction was very good.
T3-0874.t: Pronounced [바능]: the ㄴ moves over to the next syllable.

T3-0875.x: The baby reacted right away to its mom's voice.
T3-0875.t: 반응하다 is a natural reaction; 대응하다 is deliberately dealing with a problem.

T3-0876.x: The construction noise is getting in the way of my studying.

T3-0877.m: to disturb, to interrupt, to get in the way of
T3-0877.x: My little brother keeps disturbing my studying.
T3-0877.t: 방해하지 마세요 is the common phrase for 'Do not disturb.'

T3-0878.m: to be changed, to be modified
T3-0878.x: The meeting time has been changed to 3 p.m.
T3-0878.t: 변경되다 is formal, typical of notices; in everyday speech, 바뀌다 is more common.

T3-0879.m: to guarantee, to ensure, to secure
T3-0879.x: The company must guarantee its employees' safety.

T3-0880.m: to supplement, to make up for, to fill in
T3-0880.x: I make up for missing vitamins with fruit.

T3-0881.x: With the exam coming up, I feel a lot of pressure.
T3-0881.e: Literally 'bear on the back and shoulder'.

T3-0882.m: to be burdensome, to feel pressured, to feel like too much
T3-0882.x: An expensive gift feels like a bit much.
T3-0882.e: 부담 'burden' plus -스럽다 'feeling like': it feels like a burden.
T3-0882.t: Koreans also use it for too much attention or kindness, like a stare or a pushy friend.

T3-0883.m: to classify, to sort, to categorize
T3-0883.x: Sort your trash by type before throwing it out.
T3-0883.t: Pronounced [불류하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-0884.x: This café has a quiet, nice atmosphere.
T3-0884.t: Useful phrases: 분위기 있다 'to be atmospheric' and 분위기를 깨다 'to kill the mood'.

T3-0885.x: Complaints from customers kept coming in.
T3-0885.e: Literally 'not even' — things feel unfair or off balance.

T3-0886.x: He always complains that the food doesn't taste good.
T3-0886.e: Literally 'not even' — things feel unfair or off balance.

T3-0887.x: That policy received a lot of criticism.
T3-0887.t: 비판 is reasoned criticism; 비난 is blame or condemnation and sounds more emotional.

T3-0888.x: The newspaper strongly criticized the government's decision.

T3-0889.x: Please refrain from using your phone in the library.
T3-0889.t: 사용 is for tools and things; 이용 is for services and facilities like the subway.

T3-0890.x: Please tell me how to use this machine.
T3-0890.e: -법 = way or method of doing it: 사용법, 요리법, 공부법.
T3-0890.t: Pronounced [사용뻡] — the ㅂ of 법 is tensed here.

T3-0891.m: to be produced, to be manufactured
T3-0891.x: This car is produced in Korea.

T3-0892.x: This year's player selection was carried out fairly.
T3-0892.t: 선발 is for selecting people such as players or students; for things, use 선택.

T3-0893.ex: 오랜 설득 끝에 부모님이 유학을 허락하셨어요.
T3-0893.x: After a long effort to persuade them, my parents allowed me to study abroad.
T3-0893.e: Literally 'speak and gain' — win someone over with words.

T3-0894.x: I persuaded my friend, and we went on a trip together.
T3-0894.e: Literally 'speak and gain' — win someone over with words.
T3-0894.t: Pronounced [설뜨카다] — ㄷ after ㄹ tenses in Sino-Korean 설득 [설뜩], and ㄱ + ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-0895.ex: 휴대폰 설정에서 언어를 바꿀 수 있어요.
T3-0895.x: You can change the language in your phone's settings.
T3-0895.t: Pronounced [설쩡]; also common in 목표 설정 'goal setting'.

T3-0896.m: to be introduced, to be featured
T3-0896.ex: 이 식당은 텔레비전에 여러 번 소개되었어요.
T3-0896.x: This restaurant has been featured on TV several times.

T3-0897.x: This building is owned by the city.

T3-0899.ex: 이 앱은 사용자의 개인 정보를 수집하지 않습니다.
T3-0899.x: This app does not collect users' personal information.

T3-0900.m: to acquire, to learn (a skill or knowledge)
T3-0900.x: Children acquire languages faster than adults.
T3-0900.t: A homonym 습득 means 'picking up a lost item', as in 습득물 'found property'.

T3-0901.ex: 첫 번째 시도는 실패했지만 포기하지 않았어요.
T3-0901.x: The first attempt failed, but I didn't give up.

T3-0902.x: I tried a new dish over the weekend.

T3-0903.m: to carry out, to conduct, to implement
T3-0903.ex: 학교에서 다음 주에 건강 검사를 실시합니다.
T3-0903.x: The school will conduct health checkups next week.
T3-0903.t: Formal; common in news and notices, e.g. 조사를 실시하다 'to conduct a survey'.

T3-0904.m: to get worse, to worsen, to deteriorate
T3-0904.x: My cold got worse as the weather turned cold.
T3-0904.t: Formal; in everyday speech, 나빠지다 is more natural. Pronounced [아콰되다].

T3-0905.m: stability, security (of a job, prices, etc.)
T3-0905.ex: 요즘은 직업의 안정을 가장 중요하게 생각하는 사람이 많아요.
T3-0905.x: These days many people consider job stability the most important thing.
T3-0905.t: A homonym 안정 (different hanja) means 'rest, calm', as in 절대 안정 'complete bed rest'.

T3-0906.m: to become stable, to settle down, to stabilize
T3-0906.x: Prices have stabilized a little lately.

T3-0907.ex: 그는 회사에서 많은 압력을 받고 있어요.
T3-0907.x: He is under a lot of pressure at work.
T3-0907.t: Pronounced [암녁] — nasalization turns ㅂ + ㄹ into ㅁ + ㄴ.

T3-0908.x: My older brother works at a science research institute.
T3-0908.e: -소 = a place for it: 연구소, 사무소, 주유소.

T3-0909.ex: 이 그림은 완성까지 일 년이 걸렸어요.
T3-0909.x: This painting took a year to complete.

T3-0910.x: I finally finished my graduation project.
T3-0910.t: 완성하다 is for finishing a product or work; for finishing a task, 끝내다 is more natural.

T3-0911.ex: 이 글의 내용을 세 줄로 요약해 보세요.
T3-0911.x: Try summarizing this text in three lines.

T3-0912.ex: 물가 상승에 대한 우려가 커지고 있습니다.
T3-0912.x: Concerns about rising prices are growing.
T3-0912.t: 우려 is formal and typical of the news; in daily conversation, use 걱정.

T3-0913.m: operation, management, running (of a business or facility)
T3-0913.x: The library's operating hours are until 6 p.m.
T3-0913.e: Literally 'move and manage' — keep something running.

T3-0914.m: to run, to operate, to manage
T3-0914.x: My parents run a small restaurant.
T3-0914.e: Literally 'move and manage' — keep something running.

T3-0915.ex: 환경 오염은 건강에 큰 위협이 됩니다.
T3-0915.x: Environmental pollution is a major threat to health.

T3-0916.x: I exercise every day to stay healthy.
T3-0916.e: Literally 'tie and hold' — keep things as they are.

T3-0917.x: Keep the indoor temperature at 20 degrees.
T3-0917.e: Literally 'tie and hold' — keep things as they are.

T3-0918.ex: 스마트폰에 대한 의존이 점점 심해지고 있어요.
T3-0918.x: Dependence on smartphones is getting more and more serious.

T3-0919.ex: 출퇴근 시간에는 지하철 이동이 정말 힘들어요.
T3-0919.x: Getting around by subway during rush hour is really hard.

T3-0920.m: to move, to go (to another place)
T3-0920.x: For the next class, please move to the third-floor classroom.
T3-0920.t: 이동하다 means changing location; for moving to a new home, use 이사하다.

T3-0921.x: That athlete's skill was recognized worldwide.
T3-0921.t: A homonym 인정 means 'warmth, kindness', as in 인정이 많다 'kind-hearted'.

T3-0922.x: I withdrew cash at the bank.
T3-0922.t: 현금 인출기 means 'ATM'; the opposite action is 입금하다 'to deposit'.

T3-0923.m: to input, to enter (data), to type in
T3-0923.e: Literally 'put in force'; think 'put in', the opposite of 출력 'output'.
T3-0923.t: Pronounced [임녀카다] — nasalization, plus ㄱ + ㅎ becoming ㅋ.

T3-0924.ex: 친구의 성공이 저에게 좋은 자극이 됐어요.
T3-0924.x: My friend's success was a good motivation for me.
T3-0924.e: Literally 'pierce with a spear' — something that pokes you into action.
T3-0924.t: 자극적인 음식 means very spicy or salty food.

T3-0925.t: 부작용 'side effect' is a very common word built on 작용.

T3-0926.m: to apply (a rule, method or knowledge)
T3-0926.ex: 배운 내용을 실제 생활에 적용해 보세요.
T3-0926.x: Try applying what you learned to real life.
T3-0926.t: For applying to a job or school, use 지원하다, not 적용하다.

T3-0927.x: This field has a bright outlook going forward.
T3-0927.e: Literally 'unfold and gaze' — look far ahead.
T3-0927.t: It can also mean a literal view: 전망이 좋은 방 'a room with a nice view'.

T3-0928.x: Taking a walk is good for refreshing your mood.
T3-0928.t: 기분 전환 'a change of pace, refreshing yourself' is the most common collocation.

T3-0929.ex: 엘리베이터 점검 때문에 계단을 이용해 주세요.
T3-0929.x: Due to elevator inspection, please use the stairs.
T3-0929.e: Literally 'tick off and examine' — check item by item.

T3-0930.x: I checked the car carefully before the trip.
T3-0930.e: Literally 'tick off and examine' — check item by item.
T3-0930.t: 점검하다 is checking for problems in machines or systems; 확인하다 is just confirming a fact.

T3-0931.x: Look up the definition of this word in the dictionary.
T3-0931.t: A homonym 정의 means 'justice', as in 정의로운 사회 'a just society'.

T3-0932.x: This movie took three years to make.

T3-0933.m: to produce, to make (a film, program or product)
T3-0933.x: The students made a short film themselves.

T3-0934.m: to adjust, to control, to regulate (amount or level)
T3-0934.x: Please adjust the air conditioner temperature.
T3-0934.t: 조절 is for amounts or levels like temperature or volume; 조정 is for plans, schedules or positions.

T3-0935.m: to adjust, to coordinate, to rearrange
T3-0935.x: We rescheduled the meeting to next week.

T3-0936.ex: 그 배우는 잠깐 나와도 존재감이 커요.
T3-0936.x: That actor has a strong presence even when he appears only briefly.
T3-0936.e: -감 = a sense or feeling of it: 존재감, 책임감, 자신감.

T3-0937.ex: 그 배우는 요즘 많은 주목을 받고 있어요.
T3-0937.x: That actor is getting a lot of attention these days.
T3-0937.t: Common pairs: 주목을 받다 (to get attention) and 주목을 끌다 (to draw attention).

T3-0938.m: to pay attention to, to watch closely
T3-0938.ex: 전문가들은 이 회사의 성장에 주목하고 있어요.
T3-0938.x: Experts are closely watching this company's growth.
T3-0938.t: Pronounced [주모카다] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes an aspirated ㅋ sound.

T3-0939.m: to stop, to halt, to suspend
T3-0939.x: It rained a lot, so they stopped the game.

T3-0940.ex: 그는 자신이 범인이 아니라는 것을 증명했어요.
T3-0940.x: He proved that he wasn't the culprit.
T3-0940.t: 증명서 means certificate, as in 재학 증명서 (proof of enrollment).

T3-0941.x: My teacher pointed out the problems in my presentation.
T3-0941.e: Literally 'point at and pick out' a flaw.
T3-0941.t: Don't confuse it with the different word 지적 meaning 'intellectual,' as in 지적인 사람.

T3-0942.m: to continue, to last, to be sustained
T3-0942.ex: 더운 날씨가 다음 주까지 지속될 거예요.
T3-0942.x: The hot weather will continue until next week.
T3-0942.t: Pronounced [지속뙤다] — ㄷ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T3-0943.x: The employees worked according to the boss's instructions.
T3-0943.e: Literally 'point and show' what to do.

T3-0944.m: advance, entry (into a market or field); advancing (to the next round)
T3-0944.ex: 그 회사는 해외 시장 진출을 준비하고 있어요.
T3-0944.x: That company is preparing to enter overseas markets.
T3-0944.e: Literally 'advance out' into a new area.
T3-0944.t: Common collocations: 해외 진출 (expanding overseas) and 결승 진출 (reaching the finals).

T3-0945.ex: 이 자료가 숙제에 참고가 될 거예요.
T3-0945.x: This material will be a useful reference for your homework.
T3-0945.t: 참고로 means 'for your information' or 'FYI' at the start of a sentence.

T3-0946.x: Write your report using this book as a reference.

T3-0947.ex: 이 영화는 새로운 문화 창조에 큰 역할을 했어요.
T3-0947.x: This movie played a big role in creating a new culture.

T3-0948.x: Please tell me how to dispose of the trash.
T3-0948.e: Literally 'deal with and put in order.'
T3-0948.t: It also covers data: 데이터 처리 means data processing.

T3-0949.x: I came to this restaurant on a friend's recommendation.
T3-0949.e: Literally 'push forward and recommend' someone or something.

T3-0950.ex: 이 근처에 맛있는 식당 좀 추천해 주세요.
T3-0950.x: Please recommend a good restaurant around here.
T3-0950.e: Literally 'push forward and recommend' someone or something.
T3-0950.t: 추천해 주세요 is the go-to phrase for asking anyone for a recommendation.

T3-0951.x: I'm from Busan, so I love the ocean.
T3-0951.e: Literally the place your body 'came out' from.
T3-0951.t: Pattern: [place or school] 출신이에요 means 'I'm from…' or 'I'm a graduate of…'.

T3-0952.ex: 두 사람은 의견 충돌이 자주 있어요.
T3-0952.x: The two of them often clash over their opinions.
T3-0952.e: Literally 'strike and rush' into each other.

T3-0953.ex: 이 문제는 여러 측면에서 생각해 봐야 해요.
T3-0953.x: We need to think about this problem from several angles.
T3-0953.t: Pronounced [층면] — nasalization turns ㄱ into ㅇ before ㅁ.

T3-0954.m: to pass through; to pass (a test, a bill)
T3-0954.ex: 저는 한 번에 운전면허 시험에 통과했어요.
T3-0954.x: I passed my driver's license test on the first try.
T3-0954.t: Both 시험에 통과하다 and 시험을 통과하다 are common; 합격하다 is the standard word for passing exams.

T3-0955.ex: 축제 기간에는 이 도로의 차량 통제가 있어요.
T3-0955.x: During the festival, traffic on this road is restricted.

T3-0956.m: to grasp, to understand, to figure out
T3-0956.x: First, we need to understand the situation accurately.
T3-0956.e: Literally 'grasp and hold' something in your mind.
T3-0956.t: Pronounced [파아카다]; it sounds more formal than 알다 and fits work or news contexts.

T3-0957.x: I marked the important parts in red.

T3-0958.m: to mark, to indicate; to express
T3-0958.ex: 지도에 우리 집 위치를 표시해 주세요.
T3-0958.x: Please mark where our house is on the map.
T3-0958.t: It can express feelings too: 감사의 뜻을 표시하다 means to express one's thanks.

T3-0959.m: to relieve, to resolve, to get rid of (stress, a problem)
T3-0959.t: 스트레스를 해소하다 means the same as 스트레스를 풀다, but 풀다 sounds more casual.

T3-0960.ex: 꾸준한 연습은 실력 향상에 도움이 돼요.
T3-0960.x: Steady practice helps you improve your skills.
T3-0960.e: Literally 'toward up' — moving upward, getting better.

T3-0961.ex: 매일 연습해서 한국어 실력이 많이 향상됐어요.
T3-0961.x: I practiced every day, so my Korean improved a lot.
T3-0961.e: Literally 'toward up' — moving upward, getting better.
T3-0961.t: To improve something yourself, use 향상시키다: 실력을 향상시키다.

T3-0962.ex: 두 회사는 오랜 협상 끝에 계약을 맺었어요.
T3-0962.x: After long negotiations, the two companies signed a contract.
T3-0962.t: Pronounced [협쌍] — ㅅ after ㅂ becomes tense.

T3-0963.x: The government announced a policy to expand jobs.
T3-0963.t: Its opposite is 축소 (reduction); on phones, 확대 also means zooming in.

T3-0964.m: to expand, to enlarge; to zoom in
T3-0964.ex: 글씨가 너무 작아서 사진을 확대해서 봤어요.
T3-0964.x: The writing was too small, so I zoomed in on the photo.

T3-0965.ex: 감기 확산을 막으려면 손을 자주 씻으세요.
T3-0965.x: To stop colds from spreading, wash your hands often.
T3-0965.t: Pronounced [확싼] — ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T3-0966.m: to be confirmed, to be verified
T3-0966.x: The cause of the accident has not been confirmed yet.

T3-0967.ex: 시간 활용을 잘하면 공부와 운동을 다 할 수 있어요.
T3-0967.x: If you use your time well, you can both study and exercise.
T3-0967.e: Literally 'living use' — putting something to active use.
T3-0967.t: In grammar books, 활용 means conjugation, like 가다 becoming 가요.

T3-0968.m: to make use of, to utilize, to apply
T3-0968.x: I use my spare time to study Korean.
T3-0968.e: Literally 'living use' — putting something to active use.
T3-0968.t: Unlike plain 사용하다, 활용하다 suggests using something cleverly or to its full advantage.

T3-0969.x: After a good rest, my health recovered a lot.
T3-0969.t: Pronounced [회복뙤다] — ㄷ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T3-0970.t: Pronounced [훌련] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T3-0971.ex: 우리 팀은 대회를 위해 열심히 훈련하고 있어요.
T3-0971.x: Our team is training hard for the competition.

T3-0972.m: to get excited; to get worked up, to get agitated
T3-0972.ex: 너무 흥분하지 말고 천천히 얘기해 보세요.
T3-0972.x: Don't get so worked up — try talking it through slowly.
T3-0972.t: 흥분하다 often means getting agitated or angry; for happy excitement, 신나다 is usually more natural.
rel: to be excited, to have fun

T3-0973.x: I go to the gym after work.
T3-0973.e: From English 'health' plus -장 (place); in Konglish 'health' means working out.
T3-0973.t: 체육관 is a sports gymnasium; for a weight-training gym, Koreans say 헬스장.

T3-0974.x: I play volleyball with my friends every weekend.
T3-0974.e: Literally 'push-away ball'; -구 = ball game: 축구, 야구, 농구, 배구.

T3-0975.x: My dad plays golf with his friends on weekends.
T3-0975.e: From English 'golf'; the final f becomes an extra syllable, 프.
T3-0975.t: Use 치다 with golf, just like tennis: 골프를 치다.

T3-0976.ex: 저는 내년에 마라톤 대회에 참가할 거예요.
T3-0976.x: I'm going to take part in a marathon next year.
T3-0976.t: Say 마라톤을 뛰다 for 'run a marathon' and 완주하다 for finishing the whole course.

T3-0977.x: These days I'm doing yoga every morning.

T3-0978.x: The kids are jumping rope on the playground.
T3-0978.e: 줄 (rope) + 넘기 (going over, from 넘다) — literally 'rope-crossing.'
T3-0978.t: Pronounced [줄럼끼] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ after ㄹ, and ㄱ is tensed.

T3-0979.ex: 저는 매일 아침 공원에서 조깅을 해요.
T3-0979.x: I go jogging in the park every morning.

T3-0980.x: Be sure to stretch before you exercise.
T3-0980.e: From English 'stretching'; the 'st' cluster splits into two syllables, 스트.
T3-0980.t: The verb is 스트레칭(을) 하다; there's no separate Korean verb for 'to stretch' in this sense.

T3-0981.x: My stamina has gotten weak lately, so I started exercising.
T3-0981.e: Literally 'body power'; -력 = power or ability: 체력, 실력, 능력.
T3-0981.t: 체력이 좋다 / 체력이 약하다 mean to have good / poor stamina.

T3-0982.forms: 땀을 흘려요 · 땀을 흘렸어요 · 땀을 흘릴 거예요
T3-0982.ex: 오늘 운동을 열심히 해서 땀을 많이 흘렸어요.
T3-0982.x: I worked out hard today, so I sweated a lot.
T3-0982.e: Literally 'to spill sweat'; 흘리다 also means to spill or shed, as in 눈물을 흘리다.
T3-0982.t: 땀이 나다 just says sweat appears; 땀을 흘리다 suggests sweating a lot, often from hard work.
rel: to sweat, to break a sweat

T3-0983.x: I exercise regularly for my health.
T3-0983.t: Use 규칙적인 before nouns (규칙적인 생활) and 규칙적으로 before verbs.

T3-0984.ex: 꾸준하게 연습하면 누구나 잘할 수 있어요.
T3-0984.x: If you practice consistently, anyone can get good at it.
T3-0984.e: Its adverb 꾸준히 (steadily) is just as common as the adjective.
T3-0984.t: 꾸준히 + verb is a top collocation: 꾸준히 운동하다 (to exercise consistently).

T3-0985.x: The cheering squad sang the fight song loudly.
T3-0985.e: Literally 'respond-and-help group' — a group that backs a team.

T3-0986.x: We beat the other team 3 to 1.

T3-0987.forms: 점수를 내요 · 점수를 냈어요 · 점수를 낼 거예요
T3-0987.ex: 우리 팀이 마지막에 점수를 내서 이겼어요.
T3-0987.x: Our team scored at the end and won.
T3-0987.e: Literally 'bring out points'; 내다 means to produce or put out.
T3-0987.t: For test results, say 점수를 받다 (to get a score), not 점수를 내다.

T3-0988.ex: 그 선수가 이번 경기에서 가장 많은 득점을 했어요.
T3-0988.x: That player scored the most points in this game.
T3-0988.t: Pronounced [득쩜] — ㅈ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T3-0989.m: to tie, to draw (in a game)
T3-0989.x: Yesterday's soccer game ended in a 1-1 tie.
T3-0989.e: The noun for a tie game is the Sino-Korean word 무승부.
T3-0989.t: Use 와/과 for the opponent: 그 팀과 비겼어요 means 'We tied with that team.'

T3-0990.x: Thanks to advances in science and technology, life has become convenient.

T3-0991.x: The invention of the telephone changed the world greatly.
T3-0991.t: 발명 is creating something new; 발견 is discovering something that already exists.

T3-0992.x: Edison invented many things during his life.

T3-0993.x: This museum has a lot of interesting inventions.
T3-0993.e: 발명 + -품 = item, product: 발명품, 작품, 제품.

T3-0994.ex: 이 건물에는 안전 장치가 잘 되어 있어요.
T3-0994.x: This building is well equipped with safety devices.

T3-0995.x: These days, robots even do the cleaning for us.
T3-0995.e: From English 'robot'; the final t becomes a ㅅ batchim, so 로봇이 sounds like [로보시].

T3-0996.ex: 요즘 인공 지능 기술이 빠르게 발전하고 있어요.
T3-0996.x: AI technology is developing rapidly these days.
T3-0996.t: In everyday speech, people often just say AI, pronounced 에이아이.

T3-0997.m: informatization, the shift to an information society
T3-0997.ex: 정보화 시대에는 컴퓨터를 잘 다룰 줄 알아야 해요.
T3-0997.x: In the information age, you need to know how to use a computer well.

T3-0998.ex: 산속에서는 휴대폰 통신이 잘 안 돼요.
T3-0998.x: Cell phone reception is poor in the mountains.
T3-0998.t: 통신사 is your mobile carrier, and 통신비 is your phone bill.

T3-0999.ex: 언젠가 우주로 여행을 가 보고 싶어요.
T3-0999.x: Someday I'd like to travel to space.
T3-0999.e: Classically 'all of space and all of time' together.

T3-1000.x: Earth is a planet that circles the sun.
T3-1000.e: Literally 'moving star' — planets wander across the night sky.

T3-1001.x: The Olympics are a festival for the whole world.
T3-1001.e: Literally 'earth-ball village' — the whole world as one village.

T3-1002.x: Korea's auto industry is highly developed.

T3-1003.ex: 이 과자는 우리 밀을 원료로 만들었어요.
T3-1003.x: This snack is made from Korean wheat.
T3-1003.t: Pronounced [월료] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-1004.ex: 집에 도착하면 문자 메시지를 보내 주세요.
T3-1004.x: Please send me a text when you get home.
T3-1004.t: People usually shorten it to 문자: 문자 보낼게요 means 'I'll text you.'

T3-1005.forms: 통화 중이에요 · 통화 중이라서 (because the line is busy)
T3-1005.m: on the phone, (the line is) busy
T3-1005.x: I called, but the line was busy the whole time.
T3-1005.e: Literally 'in the middle of a call'; -중 = in the middle of: 회의 중, 수업 중.

T3-1006.ex: 친구가 전화를 안 받아서 음성 메시지를 남겼어요.
T3-1006.x: My friend didn't answer, so I left a voicemail.
T3-1006.t: Use 남기다 (to leave): 음성 메시지를 남기다.

T3-1007.t: On the phone, 연결해 드릴게요 means 'I'll put you through.'

T3-1008.m: to be cut off, to be disconnected; to snap, to break (a string)
T3-1008.x: The call suddenly got cut off while we were talking.
T3-1008.e: From 끊다 (to cut, to hang up) + -어지다 (to become).
T3-1008.t: Pronounced [끄너지다] — the ㅎ in ㄶ is silent.

T3-1009.m: to reply (to a message or letter)
T3-1009.x: I haven't replied to my friend's text yet.
T3-1009.t: Use 에 for what you reply to: 메시지에 답장하다; pronounced [답짱하다].

T3-1010.ex: 대학 시절에 친구들과 여행을 많이 했어요.
T3-1010.x: In my college days, I traveled a lot with friends.
T3-1010.t: It usually refers to a past period, often with nostalgia: 그 시절 (those days).

T3-1011.x: I lived in the countryside as a child.
T3-1011.e: 어린 (young, from 어리다) + 시절 (period of life).

T3-1012.ex: 학창 시절에 가장 친했던 친구를 오랜만에 만났어요.
T3-1012.x: I met up with my best friend from school for the first time in ages.
T3-1012.e: Literally 'study-window days' — the years spent learning by the classroom window.
T3-1012.t: It covers all your school years together, and people usually say it looking back fondly.

T3-1013.ex: 그는 이십 대 초반에 회사를 시작했어요.
T3-1013.x: He started his company in his early twenties.
T3-1013.e: Originally the opening stage of a board game such as baduk.
T3-1013.t: Ages work like English: 20대 초반 is 'early twenties,' 30대 후반 is 'late thirties.'

T3-1014.ex: 경기 중반에 우리 팀이 첫 골을 넣었어요.
T3-1014.x: Our team scored the first goal midway through the game.
T3-1014.e: Originally the middle stage of a board game such as baduk.

T3-1015.ex: 축구 경기 후반에 우리 팀이 골을 넣었어요.
T3-1015.x: Our team scored a goal in the second half of the soccer game.
T3-1015.t: Often used with ages: 20대 후반 means 'late twenties'.

T3-1016.ex: 올해 상반기에 새 제품이 나올 예정입니다.
T3-1016.x: A new product is scheduled to come out in the first half of this year.
T3-1016.e: Literally 'upper half period' — January to June.

T3-1017.ex: 회사는 하반기에 직원을 더 뽑을 계획이에요.
T3-1017.x: The company plans to hire more employees in the second half of the year.
T3-1017.e: Literally 'lower half period' — July to December.
T3-1017.t: Common in business news and job ads, e.g. 하반기 공채 'second-half open recruitment'.

T3-1018.e: Literally 'divided period' — the year split into four parts.

T3-1019.m: year (as a period, e.g. fiscal or school year)
T3-1019.x: Please write your graduation year here.
T3-1019.e: Literally 'year term' — a year counted as a unit.
T3-1019.t: After a number it becomes 년도: 2025년도 'the year 2025' — at the start of a word it is 연도.

T3-1020.x: It's the end of the month, so there's a lot of work at the office.

T3-1021.m: meanwhile, all this time, in the meantime
T3-1021.ex: 그동안 저를 많이 도와주셔서 정말 감사했습니다.
