T3-1021.x: Thank you so much for all your help all this time.
T3-1021.e: Built from 그 'that' + 동안 'period' — 'during that time'.
T3-1021.t: 그동안 잘 지냈어요? is the classic greeting when meeting someone after a long time.

T3-1022.m: that day, the same day, the day itself
T3-1022.ex: 표는 공연 당일에도 살 수 있어요.
T3-1022.x: You can also buy tickets on the day of the show.
T3-1022.t: 당일치기 여행 means a same-day round trip — a very common phrase.

T3-1023.m: the day before, the previous day
T3-1023.ex: 시험 전날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
T3-1023.x: It's good to go to bed early the day before an exam.

T3-1024.m: the next day, the following day
T3-1024.ex: 술을 많이 마신 다음날은 머리가 아파요.
T3-1024.x: The day after I drink a lot, I get a headache.
T3-1024.e: 다음 'next' + 날 'day'; dictionaries spell it with a space: 다음 날.
T3-1024.t: Use 내일 for 'tomorrow' from today; use 다음날 for the day after some other event.

T3-1025.ex: 김치는 한국의 가장 대표적인 음식 중 하나예요.
T3-1025.x: Kimchi is one of Korea's most representative foods.

T3-1026.ex: 일반적으로 한국 사람들은 저녁을 일곱 시쯤 먹어요.
T3-1026.x: Generally, Koreans eat dinner around seven o'clock.
T3-1026.e: Literally 'of one kind' — what applies to everyone.
T3-1026.t: 일반적으로 'generally' is a handy sentence opener in TOPIK writing.

T3-1027.x: This park is open to the general public on weekends.
T3-1027.t: Often used before nouns like an adjective: 일반 쓰레기 'general trash', 일반석 'economy seat'.

T3-1028.x: These clothes are made from a special material.

T3-1029.x: Loving your family is a universal feeling.

T3-1030.x: Housing in this neighborhood is relatively cheap.
T3-1030.e: Literally 'facing each other' — judged by comparison.
T3-1030.t: 상대적으로 'relatively' is very common in news and essays.

T3-1031.x: Children absolutely need their parents' love.
T3-1031.e: Literally 'cut off from any comparison' — not relative.
T3-1031.t: Don't mix it up with 절대: 절대 안 돼요 'absolutely not' uses 절대 alone with negatives.

T3-1032.ex: 계획을 좀 더 구체적으로 설명해 주세요.
T3-1032.x: Please explain the plan in a bit more detail.
T3-1032.e: Literally 'having a body' — something with a clear shape.

T3-1033.x: I strongly agree with that opinion.
T3-1033.e: Literally 'piled up to the extreme' — full effort.
T3-1033.t: Usually used right before a verb: 적극 지원하다 'to actively support', 적극 추천하다 'to highly recommend'.

T3-1034.x: Summer starts in earnest next week.
T3-1034.e: Literally 'by the real standard' — doing it properly now.
T3-1034.t: Pronounced [본껵쩍]; 본격적으로 시작하다 'to really get started' is the key collocation.

T3-1035.x: That actor's acting is really natural.
T3-1035.t: 자연스럽게 is the adverb: 자연스럽게 말해요 'speak naturally'.

T3-1036.x: The smile in the photo looks a bit forced.
T3-1036.t: In conversation 어색하다 is more common for awkward situations; 부자연스럽다 sounds more descriptive.

T3-1037.ex: 그 친구는 패션 감각이 정말 좋아요.
T3-1037.x: That friend has a really good sense of fashion.
T3-1037.t: Collocations: 감각이 있다 'to have a flair', 감각이 없다 'to feel numb' or 'to lack taste'.

T3-1038.x: If you think about it with common sense, that statement is strange.

T3-1039.ex: 기술적인 문제 때문에 방송이 잠시 멈췄습니다.
T3-1039.x: The broadcast stopped briefly because of a technical problem.

T3-1040.ex: 이 일은 제 적성에 잘 맞아요.
T3-1040.x: This job really suits my aptitude.
T3-1040.t: Key pattern: 적성에 맞다 'to suit one's aptitude', often about jobs or majors.

T3-1041.x: That child has a talent for music.
T3-1041.t: Pattern: N에 재능이 있다 'to have a talent for N'.

T3-1042.ex: 저는 요리에 소질이 없는 것 같아요.
T3-1042.x: I don't think I have a knack for cooking.
T3-1042.e: Literally 'basic quality' — what you're born with.
T3-1042.t: Often used modestly: 소질이 없어요 'I'm not cut out for it'.

T3-1043.t: 취향 저격 'hits my taste exactly' is popular slang for something you love.

T3-1044.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들은 작은 집에 대한 선호가 높아요.
T3-1044.x: Young people these days have a strong preference for small homes.

T3-1045.x: Many people prefer their own car to public transportation.
T3-1045.e: Literally 'to choose and like' something over others.
T3-1045.t: Pattern: A보다 B를 선호하다 'to prefer B to A'; it sounds formal, common in surveys and news.

T3-1046.x: My special skill is playing the piano.
T3-1046.t: 취미와 특기 'hobbies and special skills' is a classic resume and self-introduction section.

T3-1047.ex: 저는 요즘 채소 위주로 식사를 해요.
T3-1047.x: These days I eat meals that are mostly vegetables.
T3-1047.t: Almost always appears after a noun: 학생 위주의 수업 'a student-centered class'.

T3-1048.x: The subway is the most convenient means of transportation in Seoul.
T3-1048.e: Literally 'hand steps' — the moves you use to get something done.
T3-1048.t: Idiom: 수단과 방법을 가리지 않다 'to use any means necessary'.

T3-1049.ex: 이 도구를 사용하면 쉽게 고칠 수 있어요.
T3-1049.x: If you use this tool, you can fix it easily.
T3-1049.e: Literally 'equipment for the way' of doing a task.

T3-1050.ex: 이 제품에는 몸에 해로운 물질이 들어 있어요.
T3-1050.x: This product contains substances that are harmful to the body.
T3-1050.t: Pronounced [물찔] — ㄹ before ㅈ in Sino words often becomes tense.

T3-1051.ex: 이 프로젝트는 아직 첫 단계에 있어요.
T3-1051.x: This project is still at the first stage.

T3-1052.x: The proposal passed because a majority voted in favor.
T3-1052.t: Common in voting news: 과반수 찬성 'majority approval'.

T3-1053.x: We decided to follow the majority's opinion.

T3-1054.x: We should respect the opinions of the minority too.
T3-1054.e: Literally 'few in number'; a different 소수 means 'decimal' in math.

T3-1055.ex: 반 학생 대다수가 그 영화를 봤어요.
T3-1055.x: Most of the students in the class saw that movie.

T3-1056.m: a considerable number, a good many
T3-1056.ex: 우리 회사 직원 상당수가 재택근무를 원합니다.
T3-1056.x: A considerable number of our company's employees want to work from home.

T3-1057.x: Don't post your personal information online carelessly.
T3-1057.t: 개인정보 유출 'personal data leak' is a frequent news phrase.

T3-1058.x: This university's competition rate this year was ten to one.
T3-1058.t: Pronounced [경쟁뉼]; ratios are read with 대: 10대 1 'ten to one'.

T3-1059.x: Words like 'haneul' (sky) and 'bada' (sea) are native Korean words.

T3-1060.ex: 내년부터 전기와 가스 같은 공공요금이 오를 예정입니다.
T3-1060.x: Utility rates such as electricity and gas are expected to go up starting next year.
T3-1060.t: Covers electricity, gas, water and public transit fares — set or regulated by the government.

T3-1061.x: All workers have the right to rest.
T3-1061.e: -자 = person who does it: 근로자, 노동자, 보행자.
T3-1061.t: Pronounced [글로자]; 근로자 is the neutral, official term, while 노동자 can sound more political.

T3-1062.ex: 이 일은 힘든 육체 노동이 필요해요.
T3-1062.x: This job requires hard physical labor.

T3-1063.x: Factory workers demanded a wage increase.

T3-1064.ex: 이 지역 사람들은 대부분 농업에 종사합니다.
T3-1064.x: Most people in this area work in agriculture.
T3-1064.e: Literally 'farming industry'; -업 = industry: 농업, 산업, 어업.

T3-1065.ex: 그 가수는 대중에게 큰 사랑을 받았어요.
T3-1065.x: That singer was greatly loved by the public.
T3-1065.t: Don't confuse with 대충 'roughly' — 대중 has a plain ㅈ sound.

T3-1066.ex: 한국 대중문화는 전 세계에서 인기가 많아요.
T3-1066.x: Korean pop culture is very popular around the world.

T3-1067.ex: 요즘은 아이를 키우는 맞벌이 부부가 많아요.
T3-1067.x: These days there are many dual-income couples raising children.
T3-1067.e: 맞- 'facing each other, both' + 벌다 'to earn' + -이.
T3-1067.t: Collocations: 맞벌이 부부 'dual-income couple', 맞벌이하다 'both spouses work'.

T3-1068.x: Korea's economy developed greatly through trade.

T3-1069.ex: 고대 문명은 큰 강 주변에서 시작되었습니다.
T3-1069.x: Ancient civilizations began near large rivers.
T3-1069.e: Literally 'writing and brightness' — an enlightened society.

T3-1070.x: Lunar New Year is a big holiday for the Korean people.
T3-1070.t: Koreans often say 우리 민족 'our people' to mean all ethnic Koreans, across both Koreas.

T3-1071.ex: 운전할 때는 보행자를 항상 조심해야 해요.
T3-1071.x: When you drive, you always have to watch out for pedestrians.

T3-1072.ex: 산업화 이후 많은 사람들이 도시로 이사했습니다.
T3-1072.x: After industrialization, many people moved to the cities.
T3-1072.t: Pronounced [사너퐈] — the ㅂ and ㅎ combine into ㅍ.

T3-1073.ex: 그는 생계를 위해 두 가지 일을 해요.
T3-1073.x: He works two jobs to make a living.
T3-1073.t: Collocations: 생계를 꾸리다 or 생계를 유지하다 'to make a living'.

T3-1074.ex: 한국 사람들의 평균 수명이 점점 길어지고 있습니다.
T3-1074.x: The average life expectancy of Koreans is getting longer and longer.

T3-1075.t: 외래어 are borrowed words used in Korean; 외국어 means a foreign language itself.

T3-1076.x: Environmental problems are a problem for all of humanity.
T3-1076.t: Pronounced [일류] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ; don't confuse with 일류 'first-class'.

T3-1077.x: The minimum wage went up a little this year.
T3-1077.e: Literally 'hire money'; a native homonym 임금 means 'king'.

T3-1078.ex: 자연 보호를 위해 쓰레기를 줄여야 해요.
T3-1078.x: We need to reduce trash to protect nature.

T3-1079.ex: 이 지역은 겨울에 눈이 많이 와요.
T3-1079.x: It snows a lot in this area in winter.

T3-1080.ex: 우리 회사는 지역 사회를 위해 봉사 활동을 해요.
T3-1080.x: Our company does volunteer work for the local community.

T3-1081.m: region, the provinces (outside Seoul); local area
T3-1081.x: During the holidays, there are many cars heading out to the provinces.
T3-1081.e: Literally 'land in a direction'; a different 지방 means 'fat'.
T3-1081.t: In Korea 지방 usually means everywhere outside the Seoul area, not just rural places.

T3-1082.ex: 김 부장님은 부하 직원들에게 항상 친절해요.
T3-1082.x: Manager Kim is always kind to the employees under him.
T3-1082.t: 부하 can sound hierarchical; in polite office talk people often say 후배 or 팀원 instead.

T3-1083.m: chairman, president (of a company or group)
T3-1083.x: The chairman came to the meeting in person today.
T3-1083.t: Add 님 when addressing or referring to them politely: 회장님.

T3-1084.ex: 아버지는 은퇴하시면서 형에게 회사 경영을 맡기셨어요.
T3-1084.x: When my father retired, he left the running of the company to my older brother.

T3-1085.ex: 이번 주에는 야근이 많아서 너무 피곤해요.
T3-1085.x: I've had to work late a lot this week, so I'm really tired.

T3-1086.m: to work late, to work overtime at night
T3-1086.x: Because of the deadline, I have to work late again today.
T3-1086.t: Also heard as 야근을 하다; 칼퇴근 'leaving right on time' is its happy opposite.

T3-1087.x: Our company's pay comes in on the 25th of every month.
T3-1087.t: 급여 is the formal, paperwork word; in conversation people usually say 월급.

T3-1088.ex: 올해 연말에 회사에서 보너스를 많이 받았어요.
T3-1088.x: I got a big bonus from my company at the end of this year.

T3-1089.x: I started job hunting after graduation.
T3-1089.t: Contrast: 구인 is the company seeking workers.

T3-1090.ex: 이번 주 금요일까지 지원서를 내야 해요.
T3-1090.x: I have to submit my application by this Friday.
T3-1090.e: Literally 'a document of your wish' to join.

T3-1091.x: The interviewer asked me about my experience.

T3-1092.m: to hire, to employ, to recruit
T3-1092.ex: 그 회사는 올해 신입 사원을 50명 채용했습니다.
T3-1092.x: That company hired fifty new employees this year.
T3-1092.t: Passive form 채용되다 'to be hired'; in casual talk people often say 뽑다 instead.

T3-1093.ex: 우리 회사에서 신입 사원을 모집하고 있어요.
T3-1093.x: Our company is recruiting new employees.
T3-1093.t: Pronounced [모지파다] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T3-1094.m: failure (of an exam or selection), rejection
T3-1094.ex: 시험에 불합격해서 내년에 다시 볼 거예요.
T3-1094.x: I failed the exam, so I'll take it again next year.
T3-1094.t: In everyday speech people usually say 시험에 떨어졌어요 instead of 불합격했어요.

T3-1095.m: to be promoted, to get a promotion
T3-1095.ex: 우리 형이 올해 드디어 과장으로 승진했어요.
T3-1095.x: My older brother finally got promoted to manager this year.
T3-1095.e: Literally 'rise and advance' up the ladder.

T3-1096.x: My father is going to retire next year.

T3-1097.m: to retire, to leave one's job
T3-1097.ex: 삼촌은 작년에 회사를 퇴직하고 시골로 이사했어요.
T3-1097.x: My uncle left his company last year and moved to the countryside.
T3-1097.t: 퇴직하다 is leaving a specific job; 은퇴하다 is retiring from working life altogether.

T3-1098.m: to retire (from work or a career)
T3-1098.ex: 그 축구 선수는 서른다섯 살에 은퇴했어요.
T3-1098.x: That soccer player retired at thirty-five.
T3-1098.e: Literally 'withdraw out of sight' from public or working life.

T3-1099.x: He handed in his resignation letter this morning.

T3-1100.ex: 회사가 어려워서 많은 직원이 해고를 당했어요.
T3-1100.x: The company was struggling, so many employees were laid off.
T3-1100.t: From the worker's side, say 해고를 당하다 or 해고되다 'to get fired'.

T3-1101.x: Youth unemployment is a serious problem these days.
T3-1101.t: 실업 is used for society-level statistics; for one person losing a job, 실직 is more common.

T3-1102.ex: 갑자기 실직을 해서 새 일을 찾고 있어요.
T3-1102.x: I suddenly lost my job, so I'm looking for new work.

T3-1103.x: I worked a part-time job at a convenience store during vacation.
T3-1103.e: Short for 아르바이트, from German 'Arbeit' (work); in Korea it means a part-time job.
T3-1103.t: 알바 is casual; use 아르바이트 in writing or formal situations.

T3-1104.x: I want to work hard and become a permanent employee.

T3-1105.ex: 저는 일 년 계약직으로 일하고 있어요.
T3-1105.x: I'm working in a one-year contract position.

T3-1106.m: to sign a contract, to make a contract
T3-1106.x: Yesterday I signed the contract for a new place at the real estate office.
T3-1106.t: Pronounced [계야카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T3-1107.ex: 오늘 회의 결과를 부장님께 바로 보고했어요.
T3-1107.x: I reported today's meeting results to the department head right away.
T3-1107.e: Literally 'report and tell' to a superior.
T3-1107.t: Don't confuse it with 보고 'seeing and…' from 보다; context makes it clear.

T3-1108.x: This document needs the president's approval.
T3-1108.e: Literally 'decide and rule on' a document.
T3-1108.t: Don't mix it up with 결제 'payment'; they sound the same.

T3-1109.ex: 이번 행사에 여러분의 많은 협조를 부탁드립니다.
T3-1109.x: We ask for your full cooperation with this event.
T3-1109.t: Common in notices: 협조 부탁드립니다 'we ask for your cooperation'.

T3-1110.ex: 두 회사는 협력을 통해 새 제품을 만들었습니다.
T3-1110.x: The two companies created a new product through collaboration.

T3-1111.x: My older sister does accounting work at her company.

T3-1112.x: I'm in charge of planning this event.
T3-1112.e: Literally 'aim and map out' a project.
T3-1112.t: 기획 is planning a project or product at work; 계획 is any plan, including personal ones.

T3-1113.ex: 저는 화장품 회사에서 마케팅을 담당하고 있어요.
T3-1113.x: I'm in charge of marketing at a cosmetics company.

T3-1114.x: We're promoting the new store on social media.

T3-1115.ex: 그 회사는 텔레비전에서 새 휴대폰을 광고했어요.
T3-1115.x: That company advertised its new cell phone on TV.
T3-1115.t: 광고 is paid ads; 홍보 is broader publicity and PR.

T3-1116.ex: 이번 달 영업 실적이 아주 좋아요.
T3-1116.x: Our sales results this month are very good.

T3-1117.ex: 회의 자료를 열 장 인쇄해 주세요.
T3-1117.x: Please print ten copies of the meeting materials.
T3-1117.e: Literally 'stamp and brush' ink onto paper.
T3-1117.t: For printing from a computer, people also say 출력하다 or 뽑다.

T3-1118.ex: 판사가 그 사람에게 벌금을 내라고 했어요.
T3-1118.x: The judge ordered that person to pay a fine.

T3-1119.x: My friend is an engineer at a car company.

T3-1120.x: My younger sibling works as a programmer at a game company.
T3-1120.e: From English 'programmer'; extra 으 vowels break up the English consonant clusters.
T3-1120.t: In tech companies, 개발자 'developer' is the more common everyday word.

T3-1121.x: My puppy was sick, so I took it to the local vet.

T3-1122.ex: 시장 상인들이 아침 일찍 가게 문을 열어요.
T3-1122.x: The market vendors open their shops early in the morning.

T3-1123.ex: 회의에서 한국어 통역을 해 주실 수 있어요?
T3-1123.x: Could you interpret into Korean at the meeting?
T3-1123.t: 통역 is spoken interpreting; 번역 is written translation.

T3-1124.ex: 다음 주에 이사하려고 이삿짐 업체에 전화했어요.
T3-1124.x: I called a moving company because I'm moving next week.

T3-1125.ex: 저는 직원이 오십 명인 중소기업에 다녀요.
T3-1125.x: I work at a small company with fifty employees.

T3-1126.ex: 이 공장에서는 자동차 부품 제조를 합니다.

T3-1127.x: Korea exports a lot of cars every year.

T3-1128.x: I have a meeting with someone from a client company this afternoon.
T3-1128.e: Literally 'place you go back and forth with', i.e., trade with.

T3-1129.x: Ice cream sales go up a lot in summer.
T3-1129.t: Typical verbs: 매출이 오르다/늘다 'sales rise', 매출이 떨어지다 'sales drop'.

T3-1130.ex: 두 회사가 새 시장에서 경쟁하고 있어요.
T3-1130.x: The two companies are competing in a new market.

T3-1131.x: Good quality is our product's competitive edge.

T3-1132.m: starting a business, founding a company
T3-1132.x: After graduating from college, I started a business with a friend.

T3-1133.x: Lots of people invest in stocks these days.

T3-1134.x: Every month I deposit part of my salary in the bank.

T3-1135.ex: 이번 달 월세를 집주인 계좌로 입금했어요.
T3-1135.x: I deposited this month's rent into the landlord's account.

T3-1136.ex: 현금 출금은 저쪽 기계에서 하시면 됩니다.
T3-1136.x: You can withdraw cash at that machine over there.

T3-1137.m: to send money, to transfer money (remit)
T3-1137.ex: 지난주에 미국에 계신 부모님께 돈을 송금했어요.
T3-1137.x: Last week I sent money to my parents in the U.S.
T3-1137.t: 송금 is often used for sending money abroad; between local accounts, 이체 is more common.

T3-1138.x: Doing account transfers on your phone is convenient.
T3-1138.e: Literally 'move and swap over' from one account to another.

T3-1139.ex: 어제 먹은 밥값을 친구에게 이체해 줬어요.
T3-1139.x: I transferred my share of yesterday's meal to my friend.

T3-1140.ex: 여행 가기 전에 공항에서 달러를 원으로 환전했어요.
T3-1140.x: Before my trip, I exchanged dollars for won at the airport.
T3-1140.t: Pattern: A를 B로 환전하다 'exchange A into B'.

T3-1141.m: to lend, to borrow (a loan); to check out (library books)
T3-1141.x: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
T3-1141.t: Borrowers often say 대출을 받다 'get a loan'; at libraries, 책을 대출하다 means checking out books.

T3-1142.x: Please write your name here and sign.
T3-1142.t: In speech, 사인하다 is very common; 서명하다 sounds more official.

T3-1143.x: My transit card balance was low, so I topped it up at the subway station.
T3-1143.t: You'll hear 잔액이 부족합니다 on Korean buses when your card runs low.

T3-1144.x: The bank issued me a new debit card.
T3-1144.t: From the receiver's side, use 발급받다: 비자를 발급받았어요 'I got my visa issued'.

T3-1145.ex: 이번 달 말까지 전기 요금을 납부해야 합니다.
T3-1145.x: You must pay the electricity bill by the end of this month.
T3-1145.e: Literally 'pay in and hand over' to an authority.
T3-1145.t: 납부하다 is formal, used on bills and notices; in conversation people just say 내다.

T3-1146.ex: 신청 서류는 다음 주에 우편으로 보내 드리겠습니다.
T3-1146.x: We'll send you the application documents by mail next week.
T3-1146.e: From old relay-station mail service; think 'mail convenience'.

T3-1147.x: This clinic sees patients on Saturdays too.
T3-1147.t: Pronounced [질료] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-1148.ex: 병원에 갔는데 의사에게 감기라는 진단을 받았어요.
T3-1148.x: I went to the clinic, and the doctor diagnosed me with a cold.

T3-1149.ex: 회사에 진단서를 내야 해서 병원에 갔어요.
T3-1149.x: I went to the hospital because I need to submit a doctor's note to my company.

T3-1150.ex: 의사의 처방이 있어야 이 약을 살 수 있어요.
T3-1150.x: You need a doctor's prescription to buy this medicine.
T3-1150.e: Literally 'a method for handling' the illness.
T3-1150.t: In Korea you take the 처방전 from the clinic to a separate 약국.

T3-1151.m: to receive treatment, to be treated
T3-1151.ex: 다리를 다쳐서 한 달 동안 치료받았어요.
T3-1151.x: I hurt my leg and got treatment for a month.
T3-1151.t: The doctor 치료하다 'treats'; the patient 치료받다 'gets treated'.

T3-1152.x: My grandmother had knee surgery last week.
T3-1152.t: 수술하다 works for both doctor and patient; 수술을 받다 clearly means the patient had it.

T3-1153.x: If there's an emergency patient, call 119.

T3-1154.x: I got herbal medicine made at a Korean medicine clinic.
T3-1154.t: Pronounced [하늬원]; 침을 맞다 is the set phrase for getting acupuncture.

T3-1155.ex: 보건소에서 무료로 독감 주사를 맞을 수 있어요.
T3-1155.x: You can get a free flu shot at the public health center.

T3-1156.m: to register, to check in; to receive (an application)
T3-1156.x: When you get to the hospital, check in first and wait.
T3-1156.t: Technically the office 접수하다 'receives'; patients and applicants use it too, meaning 'sign in, submit'.

T3-1157.x: I caught a cold, so I keep sneezing.
T3-1157.t: Use 재채기가 나다 or 재채기를 하다; Koreans don't say 'bless you' after a sneeze.

T3-1158.ex: 어제 저녁을 먹고 나서 심한 복통이 생겼어요.
T3-1158.x: After dinner yesterday, I got a bad stomachache.
T3-1158.e: Literally 'belly pain'. -통 = pain: 두통, 치통, 복통.
T3-1158.t: 복통 is medical; in daily conversation say 배가 아파요.

T3-1159.x: Drinking a lot of water helps with constipation.

T3-1160.ex: 밥을 너무 빨리 먹어서 소화불량에 걸렸어요.
T3-1160.x: I ate too fast and got indigestion.
T3-1160.t: In daily life, Koreans often say 체했어요 'my food is stuck' instead.

T3-1161.ex: 아이가 열이 나고 구토를 해서 병원에 왔어요.
T3-1161.x: My child has a fever and is vomiting, so we came to the hospital.
T3-1161.t: 구토 is medical; in conversation people say 토했어요.

T3-1162.ex: 상처에 염증이 생겨서 약을 먹고 있어요.
T3-1162.x: The wound got inflamed, so I'm taking medicine.
T3-1162.e: Literally 'flame symptom', since inflamed skin is red and hot.
T3-1162.t: Pronounced [염쯩]; -염 names inflammations, like 위염 'gastritis' and 장염 'enteritis'.

T3-1163.x: Be careful not to get food poisoning in summer.

T3-1164.ex: 담배는 여러 가지 심장 질환의 원인이 됩니다.
T3-1164.t: 질환 is formal and usually follows a body part: 심장 질환, 피부 질환.

T3-1165.x: There are lots of germs on your hands, so wash them often.

T3-1166.ex: 감염을 막으려면 손을 깨끗이 씻어야 해요.
T3-1166.x: To prevent infection, you have to wash your hands well.
T3-1166.e: Literally 'affected and stained', like dye seeping into cloth.
T3-1166.t: 감염 is a person catching germs; 전염 is a disease spreading from person to person.

T3-1167.ex: 독감은 전염이 잘 되니까 마스크를 쓰세요.
T3-1167.x: The flu spreads easily, so wear a mask.
T3-1167.e: Literally 'pass on the stain' to others.

T3-1168.ex: 아기는 오늘 보건소에서 예방 주사를 맞았어요.
T3-1168.x: The baby got a vaccination at the health center today.
T3-1168.t: Use 맞다 with shots: 주사를 맞다 'to get a shot'.

T3-1169.ex: 이 알약은 하루에 두 번 드세요.
T3-1169.x: Take this pill twice a day.
T3-1169.e: Native 알 'grain, egg' plus 약 'medicine': medicine in little grains.
T3-1169.t: Pronounced [알략] — ㄴ is added and becomes ㄹ.

T3-1170.x: I put ointment on the cut and stuck a bandage on it.

T3-1171.x: You have to disinfect a wound first.
T3-1171.t: Pronounced [소독] but 소독약 becomes [소동냑] through ㄴ-insertion and nasalization.

T3-1172.ex: 간호사가 주사를 놓기 전에 팔을 소독했어요.
T3-1172.x: The nurse disinfected my arm before giving the shot.

T3-1173.ex: 이 약은 하루에 세 번 식후에 복용하세요.
T3-1173.x: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
T3-1173.e: Literally 'take and use' — formal word for taking medicine.
T3-1173.t: 복용하다 is formal and appears on labels; in conversation people usually say 약을 먹다.

T3-1174.x: I've been tired lately, so I take supplements every morning.

T3-1175.x: Fruit contains a lot of vitamins.
T3-1175.e: From English 'vitamin', said with a short 'bi' sound: bi-ta-min.
T3-1175.t: Vitamin C is 비타민 시, and vitamin D is 비타민 디.

T3-1176.x: After I started exercising, I lost five kilograms.
T3-1176.t: 체중 is formal or medical; in everyday talk people say 몸무게.

T3-1177.x: I developed insomnia because of stress.
T3-1177.e: Literally 'not-sleeping condition'; -증 = medical condition: 우울증, 건망증.
T3-1177.t: The common pattern is 불면증에 시달리다, 'to suffer from insomnia'.

T3-1178.ex: 우울증은 전문가의 도움을 받으면 나을 수 있어요.
T3-1178.x: Depression can get better if you get help from a professional.

T3-1179.ex: 비만은 여러 가지 병의 원인이 될 수 있어요.
T3-1179.x: Obesity can be the cause of many diseases.
T3-1179.t: 비만 is a medical term; calling a person 뚱뚱하다 to their face is rude.

T3-1180.ex: 이 건물 안에서는 흡연이 금지되어 있습니다.
T3-1180.x: Smoking is prohibited inside this building.
T3-1180.t: Pronounced [흐변]: the ㅂ batchim moves to the next syllable.

T3-1181.m: to quit smoking, to refrain from smoking
T3-1181.x: My father quit smoking last year for his health.
T3-1181.e: Literally 'forbid smoke'; 금연 alone means 'No Smoking' on signs.

T3-1182.ex: 음주 후에는 절대 운전하면 안 돼요.
T3-1182.x: You must never drive after drinking.

T3-1183.ex: 한국은 의료 서비스가 빠르고 편리한 편이에요.
T3-1183.x: Korea's medical services are fairly fast and convenient.
T3-1183.t: Mostly used before another noun: 의료 보험, 의료 기관, 의료비.

T3-1184.ex: 제 동생은 대학교에서 의학을 공부하고 있어요.
T3-1184.x: My younger sibling is studying medicine at university.
T3-1184.e: Literally 'medicine study'; -학 = field of study: 과학, 경제학.
T3-1184.t: 의학 is the science; medicine you swallow is 약.

T3-1185.x: The child's cheeks turned red in the cold weather.
T3-1185.e: Synonym of 볼; 뺨을 때리다 means 'to slap someone's face'.
T3-1185.t: 볼 is softer and common for cute cheeks; 뺨 often appears with slapping.

T3-1186.x: I was nervous, so my palms got sweaty.
T3-1186.e: 손 'hand' + 바닥 'bottom, floor'; compare 발바닥 'sole of the foot'.

T3-1187.ex: 동생이 화가 나서 주먹을 꽉 쥐었어요.
T3-1187.x: My younger brother got angry and clenched his fist tightly.
T3-1187.e: 주먹밥, 'fist rice', is a rice ball shaped by hand.

T3-1188.x: I dyed my hair brown at the hair salon.
T3-1188.t: The usual pattern is 머리를 [color]으로 염색하다.

T3-1189.x: I wanted a change of mood, so I got a perm.
T3-1189.e: From English 'permanent (wave)', shortened; Koreans say 파마하다, 'to get a perm'.

T3-1190.ex: 이 옷에는 간단한 액세서리가 잘 어울려요.
T3-1190.x: Simple accessories go well with this outfit.
T3-1190.e: From English 'accessory'; often spelled 악세사리 in casual writing, but 액세서리 is standard.

T3-1191.x: The shirt sleeves were too long, so I had them shortened.
T3-1191.e: Homonym warning: 소매 also means 'retail' (from Chinese characters), as in 소매가격.
T3-1191.t: For T-shirts, people often say 반팔 'half arm' instead of 반소매.

T3-1192.ex: 그 배우는 평소에 수수한 옷을 즐겨 입어요.
T3-1192.x: That actor usually likes to wear plain clothes.
T3-1192.e: Positive nuance: unflashy and modest, unlike 촌스럽다 'tacky'.

T3-1193.ex: 새로 생긴 카페는 인테리어가 정말 세련됐어요.
T3-1193.x: The new café has a really stylish interior.
T3-1193.e: Literally 'washed and refined' — polished until elegant.

T3-1194.ex: 이 디자인은 좀 촌스러운 것 같아요.
T3-1194.x: I think this design is a bit tacky.

T3-1195.m: officetel (studio unit for living or working)
T3-1195.x: I live alone in an officetel near my company.
T3-1195.e: Konglish blend of English 'office' + 'hotel'; it's a studio apartment building.

T3-1196.x: The landlord is looking for a new tenant.
T3-1196.e: Literally 'person who enters on rent'; -자 = person: 운전자, 이용자.

T3-1197.forms: 날라요 · 날랐어요 · 나를 거예요 · 나르세요 (르 irregular)
T3-1197.m: to carry, to move (things from place to place)
T3-1197.ex: 이삿날 친구들이 무거운 상자를 날라 줬어요.
T3-1197.x: On moving day, my friends carried the heavy boxes for me.
T3-1197.e: Don't confuse with 날다 'to fly': 날라요 is 'carry', 날아요 is 'fly'.
T3-1197.t: 나르다 means carrying things back and forth, often many items or heavy loads.

T3-1198.ex: 방이 깔끔하게 정돈되어 있어서 기분이 좋아요.
T3-1198.x: The room is neatly tidied, so it feels good.
T3-1198.t: Often paired as 정리 정돈, 'tidying and organizing'.

T3-1199.x: After moving, I changed the furniture layout.

T3-1200.x: We replaced the old windows with new ones.
T3-1200.t: Common pattern: A를 B로 교체하다, 'replace A with B'.

T3-1201.x: After cooking, open the windows and air out the room.

T3-1202.ex: 지하철 안은 냉방이 잘 되어서 시원해요.
T3-1202.x: The subway is well air-conditioned, so it's cool.
T3-1202.e: Literally 'cold room'; the opposite is 난방 'heating'.
T3-1202.t: 냉방병 is a common Korean term for colds or fatigue blamed on strong air conditioning.

T3-1203.x: It got cold, so I turned on the boiler.
T3-1203.e: From English 'boiler'; in Korea it heats water for floor heating (ondol).
T3-1203.t: Koreans say 보일러를 켜다/끄다 where Americans would say turn the heat on or off.

T3-1204.ex: 집에 들어가기 전에 대문을 꼭 잠그세요.
T3-1204.x: Be sure to lock the front gate when you go in.
T3-1204.e: Literally 'big door' — the gate to a house's yard.

T3-1205.x: The room was dark, so I turned on the light.
T3-1205.t: In speech, 불을 켜다 'turn on the light' is more common than 전등을 켜다.

T3-1206.x: The day before the interview, I ironed my shirt.
T3-1206.e: Built from 다리다 'to iron clothes'; don't confuse with 다리 'leg' or 'bridge'.

T3-1207.ex: 마트에서 휴지와 세제 같은 생활용품을 샀어요.
T3-1207.x: I bought household goods like toilet paper and detergent at the supermarket.
T3-1207.t: Pronounced [생활룡품]: an ㄴ sound is added before 용, then it becomes ㄹ.

T3-1208.x: The room is small but very cozy.
T3-1208.t: Pronounced [아느카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-1209.ex: 이 도서관은 넓고 쾌적해서 공부하기 좋아요.
T3-1209.x: This library is spacious and pleasant, so it's good for studying.
T3-1209.t: Used for spaces, air or surroundings, not for people: 쾌적한 환경.

T3-1210.m: police box, small local police station
T3-1210.ex: 지갑을 주워서 근처 파출소에 갖다 줬어요.
T3-1210.x: I found a wallet and took it to the nearby police box.
T3-1210.e: Literally 'place officers are dispatched from'; -소 = place: 연구소, 주유소.

T3-1211.ex: 외국인은 체류 기간이 끝나기 전에 비자를 연장해야 해요.
T3-1211.x: Foreigners must extend their visa before their period of stay ends.
T3-1211.t: Mostly in official contexts: 체류 기간, 체류 자격 'visa status'.

T3-1212.ex: 엘리베이터 앞에 점검 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
T3-1212.x: There's a maintenance notice posted in front of the elevator.

T3-1213.ex: 시험 일정에 대한 공지가 홈페이지에 올라왔어요.
T3-1213.x: A notice about the exam schedule was posted on the website.
T3-1213.t: On websites, the 'Notices' tab is usually 공지 사항.

T3-1214.x: The number of airport users rises sharply on weekends.
T3-1214.t: 이용객 is for people visiting places like stations or parks; for websites or services, use 이용자.

T3-1215.ex: 이 앱은 이용자가 천만 명이 넘어요.
T3-1215.x: This app has over ten million users.
T3-1215.e: 이용 'use' + -자 'person who does it': 운전자, 소비자.

T3-1216.m: to withdraw, to quit (a group or membership)
T3-1216.ex: 요즘 사용하지 않는 사이트에서 모두 탈퇴했어요.
T3-1216.x: I withdrew from all the sites I don't use these days.
T3-1216.t: Common patterns: 회원 탈퇴 'delete account' and 동아리에서 탈퇴하다 'leave a club'.

T3-1217.m: closure (of a museum, library, etc.), closed day
T3-1217.x: The museum is closed every Monday.
T3-1217.e: Literally 'the hall rests'; for shops, the word is 휴무 or 휴업.

T3-1218.m: to enter (a venue), to be admitted
T3-1218.ex: 공연 시작 30분 전부터 입장할 수 있습니다.
T3-1218.x: You can enter starting 30 minutes before the show.
T3-1218.e: Literally 'enter the venue'; a homonym 입장 means 'position, standpoint'.

T3-1219.x: On Lunar New Year, people eat traditional food.
T3-1219.e: 전통 'tradition' + -적 '-al': turns nouns into describing words: 역사적, 문화적.
T3-1219.t: Use 전통적인 before nouns and 전통적으로 as an adverb.

T3-1220.ex: 설날에 떡국을 먹는 것은 한국의 오래된 풍습이에요.
T3-1220.x: Eating rice cake soup on Lunar New Year is an old Korean custom.
T3-1220.e: Literally 'the wind and habits' of a place — its way of life.

T3-1221.x: Customs for greeting people differ from country to country.
T3-1221.e: Literally 'accustomed habits' — what a society usually does.
T3-1221.t: 관습 is a society's convention; a personal habit is 습관, the same syllables reversed.

T3-1222.ex: 그 학생은 선생님께 항상 공손하게 인사해요.
T3-1222.x: That student always greets the teacher politely.

T3-1223.ex: 처음 만난 사람에게는 높임말을 써야 해요.
T3-1223.x: You should use polite speech with people you've just met.
T3-1223.t: Pronounced [노핌말]; 존댓말 means the same thing and is just as common.

T3-1224.ex: 다른 사람의 의견을 존중하는 것이 중요해요.
T3-1224.x: It's important to respect other people's opinions.
T3-1224.t: 존중하다 is respecting rights or opinions; 존경하다 is admiring someone, like a teacher or parent.

T3-1225.m: New Year's money (given to children after a bow)
T3-1225.x: On Lunar New Year, I bowed to my grandmother and received New Year's money.
T3-1225.e: 세배 'New Year's bow' + 돈 'money'; the ㅅ links the two words.
T3-1225.t: Pronounced [세배똔/세밷똔]; children bow first, then elders hand out the money.

T3-1226.ex: 추석에는 가족이 모여서 조상께 차례를 지내요.
T3-1226.x: On Chuseok, families gather and hold a memorial rite for their ancestors.

T3-1227.x: I went to my friend's wedding and gave a cash gift.
T3-1227.t: Pronounced [추기금]; put cash in a white envelope and hand it in at the reception desk.

T3-1228.ex: 결혼식장에 하객이 이백 명 넘게 왔어요.
T3-1228.x: More than two hundred guests came to the wedding.

T3-1229.ex: 민속 마을에서 옛날 한국 집을 구경했어요.
T3-1229.x: I looked around old Korean houses at a folk village.
T3-1229.t: Mostly used before nouns: 민속놀이 'folk games', 민속 박물관 'folk museum'.

T3-1230.ex: 경주에는 신라 시대의 유적이 많이 남아 있어요.
T3-1230.x: Many historic sites from the Silla period remain in Gyeongju.
T3-1230.t: 유적 is a place or site; 유물 is an object you can carry.

T3-1231.ex: 박물관에서 오래된 왕관 같은 유물을 봤어요.
T3-1231.x: I saw relics like an ancient crown at the museum.

T3-1232.x: Today is a historic day for our team.

T3-1233.ex: 이 호수에는 용에 관한 전설이 있어요.
T3-1233.x: There is a legend about a dragon at this lake.
T3-1233.t: Like English, 전설 also describes a famous person: 축구의 전설 'a soccer legend'.

T3-1234.ex: 밤에 손톱을 깎으면 안 된다는 것은 미신이에요.
T3-1234.x: The idea that you shouldn't cut your nails at night is a superstition.
T3-1234.t: A famous Korean superstition: writing a living person's name in red ink is bad luck.

T3-1235.x: The white on the Korean flag symbolizes peace.

T3-1236.x: A red traffic light means stop.
T3-1236.e: Literally 'the taste of an idea' — its flavor or sense.
T3-1236.t: In everyday talk, 무슨 뜻이에요? 'What does it mean?' is more common than 의미하다.

T3-1237.x: Hanbok is clothing unique to Korea.
T3-1237.e: Literally 'firmly possessed' — belonging only to that thing.
T3-1237.t: Almost always used as X 고유의 (+noun), 'unique to X'.

T3-1239.ex: 한국에 처음 왔을 때 문화 충격을 받았어요.
T3-1239.x: When I first came to Korea, I experienced culture shock.
T3-1239.e: A direct translation of English 'culture shock': 문화 'culture' + 충격 'shock'.
T3-1239.t: The usual verb is 받다: 문화 충격을 받다, 'to experience culture shock'.

T3-1240.ex: 이 마을에는 젊은 예술가들이 많이 살고 있어요.
T3-1240.x: Many young artists live in this village.

T3-1241.ex: 이 미술관에서는 현대 미술 작품을 전시하고 있어요.
T3-1241.x: This art museum is exhibiting works of modern art.

T3-1242.m: to perform, to put on a show
T3-1242.ex: 그 가수는 다음 달에 서울에서 공연할 거예요.
T3-1242.x: That singer will perform in Seoul next month.

T3-1243.x: I went to a concert with a friend on the weekend.
T3-1243.t: Pronounced [으마쾨]; for pop shows, people usually say 콘서트.

T3-1244.ex: 이 곡은 제가 제일 좋아하는 노래예요.
T3-1244.t: Use 곡 to count songs: 노래 한 곡 부를게요, 'I'll sing one song'.

T3-1245.m: to watch, to view (a show, game or exhibition)
T3-1245.x: I watched a musical with my family.
T3-1245.t: Pronounced [괄람하다]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T3-1246.m: spectator, visitor (to a show or exhibition)
T3-1246.ex: 이번 전시회에는 관람객이 매일 천 명 넘게 와요.
T3-1246.x: Over a thousand visitors come to this exhibition every day.

T3-1247.m: to appreciate, to enjoy (art, music, films)
T3-1247.x: On weekends, I rest at home enjoying music.
T3-1247.t: 음악 감상 'listening to music' is a classic answer when Koreans list hobbies.

T3-1248.ex: 제 꿈은 유명한 소설가가 되는 거예요.
T3-1248.x: My dream is to become a famous novelist.

T3-1249.ex: 저는 주말마다 사진 동호회 사람들과 같이 사진을 찍으러 가요.
T3-1249.x: Every weekend I go out taking pictures with people from my photography club.
T3-1249.e: Literally 'a meeting of people who like the same thing.'
T3-1249.t: Use 동호회에 가입하다 for 'to join a club'; school clubs are usually called 동아리 instead.

T3-1250.x: I did volunteer work at a nursing home during the break.
T3-1250.t: The usual collocation is 봉사 활동을 하다, 'to do volunteer activities.'

T3-1251.ex: 이번 축제에는 자원봉사자가 이백 명 넘게 참가했어요.
T3-1251.x: More than two hundred volunteers took part in this festival.
T3-1251.e: Literally 'a person who serves by their own wish.' -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T3-1252.ex: 이 가격에는 숙박과 아침 식사가 포함돼 있어요.
T3-1252.x: This price includes lodging and breakfast.
T3-1252.t: Trip lengths use 박 for nights: 2박 3일 means 'three days, two nights.'

T3-1253.x: The incident was widely reported in the press.
T3-1253.t: Pronounced [얼론]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

T3-1254.ex: 그 드라마는 매주 금요일 밤에 방송해요.
T3-1254.x: That drama airs every Friday night.
T3-1254.e: Literally 'to release and send out' signals.

T3-1255.ex: 방송사들이 그 사고를 하루 종일 보도했습니다.
T3-1255.x: The broadcasters covered the accident all day long.
T3-1255.t: Used for news coverage only; for reporting to a boss, use 보고하다.

T3-1256.ex: 그 예능 프로그램은 시청률이 아주 높아요.
T3-1256.x: That variety show has very high ratings.
T3-1256.t: Pronounced [시청뉼]: after ㅇ, the ㄹ of 률 turns into ㄴ.

T3-1257.ex: 이 잡지는 젊은 독자들에게 인기가 많아요.
T3-1257.x: This magazine is popular with young readers.
T3-1257.t: Pronounced [독짜]; don't confuse it with 독자 'only child' or 'independent', which use different hanja.

T3-1258.ex: 저는 피곤할 때 웃긴 예능을 봐요.
T3-1258.x: When I'm tired, I watch funny variety shows.
T3-1258.e: Literally 'artistic skill'; now mostly means TV entertainment shows.

T3-1259.ex: 어제 바다 동물에 대한 다큐멘터리를 봤어요.
T3-1259.x: Yesterday I watched a documentary about sea animals.
T3-1259.e: From English 'documentary'; often shortened to 다큐.

T3-1260.ex: 그 배우는 드라마 한 편으로 스타가 됐어요.
T3-1260.x: That actor became a star from a single drama.

T3-1261.m: topic of conversation, talk of the town
T3-1261.x: That movie is the talk of the internet these days.
T3-1261.t: 화제가 되다 means 'to become a hot topic'; 화제를 바꾸다 means 'to change the subject.'

T3-1262.x: Two people died in this accident.
T3-1262.t: A formal, news-style word; in conversation say 죽다, or 돌아가시다 for elders.

T3-1263.ex: 그 선수는 다리 부상 때문에 경기에 못 나갔어요.
T3-1263.x: That player couldn't play in the game because of a leg injury.
T3-1263.t: Common verb pairings: 부상을 입다 or 부상을 당하다, 'to be injured.'

T3-1264.x: The police listened carefully to the victim's story.

T3-1265.m: to interview, to give an interview
T3-1265.ex: 기자가 경기가 끝난 후에 감독을 인터뷰했어요.
T3-1265.x: The reporter interviewed the coach after the game ended.
T3-1265.t: For a job interview, Koreans usually say 면접, not 인터뷰.

T3-1266.ex: 새 정책에 대한 여론이 좋지 않습니다.
T3-1266.x: Public opinion on the new policy is not good.

T3-1267.ex: 학생 백 명을 대상으로 설문 조사를 했어요.
T3-1267.x: We conducted a survey of one hundred students.

T3-1268.ex: 통계에 따르면 혼자 사는 사람이 계속 늘고 있습니다.
T3-1268.x: According to statistics, the number of people living alone keeps growing.
T3-1268.t: 통계에 따르면 ('according to statistics') is a very common opener in news and essays.

T3-1269.x: I deleted an important photo by mistake.
T3-1269.t: Pronounced [삭쩨하다]; in casual speech 지우다 is just as common.

T3-1270.ex: 친구가 보내 준 고양이 영상이 정말 웃겼어요.
T3-1270.x: The cat video my friend sent me was really funny.
T3-1270.t: Don't mix it up with 영상 'above zero' in weather reports, as in 영상 5도.

T3-1271.ex: 요즘은 온라인으로 수업을 듣는 학생이 많아요.
T3-1271.x: These days many students take classes online.
T3-1271.e: From English 'online'; pronounced [올라인] because ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T3-1272.x: We decided to meet in person for this gathering.
T3-1272.e: From English 'offline'; in Korean it often means 'in person' or 'in a physical store.'

T3-1273.ex: 환경 오염은 큰 사회적 문제가 되었습니다.
T3-1273.x: Environmental pollution has become a big social problem.
T3-1273.e: 사회 'society' + -적 '-al': -적 turns nouns into adjective-like words: 경제적, 국제적.
T3-1273.t: -적 words go directly before nouns (사회적 문제) or take 인/으로: 사회적인 활동, 사회적으로.

T3-1274.ex: 만 열여덟 살이 되면 선거에서 투표할 수 있어요.
T3-1274.x: Once you turn eighteen, you can vote in elections.

T3-1275.x: A new law was passed in the National Assembly.
T3-1275.t: Pronounced [범뉼]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅂ, then ㅂ becomes ㅁ.

T3-1276.ex: 회사 규정에 따라 사무실에서는 담배를 피울 수 없어요.
T3-1276.x: Under company rules, you can't smoke in the office.
T3-1276.e: Literally 'a rule that has been fixed.'

T3-1277.x: The government announced a new housing policy.

T3-1278.m: to violate, to break (a rule or law)
T3-1278.ex: 그 운전자는 신호를 위반해서 벌금을 냈어요.
T3-1278.x: That driver ran a red light and paid a fine.
T3-1278.e: Literally 'to go against and oppose' a rule.

T3-1279.ex: 음주 운전에 대한 처벌이 더 강해졌어요.
T3-1279.x: The punishment for drunk driving has become stricter.
T3-1279.t: For wrongdoers, 처벌을 받다 means 'to be punished.'

T3-1280.ex: 법을 어긴 사람은 법에 따라 처벌해야 해요.
T3-1280.x: People who break the law should be punished according to the law.

T3-1281.x: The police caught the culprit in three days.
T3-1281.e: Literally 'a person who committed a crime.'

T3-1282.x: I got pickpocketed on the subway and lost my wallet.
T3-1282.e: Built from 소매 'sleeve' + 치기, a noun from 치다 'to strike.'
T3-1282.t: Use 소매치기를 당하다 for 'to get pickpocketed.'

T3-1283.ex: 요즘 전화로 하는 사기가 많으니까 조심하세요.
T3-1283.x: There are a lot of phone scams these days, so be careful.
T3-1283.e: Literally 'deceiving and cheating.' Homonym warning: 사기 also means 'morale.'
T3-1283.t: 사기를 당하다 means 'to get scammed'; 사기를 치다 means 'to scam someone.'

T3-1284.forms: 피해를 입어요 · 피해를 입었어요 · 피해를 입을 거예요
T3-1284.m: to suffer damage, to be harmed
T3-1284.ex: 태풍 때문에 많은 농가가 피해를 입었습니다.
T3-1284.x: Many farms suffered damage because of the typhoon.
T3-1284.e: 입다 'to wear' also means 'to receive' harm or help; compare 은혜를 입다.
T3-1284.t: The opposite direction is 피해를 주다, 'to cause harm to someone.'

T3-1285.ex: 그 사건의 재판은 다음 달에 열립니다.
T3-1285.x: The trial for that case will be held next month.

T3-1286.x: You need permission to take pictures here.
T3-1286.t: 허가 is official permission from an authority; for permission from parents or friends, use 허락.

T3-1287.ex: 어릴 때부터 기본적인 도덕을 배워야 해요.
T3-1287.x: You should learn basic morals from a young age.

T3-1288.m: to yield, to give up (for someone), to concede
T3-1288.x: I gave up my seat to an elderly woman on the subway.
T3-1288.e: Literally 'to yield a step' to someone else.
T3-1288.t: 자리를 양보하다, 'to give up your seat,' is the classic collocation.

T3-1289.x: All people are equal before the law.

T3-1290.ex: 나이나 성별로 사람을 차별하면 안 돼요.
T3-1290.x: You shouldn't discriminate against people because of age or gender.
T3-1290.e: Literally 'to treat as different and separate.'
T3-1290.t: 차별 is negative unfair treatment; for neutral 'telling apart,' use 구별하다.

T3-1291.x: Everyone's human rights must be respected.
T3-1291.t: Pronounced [인꿘], with a tense ㄲ sound.

T3-1292.ex: 많은 사람들이 남북 통일을 바라고 있어요.
T3-1292.x: Many people hope for the reunification of North and South Korea.

T3-1294.ex: 한국은 고령화가 아주 빠르게 진행되고 있습니다.
T3-1294.x: Korea's population is aging very rapidly.
T3-1294.e: Literally 'becoming high in age.' -화 = '-ization': 현대화, 세계화.
T3-1294.t: Often paired in news as 저출산 고령화, 'low birth rate and aging population.'

T3-1295.ex: 중년이 되니까 건강에 더 신경을 쓰게 돼요.
T3-1295.x: Now that I'm middle-aged, I pay more attention to my health.
T3-1295.t: 중년 남성 and 중년 여성, 'middle-aged man/woman,' are common phrases in news and ads.

T3-1296.ex: 한국에서는 만 열아홉 살부터 성인으로 봅니다.
T3-1296.x: In Korea, people are considered adults from age nineteen.
T3-1296.e: Literally 'a completed person.' Homonym warning: another 성인 means 'saint.'
T3-1296.t: 어른 is the everyday word; 성인 is used for legal age, ticket prices and official contexts.

T3-1297.ex: 노후를 위해서 매달 조금씩 저축하고 있어요.
T3-1297.x: I'm saving a little every month for my retirement.
T3-1297.t: 노후 준비, 'preparing for retirement,' is a very common phrase.

T3-1298.x: The government announced that it will expand welfare for the elderly.

T3-1299.ex: 학생은 할인 혜택을 받을 수 있어요.
T3-1299.t: Common pattern: 혜택을 받다 'to receive a benefit'; 혜택을 주다 'to give a benefit.'

T3-1300.ex: 그 가수는 매년 어려운 이웃에게 돈을 기부해요.
T3-1300.x: That singer donates money to neighbors in need every year.

T3-1301.ex: 우리는 이 문제의 해결책을 찾아야 해요.
T3-1301.x: We need to find a solution to this problem.

T3-1302.m: countermeasure, measure, plan to deal with something
T3-1302.ex: 정부는 미세먼지 대책을 빨리 세워야 합니다.
T3-1302.x: The government needs to come up with measures against fine dust quickly.
T3-1302.e: Literally 'a plan for facing' a problem.
T3-1302.t: The usual verb is 세우다: 대책을 세우다, 'to come up with measures.'

T3-1303.ex: 스마트폰 때문에 사람들의 생활이 많이 변화했어요.
T3-1303.x: People's lives have changed a lot because of smartphones.
T3-1303.t: More formal than 바뀌다 or 변하다; common in news and essays about society or trends.

T3-1304.ex: 인터넷이 발달해서 정보를 쉽게 찾을 수 있어요.
T3-1304.x: Because the internet has developed, we can find information easily.
T3-1304.e: Literally 'to set out and reach' a higher level.
T3-1304.t: 발달 is common for technology, the body or skills; 발전 is preferred for countries and economies.

T3-1305.x: Traffic accidents have decreased significantly compared with last year.

T3-1306.x: Using public transportation is more economical.
T3-1306.t: Can mean both 'economic' (경제적 문제) and 'money-saving' (경제적인 차).

T3-1308.ex: 에너지 절약을 위해서 안 쓰는 불은 꺼 주세요.
T3-1308.x: To save energy, please turn off lights you aren't using.
T3-1308.t: Pronounced [저략]: the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

T3-1309.ex: 게임을 하면서 시간을 너무 많이 낭비했어요.
T3-1309.x: I wasted too much time playing games.
T3-1309.t: 시간 낭비 ('a waste of time') and 돈 낭비 ('a waste of money') are everyday phrases.

T3-1310.ex: 그 할아버지는 모든 재산을 학교에 기부했어요.
T3-1310.x: That old man donated his entire fortune to a school.

T3-1311.x: I bought a laptop on a twelve-month installment plan.
T3-1311.t: At Korean checkouts you'll hear 일시불로 하시겠어요, 할부로 하시겠어요? — 'one payment or installments?'

T3-1312.m: to refund, to give a refund
T3-1312.ex: 영수증이 있으면 일주일 안에 환불해 드려요.
T3-1312.x: If you have the receipt, we'll give you a refund within a week.
T3-1312.t: As a customer, say 환불받고 싶어요 'I'd like a refund'; the store 환불해 드려요.

T3-1313.x: The size didn't fit, so I requested a return.

T3-1314.x: The earphones I just bought were defective, so I exchanged them.
T3-1314.e: Literally 'not-good goods.' -품 = item, goods: 신제품, 반품.

T3-1315.ex: 그 회사는 다음 달에 신제품을 출시할 예정이에요.
T3-1315.x: That company plans to release a new product next month.

T3-1316.ex: 이 제품은 온라인에서만 판매를 하고 있어요.
T3-1316.x: This product is sold only online.

T3-1317.e: Both syllables mean 'buy'; 매 'buy' and 매 'sell' differ only in hanja.

T3-1318.x: Please buy your tickets in advance on the website.
T3-1318.t: More formal than 사다; common in ads, websites and shopping notices.

T3-1319.x: You can purchase tickets at the ticket office.

T3-1320.ex: 자동차 매연 때문에 공기가 많이 나빠졌어요.
T3-1320.x: The air has gotten much worse because of car exhaust.

T3-1321.ex: 한국의 여름은 습도가 높아서 더 덥게 느껴져요.
T3-1321.x: Korean summers feel hotter because the humidity is high.
T3-1321.t: Pronounced [습또]; use 높다/낮다 with it: 습도가 높아요.

T3-1322.ex: 환경 오염은 바다 생태계를 위협하고 있습니다.
T3-1322.x: Environmental pollution is threatening the ocean ecosystem.

T3-1323.m: shopping basket, reusable shopping bag; online shopping cart
T3-1323.x: I carry a reusable shopping bag instead of plastic bags.
T3-1323.e: 장 'market' (as in 장을 보다 'go grocery shopping') + native 바구니 'basket.'
T3-1323.t: On shopping websites, 장바구니 is the 'cart' button.

T3-1324.ex: 문화재 보존을 위해서 사진 촬영이 금지되어 있습니다.
T3-1324.x: Photography is prohibited to preserve cultural heritage.
T3-1324.e: Literally 'protecting so it continues to exist.'
T3-1324.t: For files on a computer, use 저장, not 보존.

T3-1325.ex: 무분별한 개발은 자연 파괴로 이어질 수 있습니다.
T3-1325.x: Reckless development can lead to the destruction of nature.

T3-1326.ex: 지진이나 홍수 같은 자연재해는 미리 막기 어려워요.
T3-1326.x: Natural disasters like earthquakes and floods are hard to prevent in advance.

T3-1327.x: When a disaster happens, you should evacuate calmly.

T3-1328.x: Wildfires often break out in the dry spring.
T3-1328.e: Literally 'mountain fire'; 불 is the native Korean word for fire.
T3-1328.t: Fires 'come out' in Korean: 산불이 나다 = a wildfire breaks out.

T3-1329.ex: 경보가 울리자 사람들이 건물 밖으로 대피했어요.
T3-1329.x: When the alarm went off, people evacuated the building.
T3-1329.e: Literally 'wait and avoid': step aside until the danger passes.

T3-1330.x: I swam at the beach with my friends in the summer.
T3-1330.t: 바닷가 is the everyday native word; 해변 sounds a bit more formal or descriptive.

T3-1331.m: fruit (of a plant), berry; result, fruits (of effort)
T3-1331.ex: 가을이 되면 나무에 열매가 많이 열려요.
T3-1331.x: In the fall, lots of fruit grows on the trees.
T3-1331.e: Related to 열리다 'to bear fruit': 열매가 열리다 is the natural pairing.
T3-1331.t: 열매 is fruit on any plant; 과일 is fruit you buy and eat. 노력의 열매 = the fruits of effort.

T3-1332.x: This tree has very deep roots.
T3-1332.e: Used figuratively too, just like English: one's roots, or the root of a problem.

T3-1333.ex: 여름에는 숲에서 다양한 곤충을 볼 수 있어요.
T3-1333.x: In summer you can see all kinds of insects in the forest.
T3-1333.e: The scientific word for insect; everyday 'bug' is 벌레.

T3-1334.forms: 야생이 · 야생을 (often before a noun: 야생 동물)
T3-1334.ex: 이 공원에서는 야생 동물을 가까이에서 볼 수 있어요.
T3-1334.x: In this park, you can see wild animals up close.
T3-1334.e: Literally 'living in the fields': growing up in nature.

T3-1335.ex: 기후 변화 때문에 많은 동물이 멸종 위기에 놓였어요.
T3-1335.x: Because of climate change, many animals are in danger of extinction.
T3-1335.t: Pronounced [멸쫑]: in Sino-Korean words, ㅈ after ㄹ becomes tense.

T3-1336.x: My grandfather farms in the countryside.
T3-1336.t: Use 짓다 with it: 농사를 짓다 = to farm (ㅅ irregular: 지어요).

T3-1337.ex: 제 동생은 집 근처 유치원에 다녀요.
T3-1337.x: My little brother goes to a kindergarten near our house.
T3-1337.e: Literally 'garden of little ones', a translation of German 'Kindergarten'.

T3-1338.m: culture, refinement; general education, liberal arts
T3-1338.ex: 대학교 1학년 때 교양 수업을 많이 들었어요.
T3-1338.x: I took a lot of general-ed classes in my first year of college.
T3-1338.e: Literally 'teaching and nurturing': cultivating the mind.
T3-1338.t: 교양 있다 = cultured, well-mannered; in college, 교양 means general-ed courses outside your major.

T3-1339.m: to lecture, to give a lecture, to teach (a course)
T3-1339.ex: 김 교수님은 대학에서 한국 역사를 강의하세요.
T3-1339.x: Professor Kim teaches Korean history at a university.
T3-1339.t: Often pronounced [강이]: 의 in a non-first syllable can sound like 이.

T3-1340.m: parent(s) of a student, school parents
T3-1340.x: There's a parents' meeting at school tomorrow.

T3-1341.ex: 한국 고등학생들은 입시 준비로 아주 바빠요.
T3-1341.x: Korean high school students are very busy preparing for entrance exams.
T3-1341.t: Pronounced [입씨]: ㅅ becomes tense after ㅂ.

T3-1342.ex: 이 앱은 단어 학습에 아주 도움이 돼요.
T3-1342.x: This app really helps with learning vocabulary.
T3-1342.t: Pronounced [학씁]; 학습 is formal or academic, while 공부 is the everyday word.

T3-1343.ex: 저는 요즘 졸업 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
T3-1343.x: These days I'm writing my graduation thesis.

T3-1344.ex: 우리는 과학 시간에 물과 소금으로 실험했어요.
T3-1344.x: We did an experiment with water and salt in science class.
T3-1344.e: Literally 'test for real': checking an idea in practice.

T3-1345.m: to take a leave of absence from school
T3-1345.x: My older brother took a year off school to do his military service.
T3-1345.t: Pronounced [휴하카다]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-1346.x: My older sister studied in the U.S. for three years.
T3-1346.e: Literally 'stay and study': living in another country to study.
T3-1346.t: Don't mix up 유학 (studying abroad) and 휴학 (leave of absence); they differ by one sound.

T3-1347.x: In college, I went to Australia for a language study program.
T3-1347.t: Pronounced [어항년수]: an ㄴ sound is added, and ㄱ turns into ㅇ before it.

T3-1348.ex: 저는 다음 학기에 일본에 교환 학생으로 가요.
T3-1348.x: Next semester I'm going to Japan as an exchange student.

T3-1349.x: He got his doctorate in the U.S.
T3-1349.t: Use 받다 or 따다: 학위를 받다 / 학위를 따다 = to earn a degree.

T3-1350.x: The elementary school entrance ceremony is in early March.
T3-1350.t: Pronounced [이팍씩]; Korean school years start in March, so entrance ceremonies are held then.

T3-1351.ex: 수업 전에 예습을 하면 이해가 더 잘 돼요.
T3-1351.x: If you prepare before class, you understand better.
T3-1351.e: Literally 'practice beforehand'; its opposite is 복습 'review'.

T3-1352.m: to learn, to master, to get used to; to cook (thoroughly)
T3-1352.ex: 외국어를 잘하려면 기본 문법을 먼저 익혀야 해요.
T3-1352.x: To be good at a foreign language, you have to master basic grammar first.
T3-1352.e: Causative of 익다 'to ripen, to become familiar': making something 'ripe' in your head or pan.
T3-1352.t: Also 'to cook through': 고기를 잘 익혀 주세요 = Please cook the meat well.

T3-1353.ex: 이 이야기는 우리에게 중요한 교훈을 줘요.
T3-1353.x: This story teaches us an important lesson.
T3-1353.t: 교훈을 얻다 = to learn a lesson (from an experience).

T3-1354.ex: 선생님의 가르침을 평생 잊지 않을 거예요.
T3-1354.x: I'll never forget my teacher's teachings.
T3-1354.e: Noun form of 가르치다 'to teach' plus -ㅁ.
T3-1354.t: Sounds respectful and weighty; use it for a mentor's, parent's or religious teacher's teachings.

T3-1355.m: to guide, to coach, to supervise, to instruct
T3-1355.x: Mr. Park coaches our soccer team.
T3-1355.t: Don't confuse with 지도 'map': same sound, different word.

T3-1356.m: to take notes, to jot down
T3-1356.x: Jot down the important points in your notebook.

T3-1357.m: to grow apart, to drift apart; to become distant, to get farther away
T3-1357.ex: 졸업 후에 그 친구와 점점 멀어졌어요.
T3-1357.x: After graduation, that friend and I gradually drifted apart.

T3-1358.m: to date, to be in a romantic relationship
T3-1358.x: The two of them dated for three years and then got married.
T3-1358.t: 사귀다 names a partner (민수랑 사귀어요); 연애하다 describes being in a relationship in general.

T3-1359.ex: 공원에서 연인들이 손을 잡고 걷고 있어요.
T3-1359.x: Couples are walking hand in hand in the park.
T3-1359.t: 연인 sounds a bit literary; in conversation people usually say 애인 or 남자 친구 / 여자 친구.

T3-1360.ex: 두 사람은 정말 잘 어울리는 커플이에요.
T3-1360.x: They really are a perfect couple.
T3-1360.e: From English 'couple'; Konglish spin-offs include 커플룩 'matching outfits' and 커플링 'couple rings'.

T3-1361.x: They say you remember your first love for a long time.
T3-1361.e: 첫 'first' + 사랑 'love'; 첫 also appears in 첫날 'first day' and 첫눈 'first snow'.
T3-1361.t: Pronounced [첟싸랑]: the ㅅ becomes tense after 첫.

T3-1362.m: to confess (one's feelings), to tell someone you like them; to confess (a secret or wrongdoing)
T3-1362.x: Yesterday I told the person I like how I feel.
T3-1362.t: In Korean dating, 고백 is the moment you ask someone to be your partner, which usually starts the relationship.

T3-1363.m: to part, to say farewell; to break up
T3-1363.x: That couple broke up after five years.
T3-1363.t: 이별하다 sounds emotional or literary, like in songs; in conversation 헤어지다 is more common.

T3-1364.x: That actor got divorced after two years of marriage.
T3-1364.e: Literally 'leave the marriage'; the opposite of 결혼.

T3-1365.ex: 이 서류에 배우자 이름도 써 주세요.
T3-1365.x: Please also write your spouse's name on this form.
T3-1365.e: Literally 'the person paired with you'; a formal word for husband or wife.
T3-1365.t: Watch out: 배우자! can also mean 'Let's learn!' (배우다 + -자).

T3-1366.ex: 우리는 신혼 때 작은 아파트에 살았어요.
T3-1366.x: When we were newlyweds, we lived in a small apartment.

T3-1367.x: My maternal uncle is my mother's younger brother.
T3-1367.e: 외 marks the mother's side; 삼촌 means 'three degrees' of kinship.

T3-1368.ex: 그 집 며느리는 시부모님께 아주 잘해요.
T3-1368.x: That family's daughter-in-law is very good to her in-laws.
T3-1368.e: Pairs with 사위 'son-in-law'; a 며느리 calls her husband's parents 시부모님.

T3-1369.ex: 장인어른이 사위를 아주 마음에 들어 하세요.
T3-1369.x: The father-in-law really likes his son-in-law.
T3-1369.e: Pairs with 며느리 'daughter-in-law'; a 사위 calls his wife's parents 장인 and 장모.

T3-1370.m: to take care of, to look after
T3-1370.x: My older sister lovingly takes care of our sick mother.
T3-1370.e: Probably 보다 'to look' + 살피다 'to watch closely': keeping a careful eye on someone.

T3-1371.m: to be a good son or daughter, to honor and care for one's parents
T3-1371.x: Being good to your parents is very important.
T3-1371.e: Literally 'the way of filial devotion', a core Confucian value in Korea.

T3-1372.x: A small quarrel turned into a big fight.
T3-1372.e: Noun form of 다투다 'to argue' plus -ㅁ.

T3-1373.x: I had an argument with my younger sibling yesterday.
T3-1373.e: 말 'words' + 다툼 'quarrel': a fight with words only.

T3-1374.ex: 우리는 싸운 다음 날 바로 화해를 했어요.
T3-1374.x: We made up the very next day after our fight.
T3-1374.e: Literally 'harmonize and untie' the knot between people.

T3-1375.ex: 진심으로 사과하면 용서를 받을 수 있을 거예요.
T3-1375.x: If you sincerely apologize, you'll probably be forgiven.
T3-1375.t: 용서를 빌다 = to beg for forgiveness; 용서해 주세요 = Please forgive me.

T3-1376.m: to trust, to have faith in
T3-1376.x: Our team members deeply trust one another.
T3-1376.t: Pronounced [실뢰하다]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T3-1377.ex: 친한 친구의 배신 때문에 많이 힘들었어요.
T3-1377.x: I had a really hard time because of a close friend's betrayal.

T3-1378.x: He never betrayed his friend, right to the end.
T3-1378.t: Takes a direct object: 친구를 배신하다 = to betray a friend.

T3-1379.m: to advise, to give (frank) advice, to warn
T3-1379.x: An older student advised me to cut back on drinking.
T3-1379.e: Literally 'loyal telling': honest advice from someone who cares.
T3-1379.t: 충고 often points out a fault; 조언 is more neutral advice or suggestions.

T3-1380.x: My professor gave me advice about my career path.

T3-1381.m: to consult, to get counseling, to counsel
T3-1381.x: I talked with my homeroom teacher about my career plans.

T3-1382.x: I asked my friend a favor, but I got turned down.
T3-1382.t: 거절을 당하다 = to be rejected or turned down.

T3-1383.x: Mom scolded my little brother for coming home late.
T3-1383.e: 야단 'fuss, uproar' + 치다; 야단났다 means 'We're in big trouble!'
T3-1383.t: The receiving side is 야단맞다: 선생님께 야단맞았어요 = I got scolded by the teacher.

T3-1384.m: to scold, to tell off, to punish
T3-1384.ex: 선생님이 숙제를 안 한 학생을 혼내셨어요.
T3-1384.x: The teacher scolded the student who didn't do the homework.
T3-1384.e: Probably 혼 'soul' + 내다 'to take out': scaring someone out of their wits.
T3-1384.t: 혼내다 = to scold someone; 혼나다 = to get scolded.

T3-1385.ex: 친구의 따뜻한 말이 큰 위로가 됐어요.
T3-1385.x: My friend's warm words were a great comfort.
T3-1385.t: Homonym: 위로 also means 'upward' (위 + 로), as in 위로 올라가세요.

T3-1386.ex: 선생님의 격려 덕분에 끝까지 할 수 있었어요.
T3-1386.x: Thanks to my teacher's encouragement, I was able to see it through.
T3-1386.t: Pronounced [경녀]: nasalization changes both ㄱ and ㄹ.

T3-1387.ex: 여러분의 응원 덕분에 경기에서 이길 수 있었어요.
T3-1387.x: Thanks to your support, we were able to win the game.
T3-1387.t: 응원할게요! = I'm rooting for you! — a common friendly encouragement.

T3-1388.ex: 두 나라는 문화 교류를 활발하게 하고 있어요.
T3-1388.x: The two countries are actively engaged in cultural exchange.

T3-1389.m: to talk, to have a conversation
T3-1389.x: I talk with my family every evening.

T3-1390.ex: 외국인 친구와 의사소통이 잘 돼서 좋아요.
T3-1390.x: I'm happy that I can communicate well with my foreign friend.
T3-1390.t: Here 의사 means 'intention', not 의사 'doctor'; they're different words that sound the same.

T3-1391.m: temper, disposition; nature, property (of a thing)
T3-1391.ex: 그 사람은 성질이 급해서 자주 화를 내요.
T3-1391.x: He's quick-tempered, so he often gets angry.
T3-1391.t: About people, 성질 usually means temper: 성질이 나쁘다 = bad-tempered, 성질을 내다 = to blow up.

T3-1392.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들은 개성을 중요하게 생각해요.
T3-1392.x: Young people these days value individuality.

T3-1393.ex: 제 남편은 성격이 느긋해서 화를 잘 안 내요.
T3-1393.x: My husband is easygoing, so he rarely gets angry.
T3-1393.e: Think of it as the opposite of 급하다 'impatient, in a hurry'.
T3-1393.t: Pronounced [느그타다]: the ㅅ sounds like ㄷ and merges with ㅎ into ㅌ.

T3-1394.x: Our daughter is cheerful, so she has lots of friends.
T3-1394.t: Pronounced [명낭하다]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T3-1395.ex: 그 아이는 식당에서 아주 얌전하게 앉아 있었어요.
T3-1395.x: That child sat very nicely in the restaurant.
T3-1395.t: Common praise for calm, well-behaved children or pets: 얌전한 강아지 = a well-behaved puppy.

T3-1396.x: He greeted me with a shy smile.
T3-1396.e: Noun 수줍음 'shyness' appears in 수줍음을 타다 'to be shy by nature'.
T3-1396.t: Regular despite the ㅂ: say 수줍어요, not 수주워요.

T3-1397.x: He acts arrogant because he has a lot of money.

T3-1398.ex: 자기 생각만 하는 것은 너무 이기적이에요.
T3-1398.x: Thinking only about yourself is too selfish.
T3-1398.t: Used like an adjective: 이기적이다, or 이기적인 + noun (이기적인 사람 = a selfish person).

T3-1399.m: slow, dull; clumsy; insensitive, slow to notice
T3-1399.ex: 저는 운동 신경이 둔해서 춤을 잘 못 춰요.
T3-1399.x: I'm not very coordinated, so I can't dance well.

T3-1400.x: Grandma is big-hearted, so she's kind to everyone.
T3-1400.t: A polite request for leniency: 너그럽게 봐 주세요 = Please go easy on me.

T3-1401.x: He coldly turned down my request.
T3-1401.t: A homonym 냉정 means 'calm, level-headed': 냉정하게 생각하다 = to think coolly and objectively.

T3-1402.ex: 우리 아버지는 어릴 때 아주 엄하셨어요.
T3-1402.x: My father was very strict when I was young.

T3-1403.ex: 우리 집 강아지는 성격이 아주 순해요.
T3-1403.x: Our dog has a very gentle personality.
T3-1403.t: Also for mild flavors or products: 순한 맛 = mild flavor, 순한 화장품 = gentle cosmetics.

T3-1404.ex: 그는 너무 순진해서 다른 사람의 말을 다 믿어요.
T3-1404.x: He's so naive that he believes everything people tell him.
T3-1404.t: Can be positive (innocent) or negative (gullible), depending on context.

T3-1405.ex: 그런 어리석은 실수를 다시는 하지 않을 거예요.
T3-1405.x: I'll never make such a foolish mistake again.
T3-1405.e: Middle Korean 어리다 meant 'foolish' before it shifted to mean 'young'.

T3-1406.ex: 우리 아이는 병원에서도 울지 않고 씩씩했어요.
T3-1406.x: My child didn't even cry at the hospital and was really brave.
T3-1406.t: Adults often praise kids with 씩씩하게 잘했어! 'You did great, so brave!'

T3-1407.ex: 저는 소심해서 처음 보는 사람에게 말을 잘 못 걸어요.
T3-1407.x: I'm timid, so I have a hard time talking to people I've just met.
T3-1407.e: Literally 'small heart': a heart too small to be bold.
T3-1407.t: In Chinese the same word means 'be careful', but in Korean it's a mild criticism.

T3-1408.ex: 그 친구는 재치가 있어서 대화가 늘 재미있어요.
T3-1408.x: That friend is witty, so talking with them is always fun.
T3-1408.e: Literally 'talent that hits the mark' at just the right moment.
T3-1408.t: Usually used as 재치(가) 있다 'to be witty' or 재치 있는 대답 'a witty reply'.

T3-1409.ex: 제 동생은 나이에 비해 아주 성숙해요.
T3-1409.x: My younger sibling is very mature for their age.
T3-1409.e: Literally 'become ripe', like fruit ready to pick.

T3-1410.m: to pound, to throb, to flutter (of the heart)
T3-1410.x: My heart was pounding so hard before the presentation.
T3-1410.e: From 두근두근, the sound of a racing heart, plus -거리다 'keep doing'.
T3-1410.t: The subject is usually 가슴 or 심장: 가슴이 두근거려요 'My heart is racing.'

T3-1411.m: to be moved, to be touched
T3-1411.x: I was really moved after watching that movie.
T3-1411.e: Literally 'feel and move': your feelings are stirred.
T3-1411.t: 감동하다 and 감동(을) 받다 both mean 'be moved'; for 'moving' use 감동적이다.

T3-1412.ex: 택시 기사님이 길을 몰라서 정말 황당했어요.
T3-1412.x: The taxi driver didn't know the way, so I was totally dumbfounded.
T3-1412.e: Originally described wild, groundless talk; now used for 'What on earth?!' moments.
T3-1412.t: Don't mix it up with 당황하다: 황당하다 means the situation is absurd, 당황하다 means you're flustered.

T3-1413.ex: 친구가 제 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 섭섭했어요.
T3-1413.x: My friend forgot my birthday, so I felt a little hurt.
T3-1413.e: Used for hurt feelings in close relationships, very close to 서운하다.

T3-1414.x: My grandmother always misses her hometown.
T3-1414.e: From 그립다 'missed' plus -어하다, which turns a feeling into an action verb.
T3-1414.t: Use 그리워하다 for other people's feelings with an object (N을); for your own, say 고향이 그리워요.

T3-1415.ex: 사람들은 그 뉴스를 보고 큰 분노를 느꼈습니다.
T3-1415.x: People felt great anger after seeing that news.
T3-1415.e: Two 'anger' syllables stacked together: serious, intense rage.

T3-1416.m: to feel nervous, to be tense
T3-1416.x: I have a job interview tomorrow, so I'm really nervous.
T3-1416.e: Literally 'tightly stretched', like a drawn bowstring.
T3-1416.t: 긴장돼요 is 'I feel nervous'; to calm someone, say 긴장하지 마세요.

T3-1417.ex: 저는 겁이 많아서 밤에 혼자 못 나가요.
T3-1417.x: I scare easily, so I can't go out alone at night.
T3-1417.t: Key phrases: 겁이 많다 'scare easily', 겁이 나다 'get scared', 겁을 주다 'scare someone'.

T3-1418.m: to envy, to be envious of
T3-1418.x: My friends were envious of my new phone.
T3-1418.e: From 부럽다 'envious' plus -어하다, used to describe someone else's feeling.

T3-1419.ex: 동생은 엄마가 언니만 예뻐해서 언니를 질투해요.
T3-1419.x: My little sister is jealous because Mom only dotes on our older sister.
T3-1419.t: 질투 sounds negative and resentful, while 부럽다 is light envy or admiration.

T3-1420.ex: 저는 그 사람을 이제 미워하지 않아요.
T3-1420.x: I don't hate that person anymore.
T3-1420.e: From 밉다 'hateful' plus -어하다, turning the feeling into a verb.

T3-1421.x: My friend really appreciated my help.
T3-1421.e: From 고맙다 'thankful' plus -어하다, describing someone else's gratitude.

T3-1422.x: The kids had a great time at the amusement park all day.
T3-1422.e: From 즐겁다 'joyful' plus -어하다, showing someone else's enjoyment.

T3-1423.x: That accident was a great misfortune for the family.
T3-1423.t: In fast speech the ㅎ weakens after ㄹ, so it often sounds like [부랭].

T3-1424.x: He failed the exam and fell into despair.

T3-1425.x: The movie I had been looking forward to was much more disappointing than I expected.
T3-1425.e: Literally 'lose hope' plus -스럽다 'seeming, giving that feeling'.
T3-1425.t: 실망스럽다 describes the thing; for the person, use 실망하다: 저는 실망했어요.

T3-1426.x: Even if studying gets hard, don't give up halfway.
T3-1426.t: A different native word 포기 counts heads of cabbage: 배추 한 포기.

T3-1427.ex: 그는 새 차를 친구들에게 계속 자랑했어요.
T3-1427.x: He kept showing off his new car to his friends.
T3-1427.t: 자랑스럽다 is positive pride, but 자랑하다 often means showing off.

T3-1428.x: I feel refreshed after taking a walk in the morning.

T3-1429.m: to look forward to, to be anticipated
T3-1429.ex: 다음 주 제주도 여행이 정말 기대돼요.
T3-1429.x: I'm really looking forward to next week's trip to Jeju Island.
T3-1429.t: 기대돼요! is the natural way to say 'I can't wait!'

T3-1430.x: That claim has no scientific basis.

T3-1431.ex: 우리 팀은 올해 목표를 모두 달성했습니다.
T3-1431.x: Our team achieved all of its goals this year.
T3-1431.t: Pronounced [달썽하다]; the classic collocation is 목표를 달성하다 'reach a goal'.

T3-1432.m: realization, fulfillment (of a dream or plan)
T3-1432.ex: 그는 오랜 노력 끝에 꿈을 실현했어요.
T3-1432.x: After years of effort, he made his dream come true.

T3-1433.ex: 계획을 세우는 것보다 실천하는 것이 더 중요해요.
T3-1433.x: Putting a plan into action is more important than making it.
T3-1433.t: Common pair: 이론과 실천 'theory and practice'.

T3-1434.ex: 생각만 하지 말고 이제 직접 행동하세요.
T3-1434.x: Don't just think about it; take action yourself now.

T3-1435.ex: 그는 강한 의지로 병을 이겨 냈어요.
T3-1435.x: He beat the illness through sheer willpower.
T3-1435.t: A homonym 의지 means 'reliance', as in 의지하다 'to lean on someone'.

T3-1436.ex: 저는 올해 꼭 담배를 끊기로 결심했어요.
T3-1436.x: I've made up my mind to quit smoking for sure this year.
T3-1436.t: 결심하다 usually takes -기로: 운동하기로 결심했어요 'I decided to exercise.'

T3-1437.x: That situation called for a quick judgment.
T3-1437.e: Literally 'judge and cut': making a clean call.

T3-1438.ex: 사기 전에 두 제품의 가격을 비교해 보세요.
T3-1438.x: Compare the prices of the two products before you buy.

T3-1439.ex: 전문가들의 분석에 따르면 물가가 더 오를 겁니다.
T3-1439.x: According to experts' analysis, prices will rise further.

T3-1440.ex: 이 그래프를 분석하면 변화를 쉽게 알 수 있어요.
T3-1440.x: If you analyze this graph, you can easily see the changes.
T3-1440.e: Literally 'divide and split apart', plus 하다 'to do'.
T3-1440.t: Pronounced [분서카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-1441.ex: 그 식당은 손님들에게 좋은 평가를 받았어요.
T3-1441.x: That restaurant got good reviews from customers.

T3-1442.ex: 환경 문제에 대한 사람들의 인식이 바뀌고 있어요.
T3-1442.x: People's awareness of environmental issues is changing.
T3-1442.t: Very common in reading passages as N에 대한 인식 'perception of N'.

T3-1443.x: I completely agree with your opinion too.
T3-1443.t: Pattern: N에 동의하다 'agree with N'; 동의서 is a consent form.

T3-1444.x: Most of the students were in favor of that plan.
T3-1444.t: 찬성 is voting yes to a plan or proposal; 동의 is agreeing with an opinion.

T3-1445.ex: 친구가 주말에 같이 여행을 가자고 제안했어요.
T3-1445.x: My friend suggested that we take a trip together this weekend.

T3-1446.ex: 그 손님은 직원에게 계속 환불을 요구했어요.
T3-1446.x: That customer kept demanding a refund from the staff.
T3-1446.t: 요구 is a firm demand; 요청 is a polite request.

T3-1447.x: I requested a week of vacation from my company.

T3-1448.ex: 이 호텔은 손님들에게 무료 아침 식사를 제공합니다.
T3-1448.x: This hotel offers guests a free breakfast.

T3-1449.ex: 이 수영장은 나이 제한이 있어서 어린이는 못 들어가요.
T3-1449.x: This pool has an age limit, so children can't go in.
T3-1449.t: Common compounds: 시간 제한 'time limit', 나이 제한 'age limit', 속도 제한 'speed limit'.

T3-1450.x: Everyone has different values, so they think differently too.
T3-1450.e: -관 = outlook or view: 가치관, 인생관, 세계관.

T3-1451.ex: 우리 마을은 서로 돕는 따뜻한 공동체예요.
T3-1451.x: Our village is a warm community where people help each other.

T3-1452.ex: 우리 학교는 여학생의 비율이 더 높아요.
T3-1452.x: Our school has a higher proportion of female students.
T3-1452.t: The 'rate' syllable is 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (비율, 할인율) and 률 elsewhere (확률).

T3-1453.ex: 이번 축제는 작년보다 규모가 훨씬 커졌어요.
T3-1453.x: This year's festival got much bigger in scale than last year's.
T3-1453.e: Literally 'compass and mold': the frame that sets something's size.

T3-1454.ex: 이곳은 이 도시에서 최초로 생긴 호텔이에요.
T3-1454.x: This is the first hotel ever built in this city.
T3-1454.t: 최초 is formal and often used as 최초의 N or 최초로; in daily talk, use 처음.

T3-1455.ex: 이 글의 핵심은 환경 보호의 중요성이에요.
T3-1455.x: The key point of this text is the importance of protecting the environment.

T3-1456.ex: 이론도 중요하지만 실제 경험이 더 필요해요.
T3-1456.x: Theory matters, but real experience is even more necessary.

T3-1457.x: He finally told people the truth.
T3-1457.t: 진실 is the truth versus lies; 사실 is a plain fact.

T3-1458.x: Contrary to experts' predictions, the economy improved.

T3-1459.ex: 저는 그의 표정을 보고 결과를 추측했어요.
T3-1459.x: I guessed the result from the look on his face.
T3-1459.e: Literally 'infer and measure': reasoning your way to a guess.
T3-1459.t: Pronounced [추츠카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T3-1460.m: to guess, to estimate, to imagine
T3-1460.ex: 그동안 얼마나 힘들었는지 짐작할 수 있어요.
T3-1460.x: I can imagine how hard it has been for you all this time.
T3-1460.e: Originally meant carefully pouring wine, gauging just the right amount.
T3-1460.t: 짐작 is an intuitive guess; 추측 sounds more reasoned and formal.

T3-1461.ex: 단어를 외우는 효과적인 방법을 알려 주세요.
T3-1461.x: Please tell me an effective way to memorize words.

T3-1462.x: It's important to use your time efficiently.
T3-1462.e: Literally 'effect-rate-ic': getting more result for the effort.
T3-1462.t: 효과적 means it works; 효율적 means it works without wasting time or money.

T3-1463.ex: 그 사고에서 모두 살아난 것은 기적이에요.
T3-1463.x: It's a miracle that everyone survived that accident.

T3-1464.x: You should respect other people's privacy.
T3-1464.t: Common phrase: 사생활 침해 'invasion of privacy', often in news about celebrities.

T3-1465.ex: 그는 우리 팀에 꼭 필요한 존재예요.
T3-1465.x: He's someone our team really can't do without.

T3-1466.ex: 대화할 때는 상대의 눈을 보고 말하세요.
T3-1466.x: When you talk with someone, look them in the eye.
T3-1466.e: Literally 'mutually facing': the one across from you.

T3-1467.ex: 말하기 대회에서 일등을 해서 상금을 받았어요.
T3-1467.x: I won first place in the speech contest and got prize money.

T3-1468.ex: 다음 달 서울에서 국제 영화제가 개최될 예정입니다.
T3-1468.x: An international film festival is scheduled to be held in Seoul next month.
T3-1468.t: News style: N이 개최되다 'N is held'; in speech, people say 열리다.

T3-1469.x: Today's meeting ran slower than expected.
T3-1469.t: 진행자 means a TV or event host, a very common use.

T3-1470.m: to proceed, to be in progress, to be held
T3-1470.ex: 오늘 행사는 비가 와도 예정대로 진행됩니다.
T3-1470.x: Today's event will go ahead as planned even if it rains.
T3-1470.e: Literally 'advance and go', plus 되다: the thing goes ahead.

T3-1471.ex: 유명한 작가가 학교 행사에 초청을 받았어요.
T3-1471.x: A famous author was invited to the school event.
T3-1471.t: 초청 is formal or official; for a friend's party, use 초대.

T3-1472.m: to become known, to be known
T3-1472.ex: 이 식당은 맛있는 냉면으로 알려져 있어요.
T3-1472.x: This restaurant is known for its delicious naengmyeon.
T3-1472.e: From 알리다 'to let know' plus passive -어지다: 'get made known'.
T3-1472.t: Pattern: N(으)로 알려져 있다 'to be known for N'.

T3-1473.x: I passed the teacher's message on to my classmates.

T3-1474.x: I'm going to my high school reunion this weekend.
T3-1474.e: Literally 'same-window meeting': people who studied by the same window.

T3-1475.ex: 내일 미술 시간 준비물은 가위와 풀이에요.
T3-1475.x: The supplies for tomorrow's art class are scissors and glue.
T3-1475.e: Literally 'prepared things': what you need to bring.
T3-1475.t: A classic school word: teachers announce tomorrow's 준비물 at the end of class.

T3-1476.ex: 자전거를 타고 인도로 다니면 안 돼요.
T3-1476.x: You shouldn't ride your bike on the sidewalk.
T3-1476.e: Literally 'people road', as opposed to 차도 'car road'.
T3-1476.t: Homonyms: 인도 also means India and 'guidance'; context makes it clear.

T3-1477.ex: 버스에 승차할 때 교통카드를 찍어 주세요.
T3-1477.x: Please tap your transit card when you get on the bus.

T3-1478.ex: 이번 정류장에서 하차하실 분은 벨을 눌러 주세요.
T3-1478.x: If you're getting off at this stop, please press the bell.
T3-1478.t: Also used when someone leaves a TV show: 프로그램에서 하차하다.

T3-1479.ex: 이 버스 노선은 시청 앞까지 가요.
T3-1479.x: This bus route goes to the front of City Hall.

T3-1480.x: It took 30 minutes to get my baggage at the airport.
T3-1480.e: Literally 'hand-load things': a formal airport word.
T3-1480.t: Airport signs say 수하물 찾는 곳 'baggage claim'; in everyday speech people say 짐.

T3-1481.x: They inspected my bag at customs when I entered the country.

T3-1482.ex: 날씨 때문에 비행기 출발이 두 시간 지연됐어요.
T3-1482.x: Because of the weather, the flight's departure was delayed two hours.
T3-1482.t: Used in airports and news; in everyday speech, people say 늦어지다.

T3-1483.ex: 폭설 때문에 비행기 출발이 두 시간 지연됐습니다.
T3-1483.x: Because of the heavy snow, the flight's departure was delayed by two hours.

T3-1484.m: in the end, finally; (with a negative) never, after all
T3-1484.ex: 그는 끝내 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
T3-1484.x: In the end, he didn't say a single word.
T3-1484.e: From 끝 'end' — 'right up to the end'.
T3-1484.t: Pronounced [끈내] — nasalization; often used with negatives for something that never happened despite waiting.

T3-1485.x: I went straight home right after class.

T3-1486.x: The weather is gradually getting colder.
T3-1486.e: Literally 'slowly, slowly' plus the adverb ending -히.
T3-1486.t: Usually pairs with change verbs like -아/어지다: 서서히 나아지다 'gradually get better.'

T3-1487.ex: 저는 때때로 혼자 영화를 보러 가요.
T3-1487.x: I sometimes go to the movies by myself.

T3-1488.forms: 한꺼번에 다 + verb: 한꺼번에 다 먹어요
T3-1488.m: all at once, at the same time
T3-1488.ex: 숙제를 한꺼번에 다 하려니까 너무 힘들어요.
T3-1488.x: Trying to do all my homework at once is really tough.
T3-1488.e: Starts with 한 'one' — everything in one go.

T3-1489.x: I was terribly tired yesterday, so I went to bed early.
T3-1489.t: Usually describes negative or intense states — cold, tired, worried — rather than pleasant ones.

T3-1490.forms: 제법 + adjective: 제법 잘해요, 제법 추워요
T3-1490.ex: 한국어를 배운 지 일 년인데 제법 잘하시네요.
T3-1490.x: You've only studied Korean for a year, but you're pretty good!
T3-1490.e: Carries a sense of 'better than you'd expect' — often light praise.
T3-1490.t: Used for pleasant surprise; saying it to a superior can sound condescending, like 'not bad for you.'

T3-1491.m: indeed, just as expected; (in questions) I wonder if really
T3-1491.ex: 과연 소문대로 이 식당 음식이 정말 맛있었어요.
T3-1491.x: Just as people said, this restaurant's food really was delicious.
T3-1491.e: Literally 'the result is so' — it turned out as predicted.
T3-1491.t: In questions it expresses doubt: 과연 그게 가능할까요? 'Is that really possible, I wonder?'

T3-1492.m: if, in case; an emergency, the unlikely event
T3-1492.ex: 만일 비가 오면 소풍은 다음 주로 미룰게요.
T3-1492.x: If it rains, we'll push the picnic back to next week.
T3-1492.e: Literally 'one in ten thousand' — a slim chance.
T3-1492.t: Interchangeable with 만약; 만일의 경우에 대비하다 means 'to prepare for the worst case.'

T3-1493.m: (not) at all, (not) possibly, no matter what
T3-1493.ex: 이 문제는 너무 어려워서 도저히 못 풀겠어요.
T3-1493.x: This problem is so hard I just can't solve it.
T3-1493.e: Literally 'reaching the bottom' — tried everything, still impossible.
T3-1493.t: Almost always paired with a negative like 못, 안, or 없다.

T3-1494.x: The wind blew and the door opened by itself.
T3-1494.e: Short form 절로 means the same; think 저 'oneself' — it happens on its own.

T3-1495.ex: 남의 물건을 함부로 만지면 안 돼요.
T3-1495.x: You shouldn't touch other people's things without asking.

T3-1496.x: I didn't have time, so I gave my room a quick, rough cleaning.

T3-1497.forms: 골고루 + verb: 골고루 먹어요, 골고루 나눠요
T3-1497.m: evenly, equally; a little of everything
T3-1497.ex: 건강을 위해서 음식을 골고루 먹어야 해요.
T3-1497.x: For your health, you should eat a balanced variety of food.
T3-1497.e: An emphatic, rhyming form of 고루 'evenly'.
T3-1497.t: 골고루 먹다 is the standard way to say 'eat a balanced diet' — parents say it to picky kids.

T3-1498.forms: 최소한 + amount: 최소한 한 시간 · 최소한의 (+noun)
T3-1498.ex: 하루에 최소한 물을 여덟 잔은 마셔야 해요.
T3-1498.x: You should drink at least eight glasses of water a day.

T3-1499.ex: 내일은 중요한 시험이 있어서 무조건 일찍 일어나야 해요.
T3-1499.x: I have an important exam tomorrow, so I absolutely have to get up early.
T3-1499.t: Pronounced [무조껀]; in casual speech it also means 'definitely': 무조건 맛있어 'it's guaranteed delicious.'

T3-1500.forms: A. 그런데도 B. (formal written: 그럼에도 불구하고)
T3-1500.m: even so, despite that, and yet
T3-1500.ex: 열이 많이 났어요. 그런데도 그는 회사에 갔어요.
T3-1500.x: He had a high fever. Even so, he went to work.
T3-1500.t: Stronger than 그래도: it stresses that the result goes against what you'd expect.

T3-1501.forms: A. 그러자 B. (B is a reaction that follows A)
T3-1501.ex: 제가 웃었어요. 그러자 아기도 따라 웃었어요.
T3-1501.x: I smiled. At that, the baby smiled too.
T3-1501.t: Only for past events in stories; for 'if you do that' use 그러면 instead.

T3-1502.x: He couldn't hide his disappointed look.

T3-1503.x: I have to get by on the money I have left until payday.

T3-1504.ex: 가격과 위치를 고려해서 이 집을 골랐어요.
T3-1504.x: I chose this house taking price and location into account.

T3-1505.x: They're twins, so it's hard to tell them apart.
T3-1505.t: 구별하다 is telling things apart by their differences; 구분하다 is sorting things into groups.

T3-1506.m: to approach, come closer, draw near
T3-1506.ex: 시험이 다가와서 요즘 도서관에 자주 가요.
T3-1506.x: Exams are coming up, so these days I often go to the library.
T3-1506.e: 다가- 'closer' + 오다 'to come'; its partner is 다가가다 'to go closer'.

T3-1507.m: to handle, deal with; to cover (a topic)
T3-1507.ex: 이 책은 환경 문제를 자세히 다루고 있어요.
T3-1507.x: This book covers environmental issues in detail.

T3-1508.ex: 키가 작아서 손이 선반에 안 닿아요.
T3-1508.x: I'm short, so my hand doesn't reach the shelf.
T3-1508.t: Pronounced [다타], and the ㅎ goes silent before vowels: 닿아요 [다아요].

T3-1509.m: to suffer, undergo (something bad), be subjected to
T3-1509.x: My friend was in a car accident and was hospitalized.
T3-1509.e: From a syllable meaning 'to face, meet head-on' — facing something unwelcome.
T3-1509.t: Attaches to nouns to make 'be done to': 무시당하다 'be ignored', 거절당하다 'be rejected'.

T3-1510.m: to add; to get worse, intensify
T3-1510.x: If the soup is bland, add a little salt.
T3-1510.t: In math, 더하기 is 'plus' and 빼기 is 'minus': 2 더하기 3은 5.

T3-1511.m: to look back, turn around; to reflect on
T3-1511.ex: 누가 제 이름을 불러서 뒤를 돌아봤어요.
T3-1511.x: Someone called my name, so I looked back.

T3-1512.forms: 떠올라요 · 떠올랐어요 · 떠오를 거예요 · 떠오른 (+noun) (르 irregular)
T3-1512.m: to rise, come up; to come to mind
T3-1512.x: A good idea came to me while I was showering.
T3-1512.t: 생각이 떠오르다 (an idea comes to you) vs. 생각을 떠올리다 (you call up a thought).

T3-1513.m: to run into, bump into; (eyes) to meet
T3-1513.x: I ran into a high school friend on the subway by chance.
T3-1513.t: 눈이 마주치다 means 'to make eye contact', often by accident.

T3-1514.m: to welcome, greet; to mark, celebrate (an occasion)
T3-1514.x: To ring in the new year, I went on a trip with my family.
T3-1514.e: From 맞다 'to receive, greet' — as in 맞은편 'the facing side'.

T3-1515.m: to affect, have (an effect); to reach
T3-1515.x: Smartphones have a big influence on children.
T3-1515.e: Homonym warning: another 미치다 means 'to go crazy'.
T3-1515.t: Learn it as the collocation 영향을 미치다 'to have an influence on'.

T3-1516.m: to happen, break out (an event); to open up, widen (a gap)
T3-1516.ex: 어젯밤 가게 앞에서 큰 싸움이 벌어졌어요.
T3-1516.x: A big fight broke out in front of the store last night.
T3-1516.e: Related to 벌리다 'to open wide' — picture a scene unfolding or a gap opening.

T3-1517.m: to shine on, light up; to reflect
T3-1517.ex: 아침 햇살이 창문으로 방 안을 비추고 있어요.
T3-1517.x: The morning sun is shining into the room through the window.
T3-1517.t: 비추다 takes an object (the sun lights up the room); 비치다 doesn't (light shines in).

T3-1518.m: to save (a life), revive; to make the most of
T3-1518.x: The doctor saved the patient who was in danger.
T3-1518.t: 살려 주세요! is how you shout 'Help!'; 장점을 살리다 means 'make the most of your strengths.'

T3-1519.m: to deceive, trick, cheat; to lie about
